en: The shrine among the centuries-old trees.
The house of the satirical poet.
Gentian and half Abruzzo at a glance.
Enter the daily life of the Cistercian monks.
The cult of the nuragic waters.

According to tradition, it was founded by the apostle Peter on his journey to Rome; the current neoclassical aspect dates back to reconstruction after the destruction of World War II. It preserves relics and a wooden statue of St. Arduino, the priest returning from Palestine who died of plague in Ceprano on July 28, 627, companion with St. Rocco, and the marble urn with the remains of Manfredi.
Large church of the upper part with neo-Gothic façade and rosette in Carrara marble; inside a wooden Crucifix of Margliano and a triptych of the Madonna with Saints Rocco and Sebastiano.
The baroque Alfierian in a hill country.
16th century church in the historic center frescoed by Pomarancio.
The historic brewery in the painted rooms and in the park.
Sanctuary excavated in the rock and dedicated to the god Silvano, dated to the second century BC, along the paths that go up to the castle of San Casto.
A Byzantine dome above the Roman baths.
The symbol of Sassari.
The Sicani tholos tombs.
The civic collection was founded in 1925 to document the Roman artistic environment, exhibited in the former convent of Via Crispi.

The last village of the valley, at 1,300 meters, founded by the Walser of Rimella that brought the cattle from 1338 (the name   ...Campello) appears in 1442); it grew from the middle of the nineteenth century to 1946 thanks to the nickel mines, long the active suns in Europe. There is still the dialect titsch; you can reach it by car from Omegna or on foot from Forno for the ancient Vegia Stro Vegia.

Under the parish basilica dedicated to Sant'Antioco Sulcitano, punish tombs united between the IV and VII century AD form the catacombs, with the room of the sarcophagus of the martyr, Christian paintings and inscriptions and the small catacomb of Santa Rosa.

Rebuilt after 1670 with slow works due to lack of funds, it has three naves on a Latin cross plan, is 44 meters high, 51 meters long and 22 wide; naves and dome have classic forms, while the white façade in stone of Priolo, of Romanesque imitation, was resumed in 1888 and completed in 1905. In the crypt the Museum of Sacred Art keeps the treasures of the community and documents of the country destroyed by the eruption of 1669.

Municipality of the valleys of Racines and Ridanna near Vipiteno: in Mareta stands Castel Wolfsthurn, baroque residence from 365 windows with the Provincial Museum of Hunting and Fishing, in Masseria the great enrichment plant of the Provincial Museum of Mines, and in Stanghe the white marble gorge of Gilfenklamm, natural monument, with the ruins of Castel Reifenegg.
Built in the first century AD, one of the most important examples of public construction of the ancient Teate Marrucinorum; visible from the outside.

18-hole par 72 course founded in 1964 on the idea of John Morrison and John Harris, in the valley of the Lerrone near Albenga and Alassio: the trail alternates views, pines, farmhouses and centuries-old olive trees.

Built in the nineteenth century by farmers of Calabrian origin, it preserves the original floor in majolica; the village of Pollara grew around it. In the square in front of the mural with Massimo Troisi and Pablo Neruda (Philippe Noiret) sitting on a bench, from which you can see the Scoglio Faraglione and, in the distance, Filicudi.
View from the postcard.
Wanted in 1606 by Pierre-Léonard Roncas, first Secretary of State of Duke Charles Emanuele I, then seat of the Savoy administration.
Wine shop closed in January and from Tuesday to Friday according to Visit MRL
Hillside, dirt paths uphill
The historic entrance to the city on the Adda.
The battle that changed the Risorgimento.
Freisa and Malvasia trails.
The Catalan Gothic in Sardinia.

From the viewpoint of Quattrocchi the view of the faraglioni Long Stone and Stone Menalda; not far away the traffic light, geophysical observatory in a former traffic light of the Navy, looks on the faraglioni and on Vulcano.

Themed area in the woods designed to be inclusive and accessible, with statues inspired by classical fairy tales (from the Little Prince to the Little Mermaid) and the Sword in the rock, braille panels and events and shows.
The little church of the mule trackers on the high ground.
Dedicated to Vincenzo Lancia, founder of the car company.
The Byzantine crucifix.

Founded in 1510, the Dominican monastery reached its maximum splendor in the 17th century: about 23,000 square meters with five cloisters and a Latin cross church with six side chapels, entirely decorated in marble by mostly Roman and Neapolitan artists. Thomas Campanella stayed there. Destroyed by the earthquake of 1659 and rebuilt by Fr. Bonaventura Presti, it was ruined by the earthquake of February 5, 1783; it remains legible, with the facade of the ancient church declared a national monument.
It preserves archaeological finds from different eras found in the territory.
The horse racing site of the Bourbon kings.
The 360 degree panorama of Valdarno and Chianti.
Six centuries of a Castiglionese family.

Quadrangular fortress that dominates the village, built by Bertoldo Falletti of Alba after having received the feud in 1225 by the Marquises of Saluzzo; the Falletti, who gave the name to the village, held it until the end of the seventeenth century, then passed to the Caramelli, the Clarotto, the arcade poet Giuseppe Cerutti and the Vassallo of Dogliani, who in the mid nineteenth century adapted it to a noble residence. It preserves the medieval system with two lateral towers and the central male; in its walls was found a Roman plaque with the figure of a "sutor" (sculpture).
The narrow alley.
Birdwatching in the heart of Sicily.
The 18th-century staircase frescoed in the town hall.

Roman triumphal arch of 2 AD, wanted by Augustus: it was the gate of the city of Fanum Fortunae and marks the point where the Via Flaminia reaches the Adriatic; around remains traces of the Roman walls.
A Greek city on a plateau 850 meters away, with the theatre overlooking the valley.
Environmental education center with the museum and weaving workshop "Penelope File."

Roccaforte founded at the beginning of the fifth century BC against Volsci (Roman Colony from 491 BC), was taken by Silla in 81 BC and, according to Appiano, burned by the inhabitants themselves; never rebuilt, it is called the "Pompei Republicana dei Lepini" . The polygonal drywalls run for about 2.5 km around 44 hectares, with four gates including the monumental Porta Maggiore; inside paved roads, monumental baths, twelve domus, two acropolis with the basements of the temples (including that of Diana) and the sanctuary of Juno Lucina. Free audio guide with 27 QR points.
The park of the fort.
Together they form a defensive complex of the village.

Medieval village of Sabina between the olive groves of DOP Sabina, with the panoramic piazza of the Cathedral, the archaeological museum of Sabina Tiberina in Palazzo Brancaleoni and the Museum of Silence of the Clarisse Hermits; in the hamlet of Farfa the Benedictine abbey, national monument since 1928.
The wreck of the ancient humid forest of plain, oasis of protection of the fauna, also known for the truffle; the entrance is on the banks of the Napoleonic Cable.

Built in 1349 in Gothic style on the remains of a pagan temple, it preserves a Byzantine holy waterworks; in April and August, during the novenas, the faithful inhabit the ancient cumbessias around the church.

First century A.D. lava stone theatre built on a Greek building, up to 7000 spectators, with the waters of the Amenano emerging in the orchestra; next to the Odeon for poetic competitions and the Antiquarium in Casa Pandolfo and Casa Liberti.

Village of steep streets that descend on the eastern shore of Lake Como, with the Villa Monastero, former Cistercian monastery today house museum with a botanical garden almost two kilometers long until Fiumelatte, the garden of Villa Cipressi, the church of San Giorgio consecrated in 1313 and the ornithological museum Luigi Scanagatta.
Dedicated to Mary Most Holy of the Visitation, wanted by Queen Eleonora d'Angiò: facade between Gothic and Sicilian Baroque, tower in facade and coffered ceiling in the central aisle.

Impressive castle overlooking the Ionian Sea, erected in the thirteenth century, when the village lived its maximum splendor; it is among the marine fortresses that defended the Calabrian coast, perfectly preserved and visitable even inside.
Two hundred species of birds in the park up close.
The visionary universe of a Salentine artist in his garden.

The museum occupies the Palazzo Caccia-Canali, a project attributed to Jacopo Barozzi called the Vignola, completed in 1589, with frescoes, friezes and large sixteenth-century fireplaces; since 2020 it is part of the network of historic residences of Lazio and also houses the Pinacoteca. The geological, anthropological, botanical and fauna routes tell the Riserva del Soratte: traces of the animals of the woods, typical plants, the formation of the caves and the prehistoric tools of the first populations.

Museum of Italian-Albanian culture dedicated to Giuseppe Gangale, glottologist and professor at the University of Copenhagen: exhibits tools of peasant and craftsman work, the permanent nativity scene  "Nativity Arbereshe" with typical costumes and original documents of Gangale, including manuscripts and testimonies of the alphabet with which he transcribed the Albanian oral heritage. It has permanent and temporary exhibitions, photo library and teaching room.
On the ground floor of the castle, the permanent archaeological exhibition shows in the mast the statues from the excavations of the Roman city of Potentia.
How the Roman spa town was.

Archaeological museum housed in the castle, with objects from all over the Lomellina, including terracotta statuettes and rare Roman glass, such as the white-green cup signed by Aristesas in Albonese.
In the fortress built in 1354 by Cardinal Gil Alvarez Carrillo de Albornoz, the museum dedicated to Etruscan archaeology and the oldest origins of the city.

From the town's viewpoint the view spans the Alps, the Ligurian Apennines, the Monferrato and the towers of the nearby villages; the town has been recognized as the second most panoramic view of Italy.
In the Jewish quarter the remains of the Portico d'Ottavia and the Teatro di Marcello, the Temple Major and the Jewish Museum of Rome.

The fifteenth-century complex was completed by 1560: Giovanni del Bene bought it from Antonio Malfatti in 1538-1539, renewed it and frescoed its interiors, and the villa hosted prelates of the Council of Trento. The monumental portal, attributed to Michele Sanmicheli, dates back to 1551; the first courtyard has the oldest building with porch and loggia, the second a crenellated dolombara tower. The frescoes, recently restored, are attributed to Domenico Brusasorzi, Nicola Crollanza and Bernardino India: pergolas with grape petti on the staircase, landscapes of the Adige and the Chiusa and Roman stories in the loggia, eight sibillas and four scenes of the Apocalypse in the salon. It is State-owned and is open on Sunday afternoons (April-September 14-19, October-March 14-18) and by reservation on other days.
Città Bandiera Arancione from the chessboard system enclosed between two monumental arches, with noble palaces, the panoramic bastions and the famous antique markets.

Great sanctuary of the second century BC dedicated to the patron god of Tibur, 188 for 140 meters on terraces above the Aniene, with a theatre for about 3,600 spectators, a piazza porticata and the temple; the Via Tecta crossed it in a vaulted gallery. It was abandoned in the 6th century.
The IGP piggy where she was born.
The Pavia of pilgrims.
The castrum above the Santa Valley.
The seventeenth-century palace of the municipality.

Founded by the Normans in the 11th century, according to Italia.it on the ruins of a temple dedicated to Poseidon; integrated in baroque forms between the seventeenth and eighteenth centuries, damaged by the earthquakes of 1905 and 1908 and then renovated. In the aisle the chapel of Our Lady of the Rosary.

Permanent exhibition at Palazzo Grosso born from Domenico Torta's research on Piedmontese folk music, with the contribution of scholars of the University of Turin as Febo Guizzi: musical instruments, objects, documents and testimonies of Piedmont's sound culture, waiting for a wider museum project.
MiC tab indicates closed every day and does not report the address, check (tel. 338 9986944)
Two beaches on the sides of the harbor.
The art saved from the earthquake.
Wild-looking beach, surrounded by rocks.
A dive into slow weather.
The oldest door in Perugia.
The museum in the premises of Palazzo Massimo, Terme di Diocletiano and Palazzo Altemps.
Twelve centuries of Friulian history on the hill of Monte.

National monument, born in the 13th century according to the legend from the passage of St. Francis directed to the sanctuary of St. Michael on the Gargano; of the sixteenth century monastery remains the cloister with the cistern, while the current structure, with new cloister and new church, is of the mid eighteenth century. The single nave church, with chapels, transept and stucco, has the Chapel of the Crucified with the relic of the Sacco of St. Francis and in sacristy the cenotaph that Margherita Orsini erected for her husband Diego I Cavaniglia, who died in 1481 after the battle of Otranto. Abandoned with suppressions, it was restored in 1933 with the return of the friars.
Theatre created for the Illuminati Academics by Antonio Gabrielli, with the first performance in 1666, rebuilt since 1783 and municipal since 1939.
The culture of Umbrian oil.

18th-century cathedral designed by Benedetto Alfieri, originally frescoed by Paolo Gaidano, overlooking St. John's Square, the center of the historic centre. The parishyard and the central door have a fixed slide for wheelchairs.
Porphid lanes between ancient medieval buildings, with Gothic churches in the profile of the city; on Advent weekends the candles illuminate lanterns and alleys.
Built in the 12th century, it houses the statue of Our Lady of Victory, carried in procession during the feasts of the Assumption and St. Joseph.
The village of the caves, between artist fountains and panorama.
Church with octagonal dome in Venetian Gothic style next to the Cathedral; it conserved a polyptych attributed to Paolo Veneziano, today exhibited in the Diocesan Museum.
Another time painted by the Baschenis.

The door of 1513 leads the Lion of St Mark on the outer arch and a Napoleonic inscription on the rights and duties of man and citizen; the stone bridge of 1780, with two large arches with six hillsides, replaced a wooden drawbridge.
The mountain village.
The most important place of worship in Civita Castellana.

Small town of the Maira Valley linked to the itinerant trade of the anchovies, told by the Seles Museum in the former seventeenth-century church of San Rocco; among the villages stands Serre with a rare log house (Blockbau), and the territory is crossed by four thematic paths, the GTA and the Occitani Routes.
visits only by reservation, free access during the events

I shelter under rock along the left bank of Natisone, near a mill of the seventeenth century, inhabited for over 5,000 years between the upper Paleolithic and the Neolithic: the oldest finds are about 10,000 years old. The Regional Speleological Catasto records it as a small cavity of 17 meters, excavated in 1978, which returned junk worked. You will arrive for a cart from Biarzo or for a path shaded by Ponteacco.
The square with the fountain of 1929 with three oval baths of white marble, in front of the portal of Ca' Spineda.

In the nave of the "Duomo Nuovo" never completed, one of the oldest private museums in Italy, with the Majesty of Duccio; from the unfinished facade you can enjoy one of the most spectacular views of the city.
Where the Sile enters the lagoon of Venice.
The 17th-century façade in festoons.

Reserve oriented established in 1997 on about 3,712 hectares between Ferla, Cassaro, Sortino, Palazzolo Acreide and Buscemi: poplars, willows and spontaneous oriental plane, orchids of the Iblei, macrostigma trout, hawks and eagles, and the Cave of the Bats. Along the valley the former Syracuse-Vizzini railway of the early twentieth century is today a pedestrian and cycle path with some galleries.

Panoramic view of the sunny side of the Val Gardena, in the Puez-Odle Nature Park, reachable with the facilities from Ortisei: from the top the view embraces the Dolomites and the mountains of South Tyrol. Several cabins serve local cuisine with sun terraces and stube; destination of skiers, hikers, paragliders and families, open all year round.
A Byzantine-Norman jewel in the country.

The complex with the remains of the Constantinian basilica, the mausoleum of St. Constance of the fourth century, the basilica of Pope Honorius I (625-638), among the best preserved early Christians, and the catacombs of St. Agnes.
The natural history of Capri.
Birdwatching on the banks of the Sile.
Energy and forest in the history of the country.

The municipality describes it as monumental architectural work of Norman times, linked to devotion to the patron saint of St. Nicholas, with statues of saints and valuable paintings. Free entry during functions.
The collection of the founder of modern criminology, with skulls, skeletons, mortuary masks and models of prisons in the original nineteenth century windows.

Set up in the Documentation Centre for Local History and Culture, the ecomuseum cell of the park in the Genoese style building linked to the holiday of the noble families of Genoese: original work tools, a room on local cultivars and reconstructions of haymaking, working land and mountain traditions, with multimedia room and library. Visitable by reservation with the park.

Medieval village at 359 meters, about 5 km from the capital on the Mondaviese road, already of Fano and autonomous municipality until the beginning of the twentieth century: you enter from a small square closed by the former town hall with the iron clock tower; in the square the church of San Michele with works of the stonemasons, then houses in sandstone, alleys, arches and escarpted walls with views from the Apennines to the Adriatic. In May the Snail Festival.

The largest church in Italy, Gothic, with its golden spires and Madonnina since 1774; inside capitals with statues, biblical windows and the sundial of 1786; in the elevator you go up to the terraces between the spires.
The ancient hospice for travellers and stone fountains recalls the importance of the village on the French Road.
A Benedictine abbey in the countryside.
The garden on the Captain's Lake.

Wanted by Cardinal Branda Castiglioni in the fifteenth century as a Renaissance village for himself and the family, after his death it was not transformed and the main buildings came almost intact; you walk up narrow streets to the terrace of the Collegiata, with views over the valley of the Olona. In the village are held the Carnival and the Giostra dei castelli.
Medieval church in the garden of Russell Page.

Municipality of the plain of Pordenone along the Meduna, with the hamlet of Rauscedo known as the world capital of the Barbatella for the wine-growing life; in the plain of Richinvelda, where in 1350 the patriarch Bertrando was killed, stands the church of San Nicolò, while in Pozzo the Museum of peasant civilization preserves the collection of Gelindo Lenarduzzi.
Walk on the way of the shepherds who gave birth to the country.
Park with exotic species 200 meters from Villa Nobel.
The Last Supper of Leonardo translated into wood carvings.
The terrace overlooking the sea of the city.
To be checked: guided tours at extra charge

Stone village 600 meters between the Reatini Mountains and Lake Piediluco, accessible only on foot, dominated by the castle Nobili Vitelleschi and restored from the seventies of the twentieth century by the Belgian architect Ivan Van Mossevelde; Orange Flag of the Touring.
The domestic life of the former hamlets.

A small early Christian cemetery discovered in the 1960s by the archaeologists of the British School at Rome, used between the 4th and 5th centuries: an underground with five short corridors and a cubicle, loculi closed by mortar and bricks and walls plastered with white, without elaborate frescoes.
The two buildings indicated by the official card among the things to see in the village.

The restorations of the sixties and seventies revealed behind the church an Etruscan temple of the fifth century BC dedicated to Tinia and Menerva: the altar remains visible, almost five meters long and reached by a staircase, used mainly between the V and the 1st century BC; the finds (antifixes at the head of Minerva, ceramics, worked blocks) are in the museums of Bibbiena and Arezzo. Between the 8th and 9th centuries there was a first Christian church; the present Romanesque parish church of the 12th century has three naves divided by decorated pillars, a splendid apse and a cylindrical bell tower.

The castle, of thirteenth-century origin, rebuilt in the fifteenth century and adapted to dwelling in the eighteenth century, dominates the village. The chapel, already documented in 1349 and once connected to the castle, houses on two registers a cycle of fourteenth-century frescoes on the life of Christ, from the Annunciation to the  "Noli me tangere" (the Annunciation to the "Noli me tangere"), defined by the Municipality as the major of Piedmont and attributed to a painter of the Lombard school called Maestro di Montiglio; covered with plaster during a pestilence, were rediscovered in 1931 and restored since 1984.
White stone and baroque decorations.
Ventilation well of 1955, 336 m, the highest point of the mine, 410 m deep: its wooden structure is the only one left in the Metalliferous Hills. Next to the winch building and the air extractor.
The mother church of Abano with the 14th century bell tower.

Cittadina della Piana di Gioia Tauro was built on the site of the ancient Medma, a town founded by the Greeks of Locri: the Archaeological Museum (2014) and the archaeological park of Pian delle Vigne with the famous medmea terracotta; in the village the Clock Tower (1812) and the churches of Purgatory and Rosary.

In the eighteenth century Palazzo Felici: about 500 local fossils of marine fauna of the lower Pliocene (cyrripeds, about sixty species of molluscs, sea urchins, shark teeth, fossil leaves) and finds from the world, including mammoth fangs of the North Sea, an egg of dinosaur from China and an egg of Aepyornis. About 1,200 minerals, including a 26 kg block of stilbite with natrolite, and a fluorescent mineral cave at the Wood lamp; on the first floor about 300 paintings made with ten thousand shells by Elio Ceccotti. In the building also the Environmental Education Center and the Ecomuseo, archive of the popular knowledge of Fermano.

The city symbol of the rebirth of Friuli after the earthquake of 1976, rebuilt stone on stone: the Romanesque-Gothic Cathedral, the oldest sanctuary dedicated to Saint Anthony, the castle and the palaces of the center, between Tagliamento and the mountains.
Covered market of local producers, Tuesday and Saturday morning.

In the upper medieval village remain the watchtower, the only remnant of the ancient fortifications, and the tower-gate of San Francesco, one of the three gates of the village; between the buildings the Palazzo del Priorato with the loggia of the sixteenth century and the Town Hall. There are also the convent and the birthplace of Blessed Maria Assunta Pallotta. In August, Antichi Flavors through the streets of Borgo will reopen the shops of the ora with live processing.
17th century church with octagonal plan on Piazza Umberto I, near the Oratory of the Immaculate.
Water and green outside of town.

Borgo at the entrance of the Varaita Valley among the orchards of the Saluzzo plain: noble palaces, the eighteenth-century bridge over Varaita and the parish with the Christ of Pietà attributed to Hans Clemer.
Dedicated to boats and marine traditions.

Baroque church with a single nave, linked to a confraternity, with dome above the apse, wooden choir, walls decorated with pilasters and golden stuccoes and bell tower with square plan. It is located about 50 meters from the main square.

Above Rusio along the path CAI 317, is traditionally the oldest church in the territory and the first parish; rectangular plan and rich in frescoes, carries the inscription "Albinonus pingere fecit p(er) his vow on the arch. 1580. Restored in 1974.

Founded in 1011 by St. Alferio Pappa Carbone in the Selano valley: the basilica of 1761 by Giovanni del Gaizo preserves an ambo from the 12th century and sculptures by Tino da Camaino; you can also visit the Romanesque cloister, the chapels of the ancient basilica, the catacombs, the Longobard cemetery, the museum and library with over 80,000 volumes and an archive of parchments since 792.

Built in 1476 on the site of a pre-Romanesque oratory documented in 954 and restored by Giulio Ulisse Arata at the beginning of the twentieth century: traces of frescoes from the fifteenth century and two wooden statues, a Madonna with Child and a Deposition, attributed to Jan Hermansz Geernaert.
The municipal gallery surrounded by the Public Gardens overlooking the sea, on the slope under the district of Castello, with a small climbing wall for beginners.
By bike to Modena on the old railway.
The theatre of the two painters.

The trail of the Olive-Arco runs for more than 4 km between the olive groves of the village; that of the Leccio climbs to the Hermitage of Sant'Erasmo and arrives at the slopes of the Anchevisa. The territory is suitable for hiking, hiking and mountain biking.
A fragment of Roman Sicily at the gates of Catania.
The market square along the stream, with the covered market Country Friend of agricultural producers (salami, Parmesan, fresh pasta, possibility to have lunch) and weekly markets.
The exhibition center in the former church of San Marco, home to large exhibitions such as those with the Guggenheim collection and the Magna Charta; open for exhibitions.

Next to the station, the names of the deportees are engraved on slabs on the ground in front of three railway cars, those of the few survivors on vertical plates. In September 1943, some 800 Jewish refugees who had crossed the French border and the Gesso Valley were stopped by the SS and interned in the former barracks of the Alps, then deported to Auschwitz; in 2001 the city received the Gold Medal to the Civil Merit. Free visit.

Dominican monastery of the fifteenth century with cloister with black stone columns; the gallery in the former dormitory preserves polyptychs and frescoes by Ludovico Brea and Canavesio and the Adoration of the Magi del Parmigianino (1528-29).

Theatre in 279 B.C. of Pirro's victory over the Romans, Ascoli Satriano houses the Trapezophoros in the Museum Pole with the grifos that pierce a deer, returned by the Getty Museum in 2007; beyond the Roman bridge on Carapelle the Archaeological Park of the Dauni opens, while the castle and the cathedral dominate the historic center.
A castle of Longobard origin.
The frescoed boats of a missing mansion.
The loggia of the manor became theater.
A Roman cistern under a church.

The nineteenth-century building is surmounted by a tower, with halls decorated with paintings by the Basile school and original Art Nouveau furnishings; the ground floor opens onto a beam. It houses the permanent exhibition of the artistic nativity scene depicting Sommatino in miniatura.
The first Christianity of the harbor.
The chief's tower.

17th century, near Porta Diaz and the headquarters of the Confraternities, with a fresco of the Madonna enthroned with the Child attributed to Vincenzo Pagani; in the village you can also visit the cloister of the Augustinians, the garden of St. James and the courtyard of the Clarisse, of thirteenth century.
The golden altar of the Badia Grande.
The two main churches of the village, both built around the year 1000.
The pier bearing the name of the emperor Caligula, remembered for wanting it as a connection with Ischia.
The majolica dome symbol of the country.

The eighteenth-century villa on the top of the hill of Sumirago, around which the village developed; among the owners the nuns of via Brera in Milan, the Sola Cabiani, the leader Bartolomeo Colleoni and, between the nineteenth and twentieth centuries, the Marquises Stanga. With a rectangular plan with a rear central body and two wings, it has to the south a large arcade with arches on the neo-Gothic rustic courtyards and a large park; inside the cantinone with brick vault, the ice-cake, the hall of the coats of arms and the library in the former barn. Today it is the seat of the Town Hall and has been opened for the FAI Fall 2020 Days.
Tristan and Isotta and Pordenone.
Romanesque church with a cycle of frescoes on the life of San Lorenzo.

Borgata with one of the few buildings in the valley with walls in overlapping wooden trunks (Blockbau). A steep covered passage dug into the rock, with lateral stairs leading to the doors of the houses, leads to the path that goes up the ridge towards Castellaro: it is indicated as one of the most interesting covered passages of the villages of the valley.
A stop for pilgrims.
Meet a hunter from 7,500 years ago and in the footsteps of dinosaurs.
The Moor beating the hours.

The convent of the Clarisse rises in the upper part of the village; it is accessed by passing the chapel of the Crucifix, of the twelfth century, entirely frescoed in the seventeenth century by Pietro Antonio Ferro, painter of Ferrandina.
The award-winning peasant museum in Europe.

The local stone walls, built from the 5th century BC, enclose the small medieval village and are still visible in some stretches; along the walls are the foundations of the Temple of Hercules of the II century BC.

Made by the Malabailas in the sixteenth century instead of an ancient oratory near the castle, of late dogotic plant with modifications in the seventeenth and nineteenth centuries, when bell tower and facade were built today.
A panoramic garden on the walls.
Art of the seventeenth century in a hill town.
Celestine V Prison, also mentioned by Dante.
An unexpected neo-Gothic villa in the village.

From Norman foundation, several times remodeled after the earthquakes, with two Gothic portals and works of art inside; at the entrance two unexploded bombs recall the protection attributed to Our Lady.
The heart of the reborn country after the eruption.

Civic tower of the 14th century about 28 meters high in the highest point of the historic center, with views from the Adriatic to the Sibillini Mountains; it had no defensive function and in the 19th century there was placed an altar to the Unity of Italy. Opening on request to the Tourist Office.

Borgo on Tufa soil of the Valle del Giovenzano, with a medieval historic center closed by doors, the churches of Santa Maria Assunta and San Lorenzo and the Palazzo di Corte; famous for the most ancient infiorata in Italy, told in the Museo dell'Infiorata, and for the House of the Ancient Tin Boxes.
Walk on the wall.

At the foot of the Fortress, just above the church of Santa Oliva, the monument reminds women victims of violence during the Second World War; from the panoramic point of view the view extends over the Valley of Sacco to the borders with Campania and Abruzzo.
The sanctuary of transhumant shepherds.
from €4 (guided tour)
Devotional bread is a tradition that expresses the spirituality of the country and the bond with the earth.
An easy walk.

Ecomuseum dedicated to the production chain of felt, born around the ancient felt factory: exhibits huge and intact machinery, some still working and sometimes in use, next to an active factory that produces every day. All tours are guided; in winter the museum is closed except for group bookings, while the workshop remains open.

Of Renaissance origin, renovated at the end of the eighteenth century by Faustino Rhodes with the neoclassical staircase; living room with ceiling in golden wood and a Napoleonic room with original canopy bed.
Hiking and snow in the National Park.

Under the cathedral, reachable by two internal stairs and by an external door; re-arranged in 1935 at the behest of Mgr. Demetrius Moscati, with the removal of the burials. It preserves a chapel dedicated to the Blessed Mgr. Castrillo and a half bust of Saint Francis of Paola; there is the miracle of the  "Scivolenta" of 1855.
Industrial archaeology in the green.
The 19th-century theatre of the city.

Borgo della Baronia at the foot of Monte Tuttovista, Orange Flag of Touring, ancient bishop's seat and "Galte" of "Canne al vento" of Grazia Deledda: the sanctuary of the Blessed Crucifix, the former cathedral of St. Peter with frescoes of the thirteenth century, the museum Sa Domo 'e sos Marras and the ruins of the Castle of Pontes.
The daily life of the Saura linguistic island.
The popular frescoes of a little church in the rock.
A Roman underground world under the square.
Rural and residential castle of the XIV-XV centuries in Surpian resort.

Cited for the first time in 1014 in the diploma with which Arrigo il Santo donated the territory to the church of Vercelli, from the thirteenth century it was fief of the de Ponzano, Castellazzo, Saliceto and de Setaria; an act of 1431 describes palace, tower of the nobles and moat. He then passed to the Donato, counts from 1635 to the Cattaneo, the Tizzoni and the Marquis Church of Cinzano; in the nineteenth century the Camozzi knight created a flower garden (1877) and at the end of the century the garden on the eastern side was built with hedges of boxwood and stone bath. The park has centuries-old trees and a tower with panoramic views; for the visit you should contact the property.
A cornerstone of Benedictine architecture in Abruzzo, at the entrance of the Valle dell'Alento.
The Roman bridge seen from the water.

The sixteen Corinthian Roman columns that delimit the churchyard of the early Christian basilica of San Lorenzo, in front of the medieval Porta Ticinese, animated evening gathering especially in summer.
A park inside a fortress.
The poor pasta of the Aniene valley.
The walkway between rock and water.
A former medieval lazzaretto along the stream.
Three Sienese masters in one room.

Started in 1626 (first Mass on 26 March) by the Oratorian Father Orazio Giustiniani and finished in 1636, as the inscription on the portal says; Visit Lazio indicates it as the first church in the world dedicated to the saint. The façade is sober and internal baroque with a single nave, with on the main altar a copy of the "Estasi di San Filippo Neri" by Guido Reni; the figure of the saint in the facade niche is Fabio Carosi (2008).

Since 1989 Bruno Carletto and Bartolomeo Cavallera (Meo and Carlet) have painted on the facades of the historic center over 150 murals and great illustrations that retrace the adventures of Pinocchio in the style of Attilio Mussino, the first color illustrator of Collodi's novel. They are mainly located along Via Maestra and in the side alleys, in Via Molino Stotto and near the parish, between fountains, squares and courtyards; Casa Carlet has painted facades and a garden with works on the characters.

In the 4th century there was a small oratory, in 1377 linked to the monastery of Chiaravalle della Colomba; the current Baroque building was started in 1665. It preserves a Nativity of the sixteenth century and, in the last chapel on the right, the oldest part, a fresco probably thirteenth century with the Madonna enthroned with the Child. Visitable on agreement taken in advance with the culture office.

Mulattiera of about three kilometers, an hour and a quarter on foot, which goes up gently to Castelvecchio; dedicated to Ilaria Del Carretto, takes its name from a fifteenth-century farm of Del Carretto.
The promontory with the biomarine park, where griffins live, and the nature reserve suitable for trekking and birdwatching.
The dome with the oculus open to the sky.
The frescoes of Orelli in the town hall.

Official residence of Gonzaga until the 17th century: Corte Vecchia with the Studio of Isabella d'Este, Corte Nuova with the Apartment of Troy of Giulio Romano, the Rooms of Pisanello, the Flemish tapestries on cardboards of Raffaello, the hanging garden; here the Orfeo of Monteverdi was represented in 1607.
May pilgrimage.

In the heart of the Sibillini Park, alpine landscape with rich flora and fauna; Mount Torrone is the base for excursions on Mount Bove (vette of 2,112 and 2,169 m) and Mount Bicco (2.052 m), walls also known for mountaineering. On clear days you can see the Adriatic.
A noble house that remains intact.
The walls that give the city its scorpion shape, with four of the six ancient gates: Porta Santi, Porta Riume, one of the two Portaccia and Porta Montanara.

Borgo grew up within three circles of concentric walls, each with four doors, of which the best preserved stretch is the civic tower next to the Town Hall; in the Palazzo Augustiniano the Museum of Sacred Art and the exhibition of the ancient walking trades.
A shop from the beginning of the twentieth century remained as it was.

On the second floor of the former Town Hall, renovated by Barone in the late nineteenth century with façade in Florentine style; the collection donated in 1897 is exhibited in two rooms with original cases: Neapolitan paintings (Luca Giordano, Francesco Solimena) and Flemish, an Egyptian canopy vase, over 120 Greek and Italian ceramics, Etruscan bronzes and jewels, porcelain of Capodimonte and Pescolanciano, Chinese, Japanese and Indian objects.
Six rooms with seven-nineteenth-century furnishings and over 2000 objects (balances, mortars, stills, vases) tell two centuries of pharmacy history.
A break in the woods with picnics.

In a clearing at the foot of Mount Ascensione, built by the monks of Farfa on the ruins of a pagan temple dedicated to Artemis; restored in the eighteenth century, it is dedicated to the Madonna of the Consolation, celebrated on 15 August. It has a nave, terracotta floor and travertine altar; in the garden an oak tree over 23 meters high.
An 18th-century theatre in the center.

The historic typography     . The nocetana graphics, purchased by the Municipality by the family of the master printer Ferdinando Libassi: a press From the Garden of the second half of the nineteenth century, a Monzese pedal, a nineteenth-century plate of the Mordini brothers and a Nebiolo plate, all working, and millions of characters, friezes and reordered fillets. Open Monday, Wednesday, Thursday and Friday 8.30-12.30; Saturday and Sunday by appointment.

In an ancient cheese factory with circular plan close to the wall of the garden of the Fortress: tools and tools of cheese processing and historical photographs. It is part of the Museums of Food in the province of Parma.

130 meters long, 142 steps built from 1606 to join the lower city to the mother church; from 1954 the raised ones are covered with majolica that reproduce in chronological order decorations from the X to the XX century. In May it hosts the Infiorata and on 24 and 25 July, for San Giacomo, it lights up with colorful lights.

Four halls of artifacts, photographs and documents on the "Valtoce" and on the "Grouping of Patriotic Divisions" (Alfredo Di Dio) were autonomous formations that supported the Republic of Ossola: after the Battle of Ornavasso in October 1944 partisans and civilians repaired in Switzerland, to return to fight until Milan on April 24-25, 1945.
visits only by appointment through the Tourist Office of the Municipality
The Vitelli Palace.
The symbolic door of the Venetian Cream.
The medieval village on the Tifatini.

On the summit of Monte Gemola, the villa is owned by the Province of Padua and is open to the public: inside two educational exhibitions on the flora and fauna of the territory of Euganean, whose visit takes 30-45 minutes. From the Brolo and the meadows you can see Mount Fasolo, Venda, Monte Rusta and Cinto Euganeo.

Already existing in the thirteenth century and rebuilt in the fifteenth century in Gothic forms such as Pico's pantheon, it kept the marble arches of the lords of Mirandola, including that of Prendiparte by Pier Paolo and Jacobello dagli Masegne (1394), and the nineteenth-century cenotaph of Giovanni Pico. The 2012 earthquake almost completely destroyed it, including the bell tower: only the facade was saved.

Relief of 785 meters of tuffs and basalts with spires and towers, about 11 km from Arbus near the former mines of Montevecchio: from the summit the view extends over the Gulf of Oristano, the Costa Verde and the Campidano. An easy path taken care of by the CAI starts from the former mines; on top the ruins of a castle documented since 1164, then Vallombrosan monastery. Lecci, spot, deer, wild boar, royal eagle and pilgrim falcon.

Church whose foundation dates back to the eighth century, with origins still wrapped in legend; it preserves frescoes from the second decade of the seventeenth century by Martino Bonfini da Patrignone depicting five Sibyls: Cumana, Ellespontica, Agrippina, Frigia and Delfica.

Free beach of white pebbles between two high rock walls, in an ancient blade that cuts the cliff a few steps from the old town: the most famous and photographed view of the Bari coast, Blue Flag and 4 Vele di Legambiente. Very crowded in summer: it is better to arrive early.
A Byzantine mosaic.

A sixteenth-century fountain linked to Margherita d'Austria, also called Farnesiana, in the main square; around, well-preserved historical palaces like the Mongalli Palaces (one is the seat of the municipality, with a local stone portal), Palazzo Ettore, the largest in the country, and Palazzo Cherubini, where in 1899 the composer Bixio Cherubini was born.
Ruire in Gothic-Svevo style in a green valley about 8 km from the village towards Lentini, once outpost of the Knights Templars.
The large park beyond the walls at the end of Corso Ercole I d'Este, the green lung of the city.
The frescoes of Civerchio in a country church.
The church of the Sacred Milk relic.
The 35 meters high statue dedicated to San Carlo Borromeo, climbable to the head, on the square of the church of San Carlo.
Etruscan and Middle Ages of Casentino in two rooms.
The village of origin of the Puccini family.
The church of the ex-voto of the Chioggiotti.

San Vito di Leguzzano preserves in the Court Priory-Gandin the Ethnographic Museum on woodworking, dedicated to carpentry and the workshop of bottai, crafts certified in the village since the early fifteenth century; the parish church of Santi Vito, Modesto and Crescenzia, rebuilt in the eighteenth century on a project by Giovanni Miazzi, has a classical facade of 1858.

Romanesque country church of the second half of the 12th century, restored in the 17th century, cited in the act of founding the Camaldolese monastery of Santa Maria di Bonarcado (the dome of sanctu Petru de Vidoni). A unique nave about eight meters long with an apse to the east, in polychrome trachite from red to light yellow, a hut façade with a small stone cross and a wooden cover with trusses; on the left of the altar a Roman funerary stele of the II century A.D. with Latin inscription.
The Roman bridge over the Buthier which gives its name to the eastern quarter of the city, Pont de Pierre,
A villa still closed.

In Torrepaduli, rebuilt in 1882 preserving the main altar in stone of 1738 with the canvas of the saint of Giovanni Grassi di Lecce (1851); mosaic floor by Michele Peluso di Tricase (1891), Latin cross plan with vaults on the edge of the Lecce and, in the transept, two nineteenth-century altars dedicated to Saint Lucia and the Baptism of Christ. Recognized as Church-Sanctuary in 1952, it is the destination of the night of San Rocco between 15 and 16 August, when the churchyard is danced the pinch until dawn.

It brings together the archaeological museum, with finds of ancient, medieval and modern age from the city and the territory, and the section of the traditional costume, dedicated to the "pacchiana" , the costume richly embroidered that was part of the dowry of the bride. The archaeological park of Gianmartino and the Ecomuseo Fortezza-Monte are also part of the polo; guided tours, also in foreign language, and excursions are offered. Access with ramps.
Hillside location at 397 meters, reached by a panoramic road with hairpin bends, rich in trulli and woods of holm oak, carobs, arbutus and lentischi.

Erected in 1420 and renovated between 1728 and 1732 on a project attributed to Giorgio Massari, with his convent; altarpiece of the apse of Pietro Damini (1616-17), altarpiece of Egidio Dall'Oglio (about 1740), six lateral altars in 18th century marble and wooden choir in carved walnut.
Three epochs in a church.
The market in the most beautiful square.

The nineteenth-century neighborhood of tanneries on the opposite bank of the river, a national monument of industrial archaeology, evidence of the production of leather between the mid-nineteenth and early twentieth centuries.
Three and a half centuries of corks and bottles.
The Dominican basilica with the façade of Leon Battista Alberti, the Masaccio Trinity, the Giotto Crucifix, the Ghirlandaio Tornabuoni Chapel and the Green Cloister.

Established on October 2, 1980 by the will of the painter William Congdon, he protects the corpus of his figurative and literary work, he manages an archive, a library and the William G Collection. Congdon Foundation is promoting research on contemporary art and organizing exhibitions, debates and the regest of the artist's omnia work.

Piazzaforte started in 1548 by Cosimo I with the architects Bellucci and Camerini, then Bernardo Buontalenti: the forts Falcone, Stella and Linguella united by walls and walkways, which in 1553 resisted the assault of the corsair Dragut; from Forte Falcone a wide panorama of the sea.
The Norman tower inside the church.
House of a 15th-century merchant with the Sala delle Sibille, linked to the monastery of Corpus Domini.
Sicilian folk traditions.
Listen to and see Stradivari's tools.

The capital of Alto Molise is more than 800 meters away, the Orange Flag of Touring, born according to tradition from a colony of Venetians following the Borrello; it is the village of the bells, with the Pontifical Fonderia Marinelli and its museum, of copper and of the 'Showed, the large torches brought in procession on the night of 24 December, and preserves a Venetian district overlooking the valley of Verrino.

It was built at his expense in 1749 by the abbot Michele Falletti, of the family that had the lordship of Rodello since the end of the sixteenth century. Baroque, with neoclassical-inspired façade, has an interior with Greek cross with three altars surmounted by eighteenth-century shovels, stuccoes and Corinthian capitals attributed to the so-called "maestro" of 1749. Today it hosts the Museum of Contemporary Art "Dedalo Montali."
Parish church rebuilt in Baroque style in the seventeenth century; in the right aisle remains traces of the original Renaissance frescoes.
Entering a Cold War missile base.
The prehistory of the Tablekeeper.
A moving tribute.

The last beach in the province of Catanzaro, 4 km long, with white silica sand bottom, free stretches, equipped beaches and tourist villages. Behind the Ionian calanchi are hinged with the historic hilly centre and form an ecosystem declared as a Site of Community Importance.
The source indicates that the fortress is privately owned

Città del Salento, linked to San Giuseppe da Copertino, the "santo dei voli" (saint of flights), born here in 1603, and to the great sixteenth-century castle where Isabella di Chiaromonte, queen of Naples, was born in the fifteenth century. The old town is a maze of narrow streets with Palazzo Pappi; around sanctuaries, the crypt of San Michele and red wine cellars.
The card of the Serenissima was born here.
Guards and Fontebasso canvases in a country church.

The residence was built around the middle of the fifteenth century by Count Ambrogio Varese of Rosate, then passed to Francesco Mussi and Carlotta Borsani. Carlo Dossi, who left his diplomatic career, at the beginning of the twentieth century dedicated himself to archaeological excavations in the territory and set up a museum: a wing houses the collections with finds from the Bronze and Iron Ages, Roman lamps and medieval and modern objects, next to the library of Alberto Pisani Dossi. The tours are guided, with the Fondazione Pisani Dossi and the Associazione Amici del Museo; the study of the writer is usually not open to the public.

Nuragic village-sanctuary in the Lanaittu valley with numerous circular and oval huts and rooms for bronze processing, linked to the cult of water. The hut, called "source" has walls in white limestone and dark basalt with heads of muflon and carved rams, from whose mouths the water gushed in a large central tank. Admission for a fee (amount not indicated).
The square collects the palaces of Remedi noble families, Magni-Griffi, Neri and Picedi.
A hermitage of Francis in the woods.
The Capuchin origins of Acre.

Of thirteenth-century origins, it was rebuilt in 1840 after the collapse of the old bell tower (1838) and completed in the present form in 1930; inside seven altars dedicated to the saints and one to the Madonna, a relic of Blessed Bartholomew, an eighteenth-century altarpiece and the frescoes of Mattielli (1929-1939) on the ceiling and presbytery. The bell tower, begun in 1842 on a project by the Venetian Antonio Diedo and completed in 1893, is 90 meters high, the third of Veneto, and hosts 16 bells (the largest weighs 2.830 kg). The summit, with 360 degrees view, is accessible during the Prima del Torcolato.
Small Romanesque church of the twelfth century on the cliffs of the city, with apse of Lombardy and Pisan taste and remains of frescoes from the end of the fourteenth century.

The sixteenth-century house where the composer was born, restored in 1994 on three levels, is home to the Fondazione Giovanni Pierluigi da Palestrina, research center with a library of polyphonic music; the biographical and iconographic exhibition, curated by Lino Bianchi, retraces life and works from 1525 to 1594. Open Tuesday-Sunday (variable hours, closed Monday).
The Civic Museum in the restored palace: history of the city and the territory, archaeological finds and medieval art.

The original nucleus on the hill overlooking the territory, with a panoramic view. Almost destroyed in 1543, it retains a few medieval traces and the walls of the eighteenth-century bastion; among the buildings, the former fifteenth-century brick nursery with four sharp arched windows, the church of the "Batù" (1596), the sixteenth-century palace of the Counts Balbiano, the Palazzo degli Ormea and the eighteenth-century Villa San Carlo of the Villa family.

Rocca on a hill separated from the center, reachable only on foot along a path; attributed to Robert Guiscardo around the Mille, it was destroyed by order of Frederick II after the conspiracy of the Barons, rebuilt around 1250 and damaged again in 1497. Parts of the towers and walls remain; in the eighteenth century the interior was transformed into the church of the Madonna della Consolazione, called Madonna di Castello, still accessible, with an eighteenth-century canvas of the Madonna and Child. In September the feast of the Madonna di Castello.

The 28 steps that tradition wants to climb from Jesus in the Praetorium of Pilate, brought to Rome by St. Helena in 326 and arranged in 1589 by Domenico Fontana for Sixtus V, with the chapel of the Popes of Sancta Sanctorum.

It was built by Domenico Ludovisi and his son Nicolò, who completed it in 1736; in 1842 the Pesiri stonemasons built the staircase of nine steps in travertine. Inside, the painting of the Palio on the reconciliation between Charles and Emanuele Gesualdo. From here on Easter the representation of the Passion towards the castle. Visits by reservation.
Columns in the sandstone and a viewpoint just a stone's throw away.
The traces of the ancient village in a walk.
Etruscan galleries 140 meters long, with a well that lets you see a lake 30 meters below the road, dedicated entirely to the Etruscan epigraph: about 500 inscriptions on urns and tombstones.
visits only by appointment
The elephant shark and the fauna of the Adriatic.
Church of the XIII century renovated in 1617, with Gothic portal.
The mother church of the high city.
On the trail of D.H. Lawrence.

The site was chosen at Augustian age, between the last years BC and the first A.D., by colonists of Augusta Taurinorum. It was a farmhouse-residence, used in three phases until the middle of the II century AD: a large but sober building, with a quadrangular plan, with two groups of rooms at different altitudes and a porch overlooking the countryside and lakes. Nearby is the oldest known settlement of Caselette, a village of the end of the ancient Bronze Age (about 1700 BC). You can visit in open days with guided tours of the association Ar.c.A.
Sacred art in the bishops' palace.
The octagonal church of the eighteenth century with the frescoes of the Trisca.
The house of the hero of the Resistance Duccio Galimberti, which can be visited free of charge: from the terrace on July 26, 1943 he gave the speech that incited the liberation struggle.
Renaissance church of elegant frescoes by Gerolamo Tornielli in 1540, the most beautiful in the city; in the cloister the Museo del Territorio biellase with Roman finds.
The mother church next to the Fortress, with the bells of Castro.
The Resistance house.
The chapel where the Doges of Amalfi were crowned.
The territory of Fobello is part of the park.
The baroque of Franciscan origin.
A small church with a single nave dedicated to the patron, built where the harvest was saved by a storm; behind the altar a fresco shows the deacon Lorenzo with the grating, symbol of martyrdom.
The castle viewpoint.

Borgo dell'alta valle della Giara in the Regional Natural Park of the Ligurian Alps, with the hamlets of Cènova and Lavina: the stones carved by the stonemasons of Cènova (XIV-XV century) are recounted by the museum spread out "Strade di pietra" (stone streets), while in the chestnut wood stands the fifteenth-century sanctuary of the Madonna Bambina frescoed by Pietro Guido da Ranzo; guarding the village the castle of the Clavesana.
Ancient parish church dating back to 1100, at the top of the climb that leads to the old village on the hill.

After the Great War, the church on the hill welcomed the fallen of 1866 and the First World War, becoming a monument to the Ossuary; around the historical park with Italian walks and trenches, which can be walked only on foot, and a path to the Cross. From the parking lot about 138 meters of dirt; ossuary open from May 1 to September 30, 10-13 and 15-18, closed on Monday. Every July 21st commemoration of the battle of 1866.

Tin south of Cannigione, birdwatching destination: they nest red heron, black stork, falcon fisherman and sultan chicken, and sometimes the flamingos arrive; Sardinia Turismo also mentions the knights of Italy and the swamp falcon.

Country of the high valley of Ceno, 625 meters on the Parma Apennines and along the Via Francigena, appreciated for the summer holiday and dominated by the castle on a spur of red jasper, which houses the museums of the village; in church a youthful work of Parmigianino.
The last walls of the fortress of the Quadrilateral.
The peasant world of the medium plain.

The underground church under the ancient hospital of Massafra, born from the union of two distinct churches, probably for the Eastern and Latin rites; the paintings range from approximately XI to XVII century. It is part of the guided route of the rock churches.

The building dates back to 1304; on the first floor the Teatro Luigi Mercantini, opened in 1824 and completed in 1843 with the Lucia di Lammermoor di Donizetti, closed in 2008 and reopened on 14 April 2012.
Built a first time in 1338, it was rebuilt in the middle of the 17th century and consecrated in 1652.

Court closed with the manor building in the center and, on the sides, the buildings that housed stables and servitude houses; on the left side stands an ancient tower (the sixteenth century for VisitModena, fifteenth century for Emilia-Romagna Tourism).
Towers and walkways of the round of a fortress of plain.
The highest bell tower in the valley and the sea view.
The Moncalvo and Orsola Hunts in a museum collected.
The Matilda church on the spur.
Farm life, mine and Leonardo's cars.

12th century castle on a sandstone spur, main defense of the village, connected by tunnels to the Castidduzzu and the apse of St. Peter; in 1283 was granted in feud to Ruggero di Lauria. Today it hosts the Regional Enoteca for Eastern Sicily.
The sky of the Novare Hills to the telescope and the planetarium.

This is the pearl of Valsassina, which has been a holiday destination since the 19th century. Barzio preserves the seventeenth-century Palazzo Manzoni, the church of Sant'Alessandro and the Museo Medardo Rosso; from the village the historic cable car for the Piani di Bobbio starts.
One of the largest suspended rooms in Europe.
A Venetian villa with sixteenth-century lemon house and frescoed chapel.

It is in the form desired in 1636 by Count Fabrizio di Colloredo, educated in Tuscany at the court of Ferdinando I: a residence in Medici style, a Tuscan villa, built on medieval ruins and inhabited by the Collored for over three centuries, until the end of the First World War. The project is probably attributed to the Florentine Matteo Nigetti: cubic body with four corner towers, large outer staircase with ramps opposite with balcony and Collored coat of arms, central hall passing high over two floors and chapel on the noble floor. A avenue of hundred-year-old cypress trees leads to the façade. Damaged by the earthquake of 1976 and renovated, today hosts exhibitions, cultural events and celebrations.
The little Venice of Treviso.
Varese Turismo indicates museum and Villa Agusta closed in winter (reopening indicated on March 1st)
old thermal buildings in complete renovation
The glass of art of Murano and Europe, a stone's throw from the spa.
A Baroque collegiate rich in works of the eighteenth century.
A crystal pool in the rocks.

1,500 m station of the Mondolè Ski area (over 100 km of slopes and 30 lifts with Artesina and Frabosa Soprana): more than 36 km of slopes with views up to Monviso and Cervino, the panoramic cable car "La Rossa" can also be used by pedestrians, snowparks, snowtubing and night skiing.
the MiC card (updated 2020) indicates closed every day; the municipality lists it among the services of the rock site, check the visit with the caves

Built between the end of the 13th and the beginning of the 14th century above the apse of the southern nave, of Romanesque phase, it was born with military functions and then served to call the faithful and citizens; it is 59,66 meters high and the mechanical clock of Domenico Crespi (1751) was restored and put into operation in 2023. From the top you can enjoy the view of Cream and surroundings; ascend on Saturday, Sunday and holidays 10-12.30 and 14-19, closed from 24 to 26 December.
The heart of ancient Interamnia.
A century of Alpine school.
Founded on the remains of a temple, rebuilt in Gothic style in the thirteenth century; in front, the Egyptian obelisk supported by Bernini's elephant, the "Pulcino della Minerva."

Temple of the XVI century to the east of the village, at the junction between the ancient road Stresa-Orta and the road to Nocco. It was dedicated to the Purification of the Virgin (Madonna of Bretta) and took the name of St. Rocco from a statue of the saint who worshiped there.
From prehistory to Galli: the archeological tale of the upper valley of Misa.
The story of one of the decisive battles on the plateau.

Country of the Cilento National Park, Vallo di Diano and Alburni overlooking the Gulf of Policastro, once a bulwark guarding the valleys of Bussento and Mingardo; on Monte Capitenali stood a fortified Lucana city (VIII century BC), whose finds and the ori of the necropolis of the Scala are exhibited in the Antiquarium and in the Civic Archaeological Museum.
The stone bridge.
In the basement of the fortress and in the moat with the ramparts of Antonio da Sangallo, the museum of the grey sandstone loved by Brunelleschi.
The frescoes by Pier Francesco Mola.
A church built with the bricks of an airfield.
The fortress door of the Carraresi.
Collection of Italian fabrics made between the sixteenth and twentieth centuries, set up in the church of Purgatory.
One of the oldest mechanical nativity scenes in Italy.
Gravina towards the border with Gioia del Colle, where there is a dolmen, a peucetic village of the VI-V century BC, a rocky settlement and a farmhouse.
The mother church of the modern city.
It preserves a cycle of frescoes; here in 1459 Giovanni di Calabria and Marquis Del Carretto signed the armistice between Genoa and the Del Carretto of Finale.
inhabited by a family, not visitable inside
Gothic-siculous portals and noble tombs.

The square with the monument to the painter from 1874 and the house where he lived until 1528, the ancient districts, the bridge over the Mastallon and Palazzo Scarognini d'Adda with the Fisheries Museum.
Murales and ceramics in the alleys of a ridge village.
Borgo della val d'Aveto, Orange Flag, with the feudal castle of the thirteenth century, the sanctuary of Our Lady of Guadalupe and the cheese of San Stè.
The finds of Albintimilium.
White truffle and Valdera cellars.

Country on the southern slopes of Monte Arci, known for the archaeological area of Cuccurada, for the churches of San Bernardino and Santa Maria Carcaxia and for the Fair of the artistic handicrafts of Sardinia, which is held every summer since 1961.
The room of the great eighteenth-century globe.
Compact coastal village of Roman origin under the Doria Castle, part of the UNESCO cultural landscape between Punta Mesco and Punta Persico.
Church of 1643 in an ancient village a few kilometers from Orvinio, along the road to Scandriglia, with works by Vincenzo Manenti.
The MiC card (updated to September 2026) indicates opening every day 9-13, without reservation; tel. 095 921861.
The sanctuary above the city.
The 42-metre waterfall from the suspended bridge.
The residence of the Dukes Caracciolo.
The patroness of the village and the finds of Valdarno.
open by reservation (Consorzio Forestale Terra tra i due Laghi, tel. 0365 745007 or 334 6686327)
The genius of Borromini in little space.
Two villages in a municipality: the Fortress of Castrocaro on the cliff and Terra del Sole, the ideal city wanted by Cosimo I in 1564. Orange Flag since 2005.
The tomb of the founder of the city.
Two-storey quadrangular tower used for the sighting and defense of the coast, part of the sixteenth-century fortifications of the Calabrian coast; visible from the outside.
The heart of the 18th century country.
Fortified building with square plan built between XI and XIII century in pebbles with granite cantonals, modified in the Tre-Quattrocento and in the eighteenth century; bound since 1967.
From the fifteenth century Dolo was a river port thanks to its basin of navigation on the Brenta; today the closed is underground and transformed into a small square.

One of the best preserved historical centers of Salento, at the foot of the Serra dei Cianci. It was closed by a walls with four doors (Porta la Terra, Porta Nova, Porta Castello, Porta Lo Chiuso), demolished in 1867; among the Renaissance palaces there is also Palazzo Orsi, with loggia with arches and battlements, and along Via Scipione Sangiovanni line up the villas of the notables of the late nineteenth and early twentieth century.
The baroque mirror salon.
Two churches outside the historic center: that of Torricella, a small country chapel, dates back to the twelfth century; that of San Rocco in the fifteenth century.
The queen's mansion.
The port symbol.
Natural amphitheatre at about 1400 meters and, higher up, the lakes reachable in summer from Grand-Brissogne passing through the bivouac Ménabréaz.
In the heart of the Calamita mine, among the remains of industrial archaeology, is a dark sandy beach that is not equipped to be reached on foot, by mountain bike or by sea.
Example of Liberty built between 1902 and 1907 for the industrial Oreste Ruggeri, with executive project by Giuseppe Brega, decorated with marine and vegetable motifs; bound in 1962.

The town of Franciacorta with its centre in Ponte Cingoli, known for the olivetan abbey of San Nicola, documented from 1050 and rebuilt between 1450 and 1534 with three cloisters and works by Moretto, Romanino and Lattanzio Gambara; it also houses a seat of the MUSIL, the Museum of Industry and Work, and cellars of Franciacorta like La Valle, in a farmhouse of the fifteenth century at the foot of Mount Delma.
The ruins of the expansive fortress.
The monastery of the friars of the plague, today a place of culture.
From the tower you can see the whole valley.
An 18th century notary palace.

It is named after archaeologist Georges Vallet (1922-1994), and is part of the Villa Fondi de Sangro, built in 1840 and restored after the 1980 earthquake. The route goes from prehistory to the imperial age: the Roman maritime villas with the colossal statue of peplophoros found in Sorrento in 1971 and the plastic of the villa of the Cape of Sorrento, the mosaic nymph of the first century A.D. by Massa Lubrense, the four lions in tufa of the sixth century B.C. of the monument to Liparos, the archaic and classical necropolis of the peninsula, the ex vows of the sanctuary of Athena in Punta Campanella and the relief with sacrifice to Diana.
Undefined times: the source indicates to ask by phone (334 8803292)
1889 cemetery with Art Nouveau friezes.
The solemn parish church of the early twentieth century in modern Baroque style.
Carruggi, focaccia and clear sea.
Outdoor hot water.

The village is closed by a wall with thirteen towers and medieval gates, dominated by the 25-metre-high male; by the Rupe di San Nicola a medieval bridge climbs over the Calore and leads to the village, among the palaces of the feudal men.

The living room of the city and its political center since the middle of the thirteenth century: Palazzo del Podestà with the clock tower, Palazzo dei Priori, Prefecture and Governor's palace, under the gaze of stone lions.

Four centuries of wrought iron in a historic factory in the Elvo Valley.

The ancient Santa Maria in Castello, built around the 1000 and passed to the Franciscans in 1225, preserves Romanesque-Gothic remains and a fifteenth-century bell tower; it houses the Pinacoteca municipale. In the nearby Palazzo Persichetti-Ugolini, inside the former convent complex, there is the Pinacoteca civica with the collection of sacred art.
The treasure of St. Richard.

Beyond the Clock Tower, a church deconsecrated and then used as a small theatre, called       Âlu theatreì Â; according to tradition it was erected in memory of Sofia Amati and preserves a fresco of the school of Carlo Crivelli.

Built at the end of the 16th century, it combines Renaissance and Baroque elements; it is located next to the municipal palace that houses the archaeological museum.
The medieval parish church in the heart of the village.
Rimini Baroque.
The tower on the bay in front of the Rabbit Island.
The ascent to the highest sanctuary in Europe.
The shop of a Venetian mask master.
The cloister of pilgrims.

Country of the wine of the Eastern Hills: in the area of the eighteenth-century Villa of Toppo Florio, where since 1933 the Regional Wine Fair is held, the Museum of Wine Civilization exhibits about 2900 objects of peasant viticulture; on the hill stands the complex of the castle of Buttrio, and the Villa Bartolini contains frescoes of Chiarottini and Canal.
Included in the Rocca ticket (€16.50, boys 6-15 years €11)
A nineteenth century sculpture in the rock, in the middle of the woods.
The Duomo of the Savonese popes.
A mountain sanctuary overlooking the sea.
Mother church of Agropoli, recently restored.
The dinner in Emmaus by Jacopo Bassano.
Really get lost in 200,000 bamboo plants.
A stop along the Ferrara-Cento bike path.
The Parmigianino of Taggia.

Just outside the village on the road to Bagnoregio, it houses a small fresco from 1619 considered miraculous; the current Baroque church was financed in 1732 by the Marquis Pompeo del Monte and his wife Anna Rosa Monaldeschi and above the portal bears the inscription   ÂFabricaverunt sinneres Â . On Sundays after Ascension, the feast with procession distributes the "panettuzzi," small hosts of unleavened bread marked with a cross and blessed.
Apulian Romanesque church next to the Palazzo Marchesale.
The country house of the late eighteenth century at the Chaos where the Nobel was born, today museum with photographs, first editions and posters; united to the Luigi Pirandello Library since 1987.

The capital of the Norman County of Ruggero I and the birthplace of Ruggero II, destroyed by the earthquake of 1783 and rebuilt not far away; today you can visit it between the medieval archaeological park of ancient Mileto, the cathedral and the museum in the bishop's palace, with views of the valley of the Messima.
Byzantine frescoes among lemons.
On the summit of Monte San Pancrazio, near Calvi, remain the ruins of an ancient shrine-hermitage, reached by a panoramic road between woods and clearings.
Zebra church with the famous pulpit of Giovanni Pisano (1298-1301).

An easy walk of about 3 km (one hour) along the road built by the lords of Brandis in 1835, today without water, from Lana di Sopra to the waterfall of Brandis to Lana di Sotto: orchards, vineyards and woods, view of Lana and Merano, the chapel of Santa Margherita, the convent of Lanegg, a shelf of open books and views of the ruins of Castel Brandis. Suitable for strollers and wheelchairs, accessible all year round.

The belt of the Medici fortress of the early sixteenth century, never completed, with the pentagonal castle; the archaeological and technological park tells the hill from the early medieval huts onward.

Built from 1522 by the University of Solofra, in the years of prosperity of the tanneries, instead of a church of Byzantine origin; the fire of 1721 transformed it from Renaissance to Baroque, and after the earthquake of 1980 was reopened in 1986. Latin cross plan, Baroque façade and Romanesque bell tower; the golden coffered ceiling houses 42 paintings with scenes of the Old and New Testament attributed to John Thomas and Francesco Guarini, and inside there are the Pentecost of Angelo Solimena, the Coronation of the Virgin of Giovan Bernardo Lama and a crypt with the chapel of St. Judas Taddeo.

In the district of Serrone remains a megalithic wall with a thickness of more than three meters, testimony of the antiquity of the settlement: dated from the national portal italia.it to the fourth century BC.
The monastery church.
The spa with indoor and outdoor pools.

Born as an archaeological section of the Municipality in the Palazzo Civico delle Arti, it was established as a stable museum with resolution of February 2026, with statute and technical-scientific committee coordinated by Fabio Astone, in collaboration with the Superintendence. It exhibits finds from the municipal territory recovered over decades, in a collection started in the seventies; in the same palace the Spazio Mare and the Civic Library " Costabile Cilento" . Timetable indicated by the Municipality: Tuesday and Thursday 9-13, Saturday 9-13 and 15-19, other days by reservation (0974 277823).
The parish church of the patron, in front of the Town Hall.

The mother church was born from a farm, with the seventeenth-century bell tower on the square.
The theater above the walls.
Uninhabited, with only one landing place in Cala di San Silverio, cliffs and clear waters; nature reserve and marine protected area, with houses dug in the rock and a restaurant on the beach.
Felice Damiani's shovel.
Italian design inside a Gothic abbey.
The great cathedral of the diocese.

Orvietano country in the valley of Paglia, collected around the Castle of the Dukes of Montevecchio and known for its brick and terracotta kilns; in the territory the Etruscan necropolis of Caldane, the villages of Monterubiaglio and Viceno and the S.T.I.N.A. Park with the sulphur springs.
In the ancient papal palaces next to the Duomo there are sculptures, paintings and sacred furnishings from the ancient Fabbrica del Duomo.

The Mother Church, whose foundation is of uncertain epoch, has on the Gothic portal of the south side, with double columns and with two ramps staircase, the inscription of 1539; on the same wall remain part of the facade of the ancient jury house and four arms in stone flag bearer. The main façade is late Baroque; inside paintings by Filippo Paladino (Martirio di San Lorenzo, Madonna della Mercede), a copy of the Last Supper by Leonardo di G. Emanuele Passanisi, the vault of Bonajuto (1786) and a triptych fourteenth century.

Municipality of the Nausicaa Riviera on the Gulf of Squillace, between sea, hills and mountains, with clear waters and beaches as intact as the stretch of granite sand between Fosso Cupid and Alaca stream; in the village the Palazzo Scoppa, ancient Carthusian crab, and the Museum of Memory.

The parish church of the patron, which unites Romanesque, Gothic and Renaissance: inscriptions on the entrance pillars recall an extension of 1347, the façade and the Gothic-Venetian marble portal are by Jacopo Corti di Valsolda (1460) and the bezel of the portal is frescoed by Bernardino Luini with the Madonna with the Child and St. Maurizio. On the south side there is a large Saint Christopher, a sundial and the coat of arms of the Quadrius; Romanesque-Lombard bell tower of the fourteenth century. Inside, three aisles frescoed and never touched by the Baroque, the bronze ciborium of the Guicciardi brothers (1578) and a golden wooden ancone of the late fifteenth century attributed to Giacomo Del Maino.
The opera house.
Nero's classic canyon, for those who practice canyoning.

From the piazza Celestino Lupi climb to amphitheatre stairs, alleys and squares on the eastern side of the mountain, among the "suppurtu" arches on which lay stone houses and beams, and portals carved with coats of arms of animals, flowers and faces. The Porticella, the old nineteenth-century Town Hall, the bell tower of St. John the Baptist became a civic tower with clock in 1887, the sixteenth-century Palazzo della Cancelleria with two-folded windows and stone architraves and, at the top of the village, the chapel of the Madonna Addolorata (1575) annexed to Palazzo Lupi; the circular defensive towers are incorporated into the houses.
Incoherent times on the MiC card (table closed, text with summer and winter times); check before visiting
An unusual harvest of traps and poaching.

Village on the Marena river, one of the most beautiful villages in Italy, home to the painter Giovan Battista Salvi, known as the Sassoferrato: the Rocca di Albornoz in 1365, the Palazzo dei Priori with the Archaeological Museum, the remains of the Roman Sentinum and the Romanesque Abbey of Santa Croce dei Conti.
Summer evenings in the park.
Small museum of concretions by Luigi Fantini, in Tazzola.
The basilica on the hill of Poggibonsi, signalled by Visit Tuscany among the ancient testimonies of the city.
Listen to the griko among the monuments.
A Jacopo Bassano in a hamlet church.

Ancient romoratory (foundation indicated in 1243) along the mule track for Campolieto, already the Grancia of the Scalzi Carmelites, then the Doctrinal Fathers until the suppression of 1809 and the Conventuals since 1840; it preserves paintings by the Neapolitan Giuseppe Castellano (1707) and epigraphs recalling Cardinal Orsini.
The stars from an uninhabited village.

The castle, founded by the Longobards to guard the streets for Benevento, hosted Norman, Swabian, Angevin and Aragonese rulers and until the nineteenth century the Head of the Principality Ultra with court and offices; today it is the seat of the Municipality. In the basement, on two superimposed lanes excavated in part in the rock, there is the prison: after the motions of 1848 the Bourbons locked you patriots like Carlo Poerio and Sigismondo Castromediano, from which the nickname "Spielberg of Irpinia" is. Closed in 1923, declared National Monument in 1928, it has been a civic museum since 1997; open Monday-Saturday 9-13, afternoons and Sundays by telephone reservation (0825 964003).

The historical centre of the Valdesi in Val Pellice, which takes its name from a year-old tower Mille: the Waldensian quarter along Via Beckwith with Temple, House Valdese and Museum, the church of San Martino with the Priory of Mauritius and the contemporary Art Gallery Filippo Scroppo; it is a base for hikers and mountain enthusiasts.
Of the fortifications of the castle, passed to the Sforza in 1433, remain the Torrione del Cassero and some stretches of walls, which once went beyond the town.

The ancient Piazza Maggiore became under the Trivulzio the administrative, legal and commercial center of the village; next, the Piazza del Mercato preserves the medieval function. The four-tower castle remains only traces of the foundations and the moat; between Via Verdi and Via Mazzini survives the cloister of Santa Chiara, and in Via Garibaldi the Palazzo Trivulzio (now Dansi), reworked in neoclassical forms by the Barattieri.
A church over a Greek temple.
It rises where, according to tradition, Saint Francis met the wolf.

Ancient commercial port of call, active especially in the eighteenth century, today marina with bars and restaurants; from here start the boat trips to the beaches difficult to reach and the night fishing of the Totani.
The traditional costume of Crucoli women.
Protected cliffs and paths on the sea.
The restored village with views up to the Alps.
Theatre decorated with frescoes by Arnaldo De Lisio.

Space of Ezio Pagano dedicated to contemporary art of Sicilian artists; open 17-20.30, closed on Mondays and on holidays, groups and schools also in the morning by reservation.
