Benedictine monastery founded in the middle of the eighth century by the sons of the Longobard Duke Peter, who in 762 received the donation of the nobles Herphus, Mark and Anto; almost destroyed by the Hungarians, it was rebuilt by the abbot Adalberto II in the appearance of a castle. The three-nave church has the vestibule with Inferno, Paradiso and San Michele (about 1450, attributed to Antonio da Firenze) and the presbytery frescoed in 1324-1336 by artists close to the Padua lesson of Giotto; in the crypt the urn of Sant'Anastasia (VIII century), an Annunciation in marble of the late thirteenth century and a fifteenth-century Vesperbild, in the atrium the lapidary with Roman and high-medieval finds. Monday-Saturday 9-12 and 15-18, Sunday 11.30-12 and 15-18; not visitable during functions.

The church with the fourteenth-century statue of the saint, the tomb of Galeotto Malaspina (1367) and the organ Serassi; next to the oratory with the seventeenth-century crucifix of the "Christ in agony."

Ring of 11.4 km (about 3 hours and 40, 480 m of difference in altitude, suitable for families, recommended in spring and autumn) between woods and terraces, with panoramic view of the lower lake from Comnago and the beech trees of Monte alle Croci; arrives at the Old Church of Santa Maria sopra Belgirate and returns to the station by skirting villas and historical gardens.

The Euganean thermal mud, in one of the oldest spas in Europe.

Founded in 1989 by volunteers in the tower of the former Villa Briolini, where the Briolini silkiers took over the main part of the sharecropping: it tells the first half of the twentieth century on average and low Val Seriana, from the chain of wheat to the rebuilt peasant house, to the cellar and the shops of shoemaker, slut, carpenter, turner, blacksmith and watchmaker. Open on Sunday 15.30-18.30.
The Christ in the column.
One of the most spectacular caves in Sardinia.
The civic museum of Santa Rita.
Franciscan and Venetian art in one of the first churches of the Order in Friuli.

Over 70,000 m2 owned by the Fondazione Senza Frontiere, born in 1973 from the plantations of Anselmo Castelli and designed by Gianfranco Paghera imitating nature: forest of native species of the Po Valley, wetland with fauna, orchard of ancient varieties, rose garden and medicinal garden, with educational trail. The Ethnographic Museum documents the Kanaka del Sepik (Papua New Guinea) and the Krahô del Tocantins (Amazon Brazilian) with masks, musical instruments and tools. Open from April to October, visits by reservation.
Morandi's work.
They're from above, in a gerla.
The nineteenth-century Cuneo.
The fresco once believed by Masaccio.

Built between 1790 and 1825 in place of three churches dedicated to the same saint, a Greek cross with neoclassical facade. Inside 42 marble tombstones with bas-relief of the late sixteenth century, baroque altars of 1764 and paintings of Gennaro Maldarelli (1838-41); the crypt preserves nineteenth-century burials, silver and urns.
Architecture of the 19th century port.
Picnic by the lake.
The cathedral of marble.
A small baroque treasure chest of sacred art.

The oratory on the moat.
A church on a Roman house.
18th-century paintings in the parish.
Jerusalem in miniature on the Pollino.
Romanesque and fifteenth century frescoes on the ascent to the castle.
The Carthusian monastery of the Certosa degli Angeli was active from 1326 to 1782; guided tours in Italian and German lead to the cloisters and rooms.
Tables of the fourteenth century and the Flemish triptych.
The Oratory of Disciplinants.

The village stands on a spur and was surrounded by an angioin age by walls with towers; from the castle the look ranges over the Camastra Valley and the mountains of Volturino and Caperrino, and the streets retain patriotic names linked to the insurrectional march of 1860 towards Potenza.
Tower of thirteenth century plant that dominates the village from the top of a hill, in the Rione Maggiore.

Opened in September 2007 in the rock, the fortified core first closed to the public, tells the story from the 10th century to today with multimedia installations by Studio Azzurro. The route touches the corticella, the clock tower with bell and sixteenth-century clock, the south-east tower with the comparison between the current and late-middle-valeval landscape, the guard body and the excavations of San Bartolomeo: ceramics from the late Middle Ages to the nineteenth century and funerary furnishings with rosaries, buttons, buckles and rings.
A small village near Jolanda di Savoia with large street art murals dedicated to cinema shot in Ferrara.

The highest tower in the city, 84 meters, began in 1172 on the Roman forum: the bells Rengo and Marangona from 1295, the octagonal cell of the fifteenth century and the clock of 1795; you climb on foot by 368 steps or by elevator.
One of the best examples of late fifteenth century fortress.

The peak of 3538 m, in the Middle Ages considered the highest of the Alps and visible from the Via Francigena; the first documented ascent is of 1 September 1358, when Bonifacio Rotario d'Asti brought to the top a bronze triptych today in the cathedral of Susa. At the top is the shrine of Our Lady of the Rock, the highest shrine in Europe, and the 3 meters high bronze statue of Our Lady, inaugurated on August 28, 1899, paid by 130,000 children and brought to the top in eight pieces by the Alpine battalion From Urbiano to the Rifugio La Riposa (2205 m), then on foot to the Rifugio Ca' d'Asti (2856 m): about 4 hours and 30, recommended in summer.

The eighteenth century, one of the largest in the region, designed by Andrea Vici, a student of Vanvitelli; it preserves a Pagani bezel, a table by Giacomo da Recanati and a marble bust by Pope Sixtus V, of which a copy is at Victoria and Albert Museum in London.

Renaissance Basilica of the sixteenth century by Galeazzo Alessi, in the plain, built to guard the Porziuncola, the chapel where Francis founded the order and where he died; the façade was rebuilt in the nineteenth century after an earthquake.

16th century castle of the Marches Beccadelli Bologna: a stone at the entrance of the noble floor indicates 1559 as a year of construction; acquired by the Sicilian Region, it houses the museum with the finds of Makella, the ancient indigenous city of Montagnola, and settlements along the Eleuterio, linking the Tyrrhenian coast and the interior. Among the pieces on display are a fourth century B.C. syceliot crater, a bowl and an archaic tomb kit, Greek jugs and amphorae, Roman finds, Arab-Norman basins and medieval glazed lamps. From the tower you can see the gorges of the Strait dug by Eleuterio. Open every day 9-19.30 (ticket office up to one hour before), Sunday and holidays 9-14.

Built in the early nineteenth century, it retains its original simplicity; on the high altar the statue of Our Lady of about 1955, restored by artisans of Barcelona, in the niche built in 1958. Free admission during the celebrations.
A water stop on the Via dei Masi.
Venue of the town hall from the eighteenth century to 1913; late-Gothic frescoes emerged in the restorations of the eighties.
The large Palazzo dei Farnese that brings together National Gallery (Correggio, Parmigianino, Leonardo), Archaeological Museum, Biblioteca Palatina and Museo Bodoni in a single itinerary.

The coast of Torvaianica is indicated as the place of the landing of Enea, near a lagoon crossed by the Numico (now Fosso di Pratica di Mare); the coastal dunes are protected area and in Via Seville remain the remains of a Roman villa.
The artifacts of Monte Adranone in the heart of the village.
Outside the walls the sanctuary attributed to Vasari and the remains of a Medici castle; a little further, among the woods, the fourteenth-century fortified village of Gargonza.
damaged by the earthquake of 2016 (Italy.it)
Small village entirely in stone, among the best preserved medieval centers of the area, with squares, courtyards, alleys, numerous covered passages and tower houses.

In the castle: daunie and magnagreche ceramics, Greek and Etruscan bronzes and jewels in gold, amber and silver (VI-III century BC), medieval glass with Islamic inscriptions and Doria rooms; in the Clock Tower the Sarcophagus of Rapolla, Roman marble of the II century A.D. carved in Asia Minor.

The fish market is held from Tuesday to Sunday in the morning, with fish brought directly by fishermen returning from the sea; at the port are moored the bragozzi, the typical boats with bright colors.

At the top of the medieval village of Scipione, 260 meters: built in the 11th century by Adalberto Pallavicino, transformed in the mid-15th century into a noble palace with cylindrical tower; extinct the Pallavicino di Scipione in 1776, passed to the Fogliani. Private but open to visitors.

At the foot of the Partenio, the municipality of the sanctuary of Montevergine, founded in 1126 by St. William of Vercelli, and the eighteenth-century Abbey Palace of Loreto which houses the library of monks.
A monumental holm oak in the woods.
The octagonal chapel frescoed by Giulio Urbanis inside an eighteenth-century church.
Courtesy frescoes and the most beautiful view of Alto Garda.
Polychrome marbles.
Octagonal building on two floors isolated on a hill, attributed to Frederick II (1220-1250), once connected to the castle by a tunnel; a spiral staircase rises to the top with views up to Etna.

In the municipal palace, it collects the ancient drawings belonging to Count Alessandro Maggiori, of the family Majori Colonna, including sheets attributed to Raffaello, Giorgio Vasari, Cavalier d'Arpino, Guercino, Domenichino and Giovanni Battista Salvi.

The village, built towards the end of the 10th century against the Saracen incursions, preserves cylindrical towers of the fourteenth century, Piazza Colonna and alleys; the Baronale Palace, residence of the Colonna (which held Neptune from 1426 to 1594), has the clock tower with the coat of arms and the inscription of the works of Marcantonio Colonna of 1569. The Cavone is the ancient walk along the walls with a view of the port.

Opened in 1997, the first museum of its kind in Italy, was born from the collection donated to the village by Giovanni Bergallo, the last watchmaker of the family who built tower clocks in the workshop house of Val Maremola between 1861 and 1980. In 260 square meters of an old town hall exhibits about thirty authentic tower clocks (the oldest of the 16th century), machinery and tools, dials, hands, pulleys and objects from bell towers, documents and a video; the visit may include the Bergallo workshop house. For the twenty-year anniversary, the documentary "Time Beyond the Ocean" was shot on the clock sold in 1934 to the Salesian mission of Puerto Santa Cruz in Patagonia. Open Friday, Saturday and Sunday: October-May 15-18, June-August 17-21, September 16-20; schools €3, free for residents; guided tour of about 45 minutes.
Where his ashes rest.
Unpublished times: the MiC card indicates closed every day, opening entrusted to the Barbarano culture association (tel. 0761 414531)
The huge piazza porticata, lounge of the city and meeting point between the medieval Cuneo and the nineteenth century, with the statue of Barbaroux and the market on Tuesday.

The municipality of the Alpone Valley, in the eastern Lessinia, of which Bolca is part, indicated as the richest fossil deposit in the world with more than 250 animal and vegetable species: the Museum of Fossil and Pesciara, with the galleries dug in the limestones, form with the Monte Postale a paleontological park. Around, paths on the extinct volcano of Monte Purga and on the crosses of the pastor Celestino Baldo.

Red brick village enclosed by a wall of 780 meters; Porta San Francesco is the main entrance and the only remaining of the three doors. In the centre of Piazza della Rovere, Palazzo Giorgi Pierfranceschi, Palazzo dei Malatesta and the fourteenth-century Palazzo della Comunanza.

The town is surrounded by Renaissance walls adorned with small loggias and polygonal towers; inside the walls are the parish church of San Pietro, in the homonymous square, and the Town Hall. Around, gentle hills covered with vineyards and olive groves and small river valleys.
Built in 1736 where the convent of Sister Virginia De Leyva, Monza's Nun, stood.
An ancient fortified residence overlooking the central square, next to the Cathedral; today it houses the seat of the Municipality.
Mollino's theater.
The story of the tombolo lace officiate.

Trail 311 from the middle school in Via Diaz: it passes through the chapel of the Santel de Pusole, Domaro (804 m, protected fossiliferous site) and Coca (875 m) to the small church of Santa Maria del Giogo, an ancient hospice for travelers and pilgrims overlooking Lake Iseo. About two hours.
The mud volcanoes of the Apennines.
To see the second river of Italy born.

A wall of vertical basaltic prisms twenty meters high, placed like organ reeds, on Mount Cèpera (Cuccureddu 'e Zéppara), a small volcanic cone of 167 meters: they were formed about three million years ago by the slow cooling of the lava. The hill was raised from the nineteenth century; closed the quarry, it is today a natural monument, with a tour of the village. In Italy similar formations are found only in Veneto and Sicily.
A noble residence intact with its park.

Born in 1836 from the donation of the collections of Giovanni Battista Filippa (1778-1838), a soldier of Napoleonic troops in the Spanish countryside, is indicated as the first museum of civic ownership established in Piedmont. Filippa called it the "cabinet of curiosity and rare things": in a building of 1415 it conserves minerals, shells, stuffed animals, books, coins, utensils and parchments, enriched then by the painter Maurizio Antonini, the parish priest Gaudenzio Cusa and donations of inhabitants and emigrants. Visits by reservation (tel. 0163 55203).
The village rises on the top of a hill from which you can enjoy a wide view.
A late Baroque altar in Lecce stone.

Ethno-anthropological museum in the garden and cellar of the former convent of Santa Maria del Pozzo, run by an association and recognized museum of regional interest: over 3,000 objects of rural life before mechanization and about 3,000 photographs, in 20 sectors (transport with soma animals, wine room, crafts, peasant food, etnomusicology), plus a nativity scene with figures in eighteenth-century clothes, stables with animals and educational garden. It is educational farm with laboratories (bread, cheese, beekeeping).
On foot to Tusculum.
Walking in the port of Traiano.
The zero mile of Reggio.
The peasant life of the Dauni Mountains inside the tower.
Vineyards, lake and trails around the village.
The Neanderthal of the Po and the great fauna of the glacial era of the plain.
Ancient Christianity of Canosa.

Church of medieval origin next to the castle, extended several times over the centuries, which preserves frescoes in part of itinerant painters and in part of the Monregalese Segurano Cigna (XV century), as well as remains of older paintings, among the oldest in the valley. It is part of the tour with audioguides of the village.
The golden pulpit and the organ of the cramârs.
The source Dante mentioned.
Tell how you lived in farms.

Ring that starts after the monumental cemetery following the signs for the Chapel of the Alps: climb to the Forcella, with views of Sarnico and the Basso Sebino, then to the Colle Cambline and among chestnuts, birch and agrifogli to the top of the Bronzone (1.334 m), with panoramic view of the lake, Monte Isola, Orobie and Pianura Padana; return from Mount Gombo, site of prehistoric finds.
The symbol of Castel del Monte.
Picnic and relaxation at altitude.

Rural village surrounded by farmhouses and agricultural land, largely owned by a single family that has preserved its original architectural aspect; it has been reported several times in the census of the Places of the Heart of the FAI (2014-2022).
An authentic corner of sea life.
The galleries of the sparkling wine.
The shoes and the ability to make Val Colvera.
An entire ancient city, port between the West and the East.

A Romanesque crypt hidden under the presbytery.

City-museum between antiquity and contemporary art: the Arch of Trajan and the Roman theatre of the second century, the Lombard church of Santa Sofia UNESCO heritage with the cloister of the Museum of Sannio, the Rectors' Rock and the Hortus Conclusus of Mimmo Paladino.
The green lung of Rome.

The original village is close to the hill of the castle: the most picturesque pedestrian route starts from Porta Mamurra and rises through Vico Giudea, the ancient Jewish quarter where a synagogue stood. In the historic center is the birthplace of Fra' Diavolo; in March the squares are lit with the fires of St. Joseph and the burning of the
Oaks and views of the plateau.
The cathedral museum, reported by Visit Tuscany among the city's museums.
Get down into the basement of a large amphitheater.
The contemporary in Piacenza.

Byzantine castle built presumably in the 10th century, dominates the valley of the river Simeri and the Gulf of Squillace. It preserves almost intact the outer walls, an imposing cylindrical tower and much of the citadel, including the Palacium Castri, seat of power. Several times reported in the FAI census "The Places of the Heart" (from 2012 to 2022).
Church of the historic center with portal of 1477.
The stone village of the Park.

Locride Municipality in the Aspromonte National Park, known for MuSaBa, the open-air museum park created since 1969 by Nik Spatari and Hiske Maas in the ancient monastic complex of Santa Barbara; on the plateau of Limina stands the Sanctuary of San Nicodemo, linked to the patron saint of the village.

Small village of Montefeltro inside the Park of Sasso Simone and Simoncello, with roads, walls and towers built with stones of the river Mutino, works of Franco Assetto, the mill of Ponte Vecchio and the monastery of Montefiorentino with the Cappella Oliva.
€12 guided tour, €10 audioguide; reduced €11/€9; €8 with 7-18 year old guide and over 65; free up to 6 years old
Deep gorge excavated by the Carmignano stream, crossed by a medieval aqueduct; just above the monastery of Sant'Ambrogio with the fourteenth-century hermitage, underground caves and frescoes.
The textile tradition of the Lanzese People's Art.
The municipal theatre inaugurated on July 24, 1870 with the opera I Promessi Sposi by Enrico Petrella.
The lake between beech and fir under the Crispo Serra.
Neoclassical frescoes and a sixteenth-century table.
A bathroom just a stone's throw from the square.
Fossils and fauna of the Oltrepò, including plesiosaur.
A large nineteenth-century processional case.

Wanted by the host Georg Paprion after the pilgrimages to the Holy Land: in 1633 the round chapel on the model of the Chapel of the Graces of Altötting, then the aisle of the Passion and in 1653 the chapel of the Holy Sepulchre, a copy of that of Jerusalem, a polygonal roundabout with dome where the light falls from above. The statues come from the workshop of the local sculptor Matthias Schranzhofer and are among the most important works of local folk art. It is part of the MIK route.
An eighteenth century forge still moved by water.
Medieval civic power.
The historic tractors of a factory in Dolonese.
Romanesque traces under the nineteenth century reconstruction.

Norman fortified church of the 11th century, probably of 1068, erected after the victory over the Arabs at Misilmeri and flanked by a Basilian monastery; it is among the first Arab-Norman buildings of the island. Today in ruins, it has a single nave, three apses and crypt, on a hill of about 56 meters near the Tyrrhenian Sea; in 2016 under the church were found about thirty burials and coins, still in the studio.
The symbol tower above the roofs.
The most scenic stretch of coastline.

Franciscan monastery founded in 1248, one of the largest in the Marche region. The Chapel of Counts Oliva, with inscription of 1484 and probably designed by Simone Ferrucci, houses the tombs of Gianfrancesco Oliva and Marsibilia Trinci by Francesco di Simone Ferrucci, the altarpiece with Madonna and Child and saints by Giovanni Santi, father of Raffaello (1489), and the kneelings inlaid by Zocchini (1493).
A Napoleonic mill that still grinds.
The living room of the village and the stone alleys.
Entrance with ramp from via de' Pignatari
Painted drawers and a frescoed cloister.
The colored arches with mirror walls by Daniel Buren and the Palazzo delle Poste Rationalista, with futurist mosaics in the tower.
Nineteenth-century theatre with 99 seats with frescoed ceiling and gilded stucco, main seat of the prose season, concerts and cultural events.
The "green pearl" of the Adriatic Sea, with the promenade and Ceccarini Avenue.

The city of paper, in the Anconetian hinterland, UNESCO Creative City since 2013 for crafts: the Museum of Paper and Filigree in the former Dominican convent, Piazza del Comune with the Fontana Sturinalto and the Pinacoteca Molajoli.
Our Lady of the Brunettes.

A country of southern Ogliastra crossed by the river Quirra, with about 12 km of coast between Foxi Manna and Foxi Murdegu, the tower of San Giovanni di Sarrala, almost 80 nuraghi including the Aleri and the museum dedicated to the sculptor Albino Manca.
He tells the University Bologna of the Middle Ages better than any book.
The history of the cockpits, from the Falisci to the twentieth century.

The square of Sant'Onofrio in Marina Corta and via Crispi in Marina Lunga collect bars and restaurants, and from May to October the evening life of the island; via Vittorio Emanuele is the main street of the capital.
Walk suspended over the Pioverna gorge.

The largest lake entirely in the province of Trento, about 5 km long just under 450 meters, with waters awarded by the Blue Flag and bathing from May to September. In Calceranica the lakefront, one of the best stretches to walk near the water, connects beaches, meadows and piers to the train station, with kiosks, bars and accesses to the shore, also suitable for strollers; from the piers you come out by sailing boat, rowing, canoeing or dragon boating.
Waterbirds and woods along the Sagittarius.
Floor pedestrian area
About 3 km from the city, beyond the pine forest of the reserve: about 3 km of sandy beaches, the fishing village, the marina and the bay where dolphins and sea turtles are often seen.

Church designed by the architect Mattia Capponi: it preserves a bust of San Sebastiano in polychrome terracotta of the sixteenth century attributed to Mattia della Robbia, a Crucifixion on canvas by Claudio Ridolfi and a golden wooden statue of St. Joseph. It once hosted a polyptych by Lorenzo Lotto, whose surviving panels are now in the State Museums of Berlin.
About 40 hectares of English designed by Piermarini, with small lake and temple, cave, statue of Neptune, Polyphemus Antros and ultra-secular trees.
A baroque villa with camellias garden, today a town house open to all.

Built in the most inhabited nucleus when the church of San Zeno needed restoration, it was established parish in 1597, enlarged in 1681, renovated and frescoed in 1921-1922 and completely restored in 1975.
The flowers of the "Giardino d'Italia" in one garden.

Country of the Treviso plain along the Muson, whose name recalls a Roman fortress and then barbaric destroyed in 1229: Villa Priuli, seventeenth century and frescoed by Paolo Piazza, with the archaeological civic museum, the church of San Pietro and the nature path of the Prai.

At the end of via Giudea, the convent was inaugurated on September 21, 1589. On the main altar there is a seventeenth-century canvas with the Adoration of the Magi by Filippo Paladini; in the sacristy there is a wooden tabernacle of the seventeenth century and a library with about 7,000 ancient works.

On the slopes of the Barro the excavations have brought to light a large residential and military settlement of Gothic age (V-VI century AD), indicated as the largest site of that era in Italy; the area is owned by the Park at the Hermitage, which in the twentieth century was sanatorium.

The ancient village preserves intact four medieval doors and three concentric rings of walls largely visible. There are the fifteenth-century Palazzo Bernabò, two-storey with central loggia on the roof, and the church of San Nicola, with altarpieces attributed to Ghezzi and Masucci.
3-4 h walk round-trip
The treasures of Mount Saraceno.
The ruins at the top of the village, overlooking the Pollino.

Private non-profit museum dedicated to poet and historian In the Cassata: 45 ancient artisan workshops rebuilt with about 20,000 vintage artefacts, catalogued and bound by the Superintendence of Messina, a garden of rare Sicilian and Mediterranean plants and a restoration workshop.

The heart of the city, once Piazza della Fontana, rises on the source where according to tradition the goddess Diana drank and bathed; the current structure is from the late nineteenth-early twentieth century, with the Town Hall of 1887, Palazzo Iacono (1894) and Palazzo Criscione (1931-1932) of engineer Santoro Cecolo. The oldest building is Palazzo Iacono-Ciarcia, with the late Baroque loggia almost certainly by Rosario Gagliardi (1735-1740); a few meters, at the entrance of Via Calogero, the remains of a Roman thermal complex enlarged in the Byzantine age.
A medieval hermitage on the heights of the Nero.

Presented as the first museum in Italy dedicated to tin boxes, it collects over a thousand Italian boxes produced between 1890 and 1950, collected by Marina Durand de la Penne and ordered by themes, from the Sabaude wedding to the colonial countryside to the boom; between the Talmone and Venchi-Unica boxes pieces and a 1929 packaging signed by Gabriele d'Annunzio. Free visit by reservation; Visit Lazio times: Friday 10-13, Saturday and Sunday 10-13 and 15-19.
The funeral monument of the poet in the heart of the village.
The one span bridge.

Built between 1855 and 1866, after the proclamation of the dogma of the Immaculate, on a project by engineer Gregorio Micillo, in place of the oldest church of the Immaculate and the Angel; in 1919 it was added to the Vatican Basilica. It has a large nave with four chapels on each side, frescoed and decorated with stucco by Cozzolino and Serino, altar in polychrome marble and wooden choir; the two-order façade has portal between Doric columns and triangular tympanum.
Wood of holm oaks, conifers and Mediterranean maquis crossed by a road and hiking trails, with Sardinian deer and deer; you can see the royal eagle and the pilgrim falcon.
15th-century castle founded by Ladislao di Napoli, with the church next to it being built in a polygonal tower.
Walk and ride on the edge of the Oglio.
The village of the thousand steps with the sunset on the Lario.
The most recent excavation of a Daunia and Roman city of the Capitanatata.
Franciscan complex of the fifteenth century isolated on a hill, with works by Pier Francesco Sacchi and Bernardo Strozzi and the former refectory with paintings by Gian Battista Casoni.
A little stone mystery.
On the slope of Mount Virgo, the medieval village that was the original center of Caserta, narrow around the cathedral, with the noble houses Pisano and Ferraiuolo along the uphill alleys.

The town of Val Pellice whose history is linked to the Waldenses, present since the 13th century and free to profess their worship only from 1848; to see the ancient village of Luserna with the Loggia dei Mercanti and the Palazzo dei Conti, the Waldensian Temple of San Giovanni, the Museum of the game and the toy and the astronomical Observatory of Val Pellice.
Roman Venusia in the basement of the castle.
Indoor paleontological collection, at the Sanctuary of the Immaculate Heart of Mary, with fossils especially of the Marche Apennines of different geological epochs.
The oldest monument in the center.

Façade in a hut facing west, marked by three-part pilgrims, with portal under a canopy and bell tower in square-based brick crowned by a dome on a drum. The interior with three naves on pillars preserves the main altar of 1823, a sixteenth-century marble tabernacle of Carrara and a fresco of San Carlo Borromeo. The patron saint's feast is celebrated on September 8.
A small church between Romanesque and Gothic.
The frescoed crypt of a millennial abbey.
A early Christian church inside the spas of Caracalla.

From the parish church of San Martino you can reach the church of San Paolo with the annexed convent, one of the churches listed by the municipality. From here you can enjoy a wide view of the Valganna, Valmarcarcolo, the valleys and the mountains of the Canton of Ticino and Lake Ceresio.
Walk in the ancient village.
One of the best preserved castles in the region.

The capital of the Vanoi valley, with streets in porphyry and many hamlets under the peaks of the Cauriòl and the Totoga: the Ecomuseum of Vanoi brings together the exhibition on the Great War on the Lagorai and the Ethnographic Path of Caoria, the Venetian sawmill of Valzanca and the mills of Ronco; from Zortea, Prade and Gobbera you go up to the lake of Calaita, in the Park of Paneveggio.

Cesare Pavese's birthplace (1908), on the Belbo torrent at the border between the provinces of Cuneo and Asti, in the heart of the Moscato area and setting of the moon and the bonfires; to see the Museum of the Fondazione Cesare Pavese, the birthplace, the shop-house of Nuto, the medieval tower and the literary benches.
The sacred heart of the Greek city.
Narrow and deep gorge excavated by the stream; the suspended footbridge looks at Mont Blanc, the basin and the valley of La Thuile.
The port of Vulci.
Municipality of chapels and village ovens, gate of the Mont Avic Regional Park among pine forests, peat bogs and lakes.
The shrine of the Siculi, before the Greeks.

At Porta Catania, in the ancient Jewish district, 14th century Gothic palace that blends Arab and Norman elements, residence of the De Spuches, family of Spanish origin; has a garden, hosts cultural events and the Foundation Mazzullo with works by sculptor Giuseppe Mazzullo.
The highest hill above Città Alta, reachable by the second funicular.

Church in the open countryside, about 2 km from the center, rebuilt in 1460-1461 by vote of Bianca Maria Visconti and Blessed Amedeo Mendes da Silva; it is one of the first central churches of the Lombard Renaissance, with polygonal choir added in 1505. Inside a vast cycle of frescoes from the late fifteenth century with stories of the life and Passion of Christ, culminating in a great Crucifixion.
Alpine and polar flora a stone's throw from the village.

Walking path of medium-low difficulty, with about 400 steps and about an hour of walk, which from the Collegiate Church of Santa Maria a Mare crosses the lemon gardens (including the Sfusato Amalfitano, IGP Lemon Coast of Amalfi) and the spontaneous vegetation, touches the village of Torre with the church of San Michele and goes down to Minori, with views of the promontory between the two villages.
The old town with its old shops and historic buildings.
The Franciscan monastery of the country.

Since 1766 Gerolamo Buniva transformed and enlarged the small church already existing before 1609: three aisles separated by binated columns with Corinthian capitals, a dome similar to those of Guarini in San Lorenzo in Turin and Vittone al Vallinotto, a brick facade with sinuous profiles.
The mountain life told by everyday tools.

Opened in 2005 in the seventeenth-century Palazzo Marinoni Barca with frescoed ceilings: paintings, drawings, sculptures and bas-reliefs from legacies of families included, the Suardo collection with works from the sixteenth to the twentieth century (including Giovan Paolo Cavagna and Palma il Giovane), two sculptures by Giacomo Manzù and the Gorla collection of mechanisms of tower clocks. In the garden three giant sequoias of about 30 meters brought from America at the end of the nineteenth century. Open Friday 15.30-18.30, Saturday and Sunday 10-12 and 15.30-18.30.

To the south of Milan, Binasco preserves the Castello Visconteo of the fourteenth century, today seat of the Municipality, where Beatrice of Tenda was beheaded; in the village the eighteenth-century church of Saints John Baptist and Stefano and MUMAC, museum of coffee machines of the Cimbali Group.
The restored castle in the Carpina valley.

Baroque church with a nave built in 1767 on a project by Lazaro Giosafatti, with paintings by Filippo Ricci. It preserves a Pietà in polychrome terracotta and an Eternal Father in marble of the fifteenth century, the reliquary of San Fortunato, an organ of the seventeenth century and wooden busts; the sacristy has marble furniture and a frescoed ceiling with stories of Saint Benedict.
The village as an open-air gallery.
The symbol square of the city.

Remains of ancient stone walls in the towns Civitella (or Civitello) and Castellone, considered testimony of the Osca and Sannite origins of the village, perhaps the ancient Fresilia. The first official news of Frosolone dates back to the 11th century, when it was part of the County of Isernia.
One of the most amazing museums in Tuscany.

Part of a complex that was a hospital of the community until the early sixteenth century and around 1528 became a monastery of Augustinian nuns; a small late Baroque church, renovated in the second half of the seventeenth century, with stuccoes, two canvases and the fresco of the ceiling of the Florentine Antonio Puglieschi, high altar of 1685 and a Madonna with Child attributed to the Master of the Nativity of Castello (about 1460).

Palace of the Napoleonic era, now seat of the Town Hall, indicated as one of the most beautiful of the Upper Lake: it preserves the Golden Hall, the Chapel of the Immaculate and an ancient library with shelves in walnut.

The Regional Museum of Natural History, with naturalistic collections and a permanent exhibition dedicated to the Sicilian cart, is located in Palazzo d'Aumale, on the promenade next to Praiola beach. Free entrance to the ground floor; open from Tuesday to Friday 9-19, Saturday and Sunday 9-13, closed on Monday.
A curiosity for those who love vintage appliances.
One of the churches not to be missed in the city, reachable through Porta Castello.
The ancient entrance to Bormio dal Gavia.
Masi with wooden roofs and autumn larch trees.
The work of the vineyard on the hill, tool for tool.

Already a baptismal font in the 15th century, it was rebuilt at the end of the 16th century with brick and rosette façade. He preserves the Crucifixion with Saints Francis, Mark and Sigismondo by Francesco Vanni, a seventeenth-century painting with Our Lady who gives the scapular to Saint Simone Stock and, on the two altars of the nave, the Madonna delle Grazie by Daniele Lonati and a Trinity with angels from the Nasinian school.

Historical-naturalistic path that starts from the village and touches the ancient silver quarries: the first information of extraction dates back to the twelfth century, when Henry VI sent Peter of Livonia to oversee the works; in 1506 the mines passed to Galeazzo Caracciolo, in 1566 they returned to the Royal Court and were exploited until 1783. Panels illustrate the extraction and processing of silver galena.
The stone city of Gallura.
A green oasis among the temples.
A small church on the water dedicated to the fishermen of the lake.

A noble residence with original furnishings and collections on the aristocratic life between the Seven and the Nineteenth Century, from 1836 residence in exile of Charles X of Bourbon; in the park trees from all over the world.
Clear water and white sand, deep waters rich in fish suitable for snorkeling and diving.
The view from the fortress.

Borgo della Valle Stura already known in Roman times as a passage to the Gallia, birthplace of Lalla Romano: in the porticoed center you can visit the Palazzo Borelli with its terrace park, the parish church of San Donato and the medieval civic tower, while above the village the ruins of the Fort of the Consolata; between June and July the meadows at the entrance of the village are colored with lavender.

The fourteenth century, rebuilt in the eighteenth century; it houses a triptych by Niccolò di Liberatore called the pupil with the Madonna enthroned with the Child between St. Francis and St. Matthew, as well as paintings from the eighteenth century.
The Renaissance customs of the Contesa.
One of Europe's biggest bosses.
Archaeological area with museum in the medieval wall tower called Donota tower, behind the Roman theatre.

It preserves the cycle of frescoes of 1483-1486 by Pasoto Da Cemmo and his son Giovanni Pietro, between Gothic international and Renaissance, rare testimony of the Lombard painting of the time: all twelve Sibyls and the history of Lamech appear there. Traditionally, the presbytery is based on a Roman temple.
The terrace on the emptiness.

In the former elementary school, it is a path on landscapes, environments and work between the late nineteenth and early twentieth centuries; the main sections are dedicated to Giovannino Guareschi, with videos, and to the cooperative experience of Faraboli. Restaurant and bookshop; recommended for families with children.
The Neolithic doline.

Inaugurated in 1923 thanks to Don Romolo Putelli, it occupies two floors of the fifteenth-century Palazzo Federici (Palazzo della Cultura) with ten rooms and a loggia: it is the only art gallery of Valcamonica, with works by Giacomo Ceruti called the Pytocchetto, Romanino, Callisto Piazza and Franca Ghitti, carvings by the Fantons, coats of arms, furniture and artefacts from Prehistory to Roman times. Open Tuesday, Thursday and Saturday 9-12 and 15-18, Wednesday and Friday 9-12, Sunday 15-18.
Venue of the Municipality of Terni, rebuilt in the late nineteenth century in Renaissance style.
Dunes and pinewoods on the Costa Verde.
The frescoed halls of the town hall.
The shop of the friend who inspired Nuto.
The Sicilian Parliament building along the Corso.
The Cathedral of Irpinia.
A signposted route of the Regional Park of the Euganean Hills with wide views and rich hill vegetation.

Severo sixteenth-century palace wanted by Giulio della Rovere at the entrance to the old castle, home of the civic museums. On the noble floor, perhaps in the ancient dance hall of the Della Rovere, the theatre dedicated to the local tenor Mario Tiberini: completed around 1820 as the Triomphe Theatre, rebuilt in masonry after a fire of 1880, inaugurated with the current name in 1882 and reopened after the restoration in 1983.
Walk along the Po outside the city.
A stop on the way to San Vicino.
Location of the museum with the findings of Augusta Bagiennorum.
Red porphyry at sunset.

The village of western Irpinia on the valleys of the Miscano and Cervaro, Casalbore symbolizes the Norman Tower with the castle that encircles it, and preserves the italic temple of the third century BC, the only testimony of the Sannitico sacred building found in Irpinia.

The square, dedicated to 19 March 1944, opens in front of Palazzo Caetani and the Collegiata and is the object of an Italian garden project that recovers the pre-war structure while preserving the monumental trees. At the center is the fountain of Ernesto Biondi, built between 1885 and 1890, depicting the goddess Feronia who defeats a demonic figure, symbol of the victory of the reclamation on the swamp and malaria.

The village is 55 km from Rome, on a hill of the Nazzano Tevere-Farfa Reserve, with the Ugonesca Tower built around the Mille by Abbot Ugo I of Farfa, the triangular square with octagonal fountain and the church of Santa Maria degli Angeli; in the hamlet of Bocchignano the Buccinian Castle and, in Vezzano, the Modern Automata Museum.
The fort of the Sabauda era in the archaeological area above the village.

On the ground floor of the ducal castle, in three rooms, exhibits more than 800 state-owned finds from 50 tombs of the first and second Iron Age (late IX-VII century BC) carved on the hill of Cemetery Old, especially ceramics and personal ornaments; a 3D video reconstructs the protohistoric settlement. Open from Tuesday to Sunday, 11-13 and 17-19.
Woods, nuraghi and the waterfall in the canyon.

On one side the Palazzo della Loggia, built between 1492 and 1570 with influences of Palladio and Sansovino, seat of the Municipality; to the east the Clock Tower with the ancient astronomical clock; on the Mount of Pietà fragments of Roman tombstones.
Wind and water for windsurfing and kite on top of Lario.
Church of the 14th century rebuilt in neoclassical forms; next to the former Franciscan convent, seat of the Municipality after 1861, and the Library with ancient illuminated manuscripts.

Borgo in the Park of the Red Gorge and Frasassi, famous for the Frasassi Caves, the Valadier Temple in the gorge, the Romanesque Abbey of San Vittore delle Chiuse and the castle of Genga with its museum.
€4 (reduced €3)
The majolica dome.
A bathroom in the newly born Arno.

The only surviving public fountain of the municipality, before the fifteenth century, made of exposed bricks: a large vaulted room and a rectangular three-sector bathtub used as a water trough and washbasin. Restored at the beginning of the eighteenth century with a round arch and Doric pilasters; the municipality signals its degradation and a restoration project.
An 11th century Romanesque parish church in the open countryside.
The entrance door to the new city.
Entrance to the Square.
Where the Appian Way ended.

The village preserves the collegiate church of Santa Maria Assunta, the churches of San Giuseppe (patron), San Michele Arcangelo and dell'Annunziata, the former synagogue and the convent of San Francesco with a holm oak considered of about 500 years; from the viewpoint the view on the Pontina Plain. The signposts guide the visitor to the historic center.
Where sports climbing is at home.
Portals in Padula stone and Roman epigraphs.
Fraction developed around the cotton factory De Ferrari, with some industrial buildings of particular interest.

The largest inland marsh in Italy, about 1,800 hectares between the provinces of Pistoia and Florence, of which about 230 in nature reserve: mirrors of water between reeds, florid and carican ferns, more than 200 species of birds and the most important gauze of central-southern Italy with seven species of herons, as well as black cranes and storks. In Larciano the visitor centre of the reserve of the Padule di Fucecchio and Castelmartini, with exhibitions, guided tours of nature and history and workshops.
Irrigation channels, vineyards and Juval in one ring.
The valley and its traditions.

The village, rebuilt in late Baroque style after the earthquake of 1693 following the original plant, has more than twenty churches and noble palaces; along Via Porta della Terra overlook the palaces of the Princes of Bellaprima and Majorana of the Nicchiara, and the church of Santi Angeli Custodi has an eighteenth century majolica floor.
Necropolis preromana near Campli, testimony of the human presence before the Romans.

Village at 608 meters on the north side of Majella, with houses dug in the rock and superimposed, developed around the seventeenth century after the destruction of the castle; to see the churches of Sant'Andrea and San Nicola, the hermitage of the Madonna della Mazza, the rock mills of the Foro Valley and the fauna of the Apennine wolf.
Church of the historical center that houses Caravaggesche works.
Over a thousand artificial fruits that tell a century of the relationship between science, agriculture and research.
Listing in extension: the guide covers for now 1 of the 5 places of culture recorded by the Ministry of Culture in this municipality, as well as churches, squares and nature.
Gorge of the Sibillini reached with a walk of about 2 hours, 6 km and 250 meters of difference in altitude, also offered in autumn excursions among the centuries-old chestnut groves of Montemonaco.

Palace of 1718, date carved on the portal, built by the Cutrullà family, then hegemony in Zungri; it was the seat of the town hall and theatre of the revolt of 1901, when hundreds of citizens broke into the municipal council against the appropriation of the former state property lands assigned to the community in 1806. Today it is home to Pro Loco (prolocozungri@gmail.com).

Villa immersed in a park of the nineteenth century, with stuccoes and frescoes eighteenth century inside and, outside, a lemon house of the sixteenth century, balustrades and decorative vases of the twenties of the twentieth century; the chapel, built in 1720, contains frescoes attributed to Giovanni Battista Canal and two paintings of the Tiepolesque school.
Contemporary art on the rocks.
Borgo della val Neva under the cliff of Rocca Barbena, Orange Flag, with the 11th century castle, the parish church of the Assunta and the woods of Mount Carmo.

Consecrated in 1453, parish since 1520, visited by Saint Charles Borromeo in 1562, rebuilt in the eighteenth century and renovated in 1867. He guards the Madonna and Child of Bartolomeo Vivarini (1485), the Mystical Bride of Saint Catherine of Giovan Battista Moroni (1567-70), the Education of the Madonna of Piccio (1826) and works of Storer, Coghetti and Temperello.

The ancient Opitergium, commercial crossroads between Veneto Euganeo, Alpine and Eastern: the Roman forum with the patrician houses, the archaeological museum among the oldest in Italy and the scenic Piazza Grande.
The Secret Room welcomes 4 people every 15 minutes.
A bourgeois Renaissance house, rare to see intact.
The main walk of the city.
The untouched tholos and the view of Lake Mulargia.
Itinerary of about 11 km between the medieval watch towers, with views of the Tuscan Archipelago.
The medieval road is elevated and covered, illuminated by irregular arches, where once the birocciai with donkeys used to pass.

Country of holiday about 800 meters in the massif of Gennargentu, in the Barbagia of Belvì, among chestnut and hazelnut woods: the parish church of San Michele Arcangelo with Gothic-Aragonese parts, the Spanish prisons of Sa Bovida with the exhibition \ Bruxas Â, the Ecomuseum of the Sardinian mountain and the natural monument of Su Texile.
Panoramic ring between lake and mountain huts.

Municipality of the Friulian plain whose name recalls a funerary mound of the Bronze Age; in the hamlet of San Marco you can visit the collection of vintage bikes of Umberto and Flavio Nigris, in Tomb the church of San Michele with the sixteenth-century frescoes of Giulio Urbanis.

The ancient town, saturated within the walls, expanded beyond the belt between the sixteenth and seventeenth centuries around two churches and the Palazzo dei Nardi (XVII century). In 1550 a bridge was filled to create Piazza Mercato, today Piazza Enrico Bianco; among the buildings the Canenea (XVII century), Alimena, D'Alessandro and Sacchini (XVI century). Outside the walls stood the Jewish district of Cafarò, closed on two sides for the shops, and the Waldensian one of Borgoltramontano along the road to the fields. In 1516 the San Francesco complex was built.

Borgo dell'alta valle del Tibere on the border with Tuscany: the Bufalini Castle with the Italian garden and the bosso maze, the 17th century villa of Celalba with the finds of the Villa of Plinio il Giovane, the tobacco museum and the memory of the Republic of Cospaia.
The ideal city of Acquaviva.

Set up in 2007 in an old stable in Someda, it collects private collections and finds recovered in the restoration of the posts of the Costabella, Monzoni and Cima Bocche front: photographs, weapons, ammunition, uniforms and objects of the soldiers, with reconstructions of a trench, a machine gun nest and a comrade; it tells about the three years of Moena near the front line. Without fixed hours: visits in other days on request telephone for groups of at least 8 people.

Borgo at 420 meters on the Messinian Ionian coast, with views of the Etna, the Bay of Taormina and the Strait, set de "The Godfather": the Norman castle, the Durazzesco Arch, the Baroque Mother Church with the Annunciation of the Antonello area and the medieval village of the Quartarello.
Panoramic trekking trail that passes next to the Botanical Garden and the nearby adventure park.
The Celestinian hermitage suspended on the rock.
Photography.
Walk on the defenses to sea of the Serenissima.
In the Maison de la Tôr, cited in 1768, about fifty agricultural machines of the 1950s (currently closed).
The Templar church among the rice fields.
A green break under the walls.

Bronze statue of the Alata Victory, symbol of Casteggio, 18.50 meters high, dedicated to the fallen of the First World War: work of the sculptor Pier Enrico Astorri, was inaugurated on 21 November 1926 by Umberto di Savoia; to melt it they served over 25 tons of bronze and a foundry built on purpose. It rises in the Giardino delle Rimembranze in front of the town hall, with two Austrian cannons of the Great War and, since 1937, the travertine urn of the explorer Giuseppe Maria Giuletti, killed in Dancalia. The monument is not accessible but can be seen from Via Castello.
The coats of arms of the Venetian podestà in the square.

The village of the top of the Moscato Langa, dominated by the castle of the Marquises of Busca, seat of the Regional Enoteca Colline del Moscato and the Pinacoteca delle Langhe; in the village of San Donato the ethnographic collection "Cà delle memorie" and, for families, the thematic path Gnomovia between vineyards and hazelnuts.
Baroque chapel in the hamlet Vesallo.
Medieval art and civil memory in the same square.

Country of the Fortore on a hill of olive groves and orchards overlooking the valley of the river, founded in the fourteenth century by the abbot of the abbey of Santa Maria a Mazzocca: it dominates the bell tower of the Mother Church, which was in fact a cathedral of the bishops of Volturara, next to the seventeenth-century convent of Santa Maria degli Angeli and the palaces of the historic center.

To the north of Sedico rise the Monti del Sole and the walls of Schiara, Talvena and Gusela del Vescovà; the territory is crossed by the Alta Via delle Dolomiti n. 1 and Rifugio Bianchet is a starting point for excursions to the Bellunesi Dolomites National Park. Paths also on Mount Peron (1486 m) and Pala Alta (1933 m).

Nature reserve between Piazza al Serchio, San Romano, Sillano and Villa Collemandina, with woods of beech, chestnut and fir where they live wolf Apennines, deer, mouflon and royal eagle. There are easy paths for families, including the Bear Path of 1,020 meters with views of the Apuan Islands, the garden of mountain flowers and fences with deer and brown bears; it includes the reserve of the Pania di Corfino with its botanical garden.

Country at 835 meters on a hill between Maiella and Monte Rotella, home to an information center and excursions of the Majella National Park and stop of the Railway of the Parks; a few kilometers you will find the archaeological park of Ocriticum, italic-Roman sacred area with three temples.
Rilke's Elegie Castle.
A quiet balcony on the Marsica.
The history of Perugina told in the exhibition spaces inside the San Sisto plant; compulsory booking, with the possibility of courses at the Chocolate School.
A monumental tomb on the ancient Appia.
The tomb of the legend on the Via Appia.

The smallest municipality in Italy by area, less than a kilometer from Amalfi along the Dragon Valley and within the UNESCO site of the Amalfi Coast: a medieval intricate alleys, arches and steps around the little square on the sea, the church of San Salvatore de' Birecto where the doges and the collegiate church of Santa Maria Maddalena were crowned.
The view of the Duomo from the rooms.
damaged by earthquakes 2016-2017, in 2023 approved the project of consolidation of the tower
Beaches with coves and volcanic cliffs, awarded with Blue Flag, and a promenade to walk, with the historic center of squares, churches and shops.
Clear water in the middle.

Next to Palazzo Caccia-Canali, it contains the ancient Palazzo Abbaziale; in 1598 the Augustinian cloistered nuns moved there. The inner church preserves an altarpiece with the Saints Elena, Augustine and Nicola and a wooden choir.

Former elegant building in Art Nouveau style, seat of the museum route of Seui with sections of art, archaeology, ethnography and folk traditions and on the mining history of the country; here you can find the ticket office and all the services of the museum pole, and you can book excursions in the forest of Montarbu. The ticket is valid for all locations of the route or for a part of your choice. From October to March Tuesday to Sunday 9-13 and 15:30-17:30; from April to September 9:30-13 and 15:30-19:30.
The Verona fossils in a Renaissance palace.
The bell tower behind the church.

On the hill Bardosu, at the top of the village, the first Sardinian church to obtain the title of minor basilica: the current building is probably a reconstruction of the late seventeenth century on a sanctuary attested from the fifteenth century, with neo-Gothic façade of 1913 between two bell towers and bas-reliefs on the legend of the statue. Inside there is a single nave with four chapels on each side, dome on the presbytery, chestnut choir and the painted stone statue of the Madonna della Neve (XV century). It is always open; it hosts the rites of the Holy Week of the Rosary fraternity.

A village between the Ausoni and Aurunci Mountains Park, 129 km from Rome, known for the Basilica Sanctuary of the Madonna del Colle, consecrated in 1610, reached by the Stairway of Peace mosaic; around, the Monte Appiolo and the Natural Monument Cima del Monte - Acquaviva - Quercia del Monaco.
A Phoenix opera.

Borgo della Valle Caudina dominated by the Longobard castle, rebuilt at the end of the fifteenth century by Francesco di Giorgio Martini, which houses the National Archaeological Museum of Sannio Caudino with the crater of Assteas; below, the districts Latovetere and Latonuovo, convents and Piazza Umberto I.
The village of Boccaccio, Orange Flag of Touring: Certaldo Alto in red bricks, reachable by funicular, with the poet's house and the Pretorio Palace.

In the 17th century Palazzo Fanzago, next to the lace school: phases of workmanship and instruments, ancient lace from private collections and ecclesiastical furnishings, some of the eighteenth century, and recent works such as the Prince's Breakfast. Open every day 11-13 and 17-20 from August 1st to September 10th, from December 24th to January 6th and on Easter week.
the Municipality indicates the museum being refurbished after a period of closure

The heart of the city, Piazza XX Settembre brings together the Town Hall, Palazzo Garzolini (the seat of the court), the Duomo and, to the south, the eighteenth-century Palazzo Frisacco, the venue of art exhibitions. Around you will find the Mua Village with Palazzo Campeis, the Roggia Village (via Del Din, via Linussio) with small mills and artisan workshops, especially textiles, built at the Porta di Sotto, still visible between the three gates of the ancient city walls, and Palazzo Linussio, designed by Domenico Schiavi as a factory and residence of Jacopo Linussio, now a military property.

Bernini's work of the seventeenth century commissioned by Alessandro VII Chigi, a Greek cross plan with dome on Doric pillars, dedicated to the saint in the year of canonization. Inside stuccoes by Antonio Raggi and paintings by Pietro da Cortona (his altarpiece of the Crucifix), Giacinto Gimignani and Guglielmo Cortese.
The rocks that frame the village.
Oratory of the Disciplinanti of 1616-34, with marble altar of Dionisio Corte (1673), altarpiece of Domenico Piola (1676) and a seventeenth-century crucifix with silver ornaments.
The history of border smugglers.
The Roman columns at the top of the Scalinata di Virgilio mark the end of Via Appia; the monumental staircase accommodates up to 900 people during the events.
In the heart of the village.

Dedicated to the trade unionist Filippo Corridoni, born here (then Pausula) on 18 August 1887 and died at the Trencea delle Frasche on 24 October 1915: the path reconstructs its figure as a revolutionary interventionist, then taken as a symbol by fascism, to relocate it to its historical dimension. Open Monday to Saturday 9-13.30, by reservation (0733 439901).

Beaches of fine and quiet sand, well equipped, on a Blue Flag sea; the promenade is on foot or by bike between bars, restaurants and ice cream parlors, and the Pontile della Sirena is the panoramic point to see at sunset.
Theatre eighteenth century finished in 1795 and inaugurated in 1797.

The shrine of Our Lady of Reggio.
Bosco about 960 meters on the north-western side of Majella, with the source of the Morgia, one of the main karst phenomena of the massif.
Where the Po ends up in the sea.
The 17th century church of Montepagano.
The archaeological secrets of the Castelraimondo hill.
Gothic church of the village, known for its richly decorated portal.
Museum of Art of the twentieth century in a grain silo of 1933.

The imposing sixteenth-century palace that dominates the village, expanded over the centuries by the Lante della Rovere and then by the Borghese.
The fossils of the Cretaceous of Cilento told everyone.

Wanted by Don Orione where in 1418 he preached St Bernardino da Siena, it was started in 1928 on a project by Mgr. Chiappetta and consecrated in 1931, basilica since 1991; in Gothic-Lombard style, in the crypt it houses the tombs of Don Orione and Don Sterpi. On the tower stands the bronze statue of the Madonna of about 14 meters, work of Narciso Cassino.

About 1.5 km from the village, in the locality of San Lorenzo, rises on the site of the Roman city of Trea and an ancient parish church built on a temple of Isis: it preserves Roman remains, including a mosaic with ibis, and a 15th century crucifix that tradition wants carved by an angel and some attribute to Donatello.

Municipal museum since 1995 in the Gothic church of San Francesco (founded around 1300) and in the former convent: the frescoes of the apse, with Stories of San Francesco, are by Antonio Alberti (1422-1424) on commission of Braccio da Montone. The picture gallery exhibits the wooden group of the Deposition (1260-1270) from the Pieve di San Gregorio, the gonfalone of the Madonna della Misericordia di Bartolomeo Caporali, an Annunciation of the Signorellian School (1532), the  "Perugine Tablecloths" and finds of a Roman villa of the second century A.D. Open from April to September Friday-Sunday and holidays 10-13 and 16-18.30; from October to March Saturday, Sunday and holidays 10.30-13 and 15-17.30.

Country of the valley of the Trigno known for the Sanctuary of Santa Maria del Canneto, ancient Benedictine abbey with the statue of the Madonna del Sorriso, next to the remains of a Roman villa of the III-IV century AD with polychrome mosaics.
A mill with the defenses of a castle.

Hypogeum dug into the tuff and buried on three sides, in Trisulina on a height about 500 meters: four arches on five pillars divide the interior into two naves and two side stairs give access. For a long time considered the nymph of a Roman villa, the Municipality indicates it as an ancient temple of Santa Rosalia and among the few traces of the Roman presence of Augustian age in Calabria; around there are Corinthian capitals in marble, capitals with palms and fragments of granite columns. Not recommended for those who have motor difficulties.
Trenches of the Great War with sea view.
The most important Gothic church in the country.
Minerals, fossils and sands of the territory in a liberty villa.
Carlo Levi's summers.
The main street of the center, flanked by noble palaces, and the central square of the city.

Palace of sixteenth-century plant with portico with irregular arches, under which is preserved a Roman funerary cyp with inscriptions and bas-reliefs. According to the MiC, today the altarpiece of Simone De Magistris from San Nicolò is kept there.
About 3 km from the center, 1528, the parent house of the order of the Capuchins; in the glazed terracotta church attributed to Mattia della Robbia.
Private property, not accessible (MiC: closed daily)
Church with façade tower which preserves a Madonna with Child in white Carrara marble, Renaissance masterpiece by Francesco Laurana (1471-72).
The legendary tomb of the Turret martyrs on the cliff.
The romantic walk on the Lario.
Excavations started in 1995 on a settlement stratified by the Bronze Age in the Roman era; at the museum the cast of a person fleeing the eruption of the Pomici di Avellino.
16th century, designed by Giulio Romano for the fish trade.

Built in the eighteenth century by the Padua architect Andrea Zorzi, it conserves paintings from the sixteenth to the eighteenth century, including an Annunciation by Jacopo Palma il Giovane, and the Ark-Cenotaph of St. Pius X.
The interiors of the villa are not normally open to visitors
The Renaissance chapel in Piazza Duomo dedicated to the leader Bartolomeo Colleoni.

The only Istrian-Venetian town on the Italian coast, on the bay at the far east of the Gulf of Trieste: the Mandracchio with fishermen, the Duomo, the 14th century castle and, on the promontory, the Basilica of Muggia Vecchia.
Romanesque wiligelmic in the cradle of the Pico.

Church and Dominican convent built by Pius V since 1566 in his native country, with the participation of Giorgio Vasari: example of Roman Mannerism in northern Italy, with two cloisters, the library modeled by San Marco in Florence, works from Vasari to Moncalvo and the mausoleum of Pius V (the remains are in Rome). After the suppression of 1809 he was a barracks of Napoleonic veterans, reformatory and juvenile prison until 1989; in 2016 he arrived second to the
The statesman's birthplace is reminiscent of his most illustrious son.

The Carthusian barn on the Francigena.

The center is an irpino with a Renaissance structure with medieval walls and four doors, linked to San Gerardo Maiella, who lived in the bishop's palace from 1741 to 1744: today the palace houses the diocesan Museum, next to the eighteenth-century Cathedral, the churches of Santa Maria della Consolazione and the Cancelata and the Castello Pappacota.

On a hill in the historic centre, probably the first cathedral of the city: Byzantine church with Greek cross with dome, three circular apses, eight columns and Byzantine frescoes that tell the story.
It keeps on the main altar a marble polyptych by Antonello Gagini and a polychrome wooden statue of the eighteenth century saint.
The Greek cross frescoed.
Founded in 1542 on a hill near the village by the Clare monks who left the convent of the Piagge; above the high altar there is a fresco by Vincenzo Pagani.

Municipal theatre built between 1861 and 1869, reopened in 2005 after the restoration; originally had a mechanism to raise or lower the audience. Today it hosts prose, concerts and dance and is in the circuit of the Cultural Places card.

On a small hill, founded in the fifteenth century just outside the town and rebuilt several times, with the current appearance following the earthquake of 1783: three small naves with golden columns and decorations, statue of the Addolorata on the ancient pink and white altar, bell tower on the left side and stations of the Via Crucis in front of the façade. Open during functions.

In the oak, oak and chestnut woods around the village: the Fonte della Lama, in stone, cited in Leopoldini documents and for a long time a public wash-house; The Fonte di via della Fonte, with arch and seventeenth-century tub in trachyte already from the Abbey of Giugnano; the Fonte dell'amore e della passione, in trachyte, made by the artists of the Stone Road.
A medieval mill that still grinds, at the end of the Water Trail.

Near the museum, it reconstructs on a real scale the huts of a spafettical village of the Bronze Age, connected by walkways, with installations, thematic routes and open-air interpreting stations; it offers educational activities designed especially for families. Ticket combined with the museum.
The Baroque heart of the rebuilt city.
An off-scale sitting on the Lecco branch.

12th century castle born as a fortification on a hill between Orvieto and Perugia, disputed by the captains of Ventura; today it is a private residence, indicated as open to the public all year round.

The town of Varesotto, an ancient feud of the Pusterla and then an industrial village thanks to the factory of motorbikes Frera (1905-1936), whose sheds now house museum and library; next door, the largest collection of vintage petrol pumps in the Museo Fisogni and, in the woods of the Pineta Park, an astronomical observatory with planetary.
The Certosa in the woods.

In the former municipal warehouse of wheat ('Ammosso'), behind Palazzo Ceccarini-Chigi; born in 1980, museum since 1990, re-assembled in March 2003, it bears the name of the archaeologist of the University of Milan (1919-1976) who studied these places. It exhibits materials from prehistory to the modern age: Paleolithic, Neolithic and Eneolithic finds, the village of the final Bronze of Sorgenti della Nova with reconstructions, an Etruscan section (Naviglione, Rofalco, tombs of Palombaro) and the ceramics of medieval throws, which tell the daily life from the 14th to the beginning of the 17th century. It is part of the Bolsena Lake Museum System.
An eighteenth-century church of Riccati twin of the nearby villa.

Built in the 17th century by the Crown of Spain against the barbaric corsairs, it dominates the coast and gives access to the long sandy beach.
The ancient neighborhood where the rafts were docked, with via Uniera dei Zatèr, the church of San Nicolò, patron saint of the rafters and the remains of the old bridge of 1841.
The Callido organ.
The patron's baroque hat.

Artificial lake born at the confluence of the rivers Sangro and Aventino, important rest area for migratory birds; the oasis is managed together with the municipalities of Altino and Casoli and can be reached from the district Brecciaio towards Casoli, near the district Castellata-Tori.

The oldest and most famous of the four bridges on the Grand Canal, at the end of the sixteenth century: a single arch of over 28 meters on twelve thousand poles, with 24 shops; leads to the colorful market of fruits and vegetables of Rialto.
Small hamlet of stone houses, paved alleys, arches and barns known as "tagge" (tagges), under the Farnese lived of the iron and copper mines of Mount Groppo Maggio, closed in 1943.
Sienese art in the mountains.

Palazzo di fine Cinquecento, renovated in the eighteenth century, built as an autonomous residence of the Forti family and today town hall, with three floors above the road and two below. Rooms with coffered ceilings and eighteenth-century decorations, works from the seventeenth century, remains of frescoes from the fifteenth to the eighteenth century and, in the library, picen and Roman finds.
The statues carried in procession and the painting of the Marche in the sixteenth century in a single path.

In the former convent of Santa Chiara the museum of the Gianfranco Luzzetti Collection, with works from the fourteenth to the nineteenth century and the Baroque church of the Bigi, and the exhibition space Clarisse Arte.
Two medieval fortified villages of the municipal territory, with houses narrow to each other and often joined by supporting arches.

The largest centre of the city, with the structure of the late nineteenth century: the Town Hall with eclectic façade, the Palazzo del Governo neo-Renaissance, Palazzo Pitteri of late eighteenth century and the Palazzo del Lloyd, today the presidency of the Region.
The palace was built in 1391 by Alberto V d'Este, then seat of the University, with the Anatomical Theatre of 1731, the staircase of Antonio Foschini and the tomb of Ludovico Ariosto.
In the Palazzo di Brera, with the Academy of Fine Arts, the Braidense Library, the Observatory and the Botanical Garden: a path from prehistory to contemporary art.

Fortification of medieval origin from the time of the Counts Cadolingi, then of the Alberti until 1332, when the Florentine bankers Bardi bought it; the defenses were destroyed in the battles of the XIV and XV century. The ruins, the well-preserved medieval village and the chapel of Sant'Agata remain; the next building is a private residence, recently restored. From San Quirico you can go up the medieval path near Casone or by car before Sasseta.
The last water forge in the valley, witness to the work of iron in Scalve.
The story of the golden chariot ended in New York.

Started in the second half of the thirteenth century and completed in 1346 by Bonanno da Barletta: unique nave with polychrome marbles and stuccoes of the eighteenth century, two portals and a Gothic monophorus; the cloister, once frescoed with stories of St. Francis, hosts cultural events.

Next to the castle, along the ancient Appia: here on September 20, 1378 Count Onorato I Caetani hosted the French cardinals who elected the Antipope Clement VII, starting the Western Schism. In the fifteenth century, Honorato II made it the "magnum palatium" with Catalan late dogotic windows, Renaissance portals and fireplaces with the coat of arms Gaetani d'Aragona (1466); Giulia Gonzaga held court there and was born there in 1531 Vespasiano Gonzaga Colonna. Restored by the Lazio Region, it preserves fragments of frescoes in the picta room, a rare profane pictorial cycle, and is the center of the Ausoni Mountains Park.

Opened in 2011, it leads to an altitude of 3,000 meters with views over most of the Eastern Alps; from the top a track of almost 8 km goes down to Peio Fonti. Around the Cevedale (3,764 m) and the Vioz (3,644 m).
The lake is just a stone's throw from the village.
The social history of a valley of magnans and shepherds.

Built in 1810 in the locality of Sorgentina, it was expanded between 1905 and 1908 with a small hydroelectric power plant that, immediately after the Second World War, flooded for a few months the public lighting of the neighboring municipalities. Restored in the early 2000s, with original turbines and generators back in operation, it is the center of the Reserve and has didactic use; next to a picnic area among olive trees, dry walls and terraces.
Giotteschi frescoes of the fourteenth century.
The ex-vote of the pestilence cluse.
Protected area of the Cozie Alps with the two morainic lakes at the foot of the city.

Medieval castle founded in 921 by the Burgundian Baron Rovero de Champeaux, founder of the counts of Campello, with circular walls, watchtowers and a single well preserved door. On the central square the former town hall and the church of San Donato (XII century, with wooden Baroque altar); just below the convent of the Barnabite Fathers, born in the seventeenth century by the union of two Benedictine monasteries.
A megalithic tomb of the Bronze Age in the middle of olive trees.
The best way up.

Rebuilt in 1511 at the behest of Ludovico Gonzaga on the remains of a previous defensive structure, it was surrounded by a large moat and was part of the defenses of the village with the Door Spinata, still existing, and the Door of the Valley, demolished at the end of the nineteenth century. There remains one wing with one of the four cylindrical towers (the eastern tower), the mast, under which you enter the courtyard, and part of the curtain. Inside a sixteenth-century Gonzaga palace, where the remains of the synagogue of the Jewish community favored by Gonzaga are preserved, and a small restored nineteenth-century theatre. Free access to the ground floor.
Nineteenth and twentieth centuries in Piazza della Scala.
The ceramics that made Cerreto famous.
The village of the quarrymen.
The museum of industrial archaeology in the former dynamite factory.
Shops and palaces along the way.

Portal between the flowered Gothic and the first Renaissance, Augustinian cloister of the first half of the fourteenth century and the Cappellone di San Nicola with frescoes by Pietro da Rimini and students; the museum of the basilica preserves paintings, sculptures, ceramics, ex-vote and a permanent nativity scene.

The residence of Captain Ferdinando Aiello, who on 29 August 1860 hosted Giuseppe Garibaldi; next to the entrance a stone post for the centenary recalls the visit (in these walls he had hospitality Giuseppe Garibaldi on 29 August 1860).
Memories of the Risorgimento on the lake.
An eighteenth-century church on Roman foundations.

Borgo dei Monti della Tolfa, Cittaslow known for its leather processing, with the medieval centre clinging to the hill of the Fortress: the ruins of the castle Frangipane and the sanctuary of the Fortress, the palaces born with the alum, the sanctuary of the Madonna della Sughera with the Civic Museum, over 17,000 hectares of hills and one of the most beautiful skys in Italy.
The triduum machine from 365 candles.
Tombs of the princes with totemic wolf.
The ocarina was born in Budrio: the museum collects a unique collection in the world.
You go out with a handmade sheet.
Get in the train in the heart of a copper mine.

Built by the lords of Tures in the twenties of the thirteenth century with the mast on the mountain, extended to residence in the fifteenth and sixteenth centuries; since 1977 it is the Südtiroler Burgeninstitut. It has 64 rooms, 24 covered in wood with coffered ceilings: armory, library, Hall of the Princes, the Chamber of the Infirms with 26 portraits of children (1564-67) and the Stube of the ghosts linked to the legend of Margarethe von Taufers; the chapel has frescoes by Friedrich Pacher and a Tardoromanic crucifix of the thirteenth century. It hosts the permanent exhibition "Hunters and prey" on the history of hunting.

Above the village, 500 climbing routes for all levels divided into 21 sectors, one of which is dedicated to children; among the most famous cliffs in the North-West.

Rural village of the Val di Cecina between forests and geothermal phenomena, in the Cornate and Fosini Reserve.
The Italian emigration told on board a ship.
The surviving tower of the oldest castle in the town, dating back to the 11th century.
The Sacred Mount on the lake.
The view from Partenio to the Gulf of Naples.
The sources between fossils and waterfalls.
Contemporary art in the landscape.
Art in San Carlo Square.
A Roman city abandoned in the middle of the meadows.

Città dell'Alta Valle Tanaro on the border with Liguria, the ancient Ulmeta has a heart-shaped plant crossed by the alleys called "Trevi": the Romanesque parish church of San Martino with frescoes of the fourteenth century, the House of Lords of the fourteenth century, the ruins of the castle, the ethnographic museum and, in the surroundings, the Balma del Messere, the Tower of the Saracens and the Balcony of Ormea.

Museum born from the Verbano Express association to restore and preserve the historic railway vehicles that have served on the lines of the Verbano. Open on the second and fourth Saturdays of the month from 14:30 to 18:00, or by appointment.

Small village on a panoramic hill between Valsesia and Valsessera, with origins around the year Mille and walls and courtyards closed of medieval plant; it is called "Country Museum Vivo" for its museums, including the Museum of Natural Sciences of the cav. Carlo Locca and the Casa dei Mestieri, and for the botanical garden Pier Carlo Bussi.
The "Piazza della Shame," one of the symbols of Palermo.
The living room of the Valdarno.

Founded around the 5th century and enlarged in Romanesque times, it has the present aspect of the thirteenth century works of Burgundian workers: a hut façade with three portals and a rhyphole rosette, inside three naves. It preserves the Madonna of Constantinople, a wooden group of the thirteenth century, the Triptych of the Redeemer by Antonio da Alatri (first half of the fifteenth century) and a baptismal font of the thirteenth century with three telamons.
Visitable during Open Monuments, in May
Perhaps Norman origin, rebuilt at the end of the seventeenth century.

In the abbey palace and under the sixteenth-century portico of Giuliano da Sangallo, it collects artifacts from the surrounding territory and the remains of the cryptoportico of the Roman villa on which the abbey stands; the most famous piece is an attic stele in pentelic marble of 430-420 BC with a young man reading a scroll. Guided tours of volunteers on Saturday at 11:00 and 4:00.

The oldest church of Teti, originally Gothic-Aragonese, rises in a park not far from the village surrounded by the cumbessias, the little houses that house the faithful during the feast of the saint at the end of August.

It tells the protected area of the Furlo Gorge by combining natural history, geology and landscape with the history of man, architecture and culture, with the role of the mountain at the centre. There's no need to book.

Collection of railway equipment set up inside the station of Cagliari, with restoration workshop.
The peak of the country's traditions, overlooking the valley.
