The museum of modern and contemporary art from the futuristic building, with over 4500 works and space for exhibitions, events and workshops; free ground floor.
Byzantine icons in an Albanian village in Abruzzo.
Cly's stone palace.

In the former nineteenth-century mill, industrial complex with large windows and large arches on the ground floor, scientifically curated by Rosario Chimirri: four rooms with panels and large projections tell geography, flora, fauna and paths, urban planning and architecture, work and food, dialect, traditional music, cult of the saints and feasts of the Serre.
The wooden Christ of the thirteenth century.
A house in the history of science.
Art and history in the upper city.

The main square of Terracina preserves the Roman limestone pavement financed by the magistrate Aulo Emilio between the end of the first century BC and the beginning of the I AD, with the inscription in bronze letters Aemilius A. F. Stravit'; on the north side runs a preserved stretch of the Appia Antica. Around stood the civil basilica, the temple then incorporated into the Cathedral and the theatre. Always accessible.
The outdoor theatre of summer festivals.

Built in several phases between ancient and middle Bronze (XIX-XVII century BC), with a four-metre-high stele; Italia.it indicates it as the largest of its kind. It is located about 1 km from La Prisgiona along the giant trail. Open every day 9-19.
The city's main museum.

Salento country dominated by the Castriota Castle, with a historic centre rich in sixteenth-seventh-century palaces, the Sanctuary of the Madonna della Coltura which houses the monolith with the image of the Madonna and the Giannelli Art Gallery in Palazzo Ferrari; in the territory the Grotta delle Veneri, discovered in 1966.

It rises on the remains of a fortress of the twelfth century; the current building was built in 1630 by the Marquises of Busca, renovated in Baroque style and recently restored. On the ground floor, the Enoteca Regionale Colline del Moscato collects the products of over 80 wine producers and 20 food and wine producers of 52 municipalities between Cuneo, Asti and Alessandria, with tastings dedicated to Moscato d'Asti DOCG, Asti Spumante, Canelli DOCG and Strevi DOC; the castle also houses the Pinacoteca delle Langhe, concerts, exhibitions and events. Dominates the old village with views of the hills.
In the unique ticket of the Museums of Fiesole (€12 with area and archaeological museum)
A young Parmigianino in the mountains.

Built in the 13th century and renovated in 1777, it has a Baroque façade, a Gothic bell tower with double-fores and crypt, and preserves a relic of St. Euphemia's arm. The most famous work is the polychrome statue of the stone saint of Vicenza, 172 cm high, dated around 1450 and brought here in 1454 by Roberto De Mabilia from the Padua workshop of Mantegna: the saint holds one hand in the mouths of a lion and with the other holds the three-top mountain with the castle, symbol of Irsina. Attribution to Mantegna is now discussed by scholars.
Damaged by the 2016 earthquake (regional portal)

Remains of a medieval castle, sloped about 13 degrees and supported by pulls, reachable by a path in the woods about 20 minutes from the hamlet of Vernazzano, about 5 km from the center; view of the lake.
A Roman temple on the plateau.

Despite its name it is not a tower but a monumental door between Piazza Duomo and Via XX Settembre, built in the early sixteenth century Lombardy instead of a more modest entrance of the citadel. On the side of the square has the statues of the Saints Pantaleone and Vittoriano and the coat of arms of Crema; towards Via XX Settembre the Lion of San Marco of 1525, scarred by the French in 1797; the clock is of 1555 and the bell of the lantern announced from 1594 the meetings of the Council. In 2016 there was a scene of "Call me by your name" .
The first Roman walls.

The seventeenth-century complex, with history dating back to the early seventeenth century, and the church from the façade of 1902; inside the large painting of Stefano da Carpi with the Exaltation of the Franciscan Saints and the wooden tabernacle of Fra' Fedele da Scandiano at the high altar.
A stone village on top of the valley.
The Risorgimento in his country house.

Inaugurated in June 1999 in a restaurant between the church and the canon of San Giorgio, used between the two wars as a small theatre. A section tells the valley of the Recchio from the Roman to the nineteenth century, with coins of Domitian and Maxentius and the cast of the Jubilee stone of Roccalanzona linked to the first Jubilee of 1300; the exhibition of peasant civilization, from the collection donated by Marco Pometti of Roccalanzona, exhibits on ten ancient keys stele, tools of blacksmiths, carpenters and peasants, tools for wine, wool and hemp, a press for spaghetti and tools of the norcino. Open every day by appointment (tel. OJ L 347, 20.12.2013, p. 671.
The sanctuary in the rock of the Sellaro.

Parma Apennines municipality, located in Mormorola (565 m), along the valley of the Mozzola stream that descends from Monte Barigazzo and La Tagliata to the Taro; among the places to see the Museum of the Resistance, the thirteenth-century ruins of the Fortress of Gusaliggio and the nearby parish church of Santa Maria Assunta.
The fifteenth-century icon and the bell tower vanvitellino.
Handicrafts at work with stone, wood, wicker and broom; among the products also dolls in Albanian costume.
The great patriarchal cathedral and its bell tower.
The sanctuary of skiers, a walk from the village.

Commissioned in 1500 by Cardinal Antonio Ciocchi Di Monte to Antonio da Sangallo the Elder, author of a plan, rustic façade in sandstone and courtyard; completed in the mid-500s, under Julius III, by Nanni di Baccio Bigio with the rear facade and the hanging garden all'italiana. Since 1822 it has been the municipality: you can visit the courtyard with loggia on Tuscan pillars and columns, the prisons of 1824 with original furnishings, the hanging garden on two levels with open-air theatre, the portrait gallery and the Council Hall with the sixteenth-century wooden door of Giovanni da Verona.
The tower at the top of the village.
The bell tower of the high village.

Church of 1585, with facade rebuilt around 1728 with the coat of arms of the Paccaroni, today deconsecrated and used for events as classical music concerts. It has a wooden ceiling painted in tempera in the eighteenth century, attributed to the stop Filippo Ricci and indicated as the most extensive of the genus in the Marches, five wooden altars gilded and marbled, blades attributed to G. Ghezzi and F. Ricci is an organ of the callidian school; the canvas of Simone De Magistris with the Madonna, the Child and Saints is today in the municipal palace.

Ancient Lombard capital on Ticino and one of the oldest university cities in the world: the Visconti Castle with the Civic Museums, San Michele Maggiore where Barbarossa, the Ark of Sant'Agostino, the Duomo and the Covered Bridge were crowned.
A place of silence in the woods.
€5 (unique ticket), free up to 5 years
To see closely the accessories and treasures that emerged from the hypogeans.
Belvedere on the plateau with a wide panorama of the Tavoloiere that reaches up to the Gargano and the Tremiti Islands.
The Gothic Cistercian overturned.
The shrine of Soliera.
Apollo's bronze head.
A house of the nineteenth century that remained as it was, between Risorgimento and domestic life.
One of the first English gardens in Italy, a few kilometers from Milan.
The museum village.

The town of Val Bormida di Millesimo, called "the village of the churches" for its twenty churches and chapels: in the hamlet of Ponte there are the Gothic parish church of San Lorenzo (1440-1445) and the Oratory of Sant'Agostino, FAI places, while in the hamlet of Riofreddo the Museum of C'era once has its seat.

Norman Castle of the 11th century on Monte Serico, 550 meters and about 15 km from the village, on the border between the Byzantine lands of the Bradano and those Lombard and Norman; it was the scene of the defeat of the Byzantines against the Normans and then masseria of the state property of Frederick II, who frequented it for raptors. It has a trunk-conical shape surrounded by a moat, central square tower, low belt with shoe and drawbridge; in the underground there are prehistoric caves. A simple chapel stands on the floor.
Rare marble altar.
The fossils of the ancient sea and the rhinoceros of the steppes found on the hill.

Karst cave under the village, with stalactites and stalagmites, discovered by chance on October 27, 1987 during the excavations for the sewer in via Dante Alighieri. It takes its name from a large thin and translucent stalactite in the shape of a fan in the center of the cavity; the tunnels suggest that it extends for tens of meters and is connected to other caves of the area.
18th century fountain of Bartolomeo Grasso on the main square.

Sanctuary of Santa Maria Bambina, better known as Madonna del Noce, dating back to 1470; it was for a period parish church and was expanded in 1615. The hut façade has a portal surmounted by a bezel with high relief terracotta.
Renaissance palace with gardens overlooking the city; next to the gate the narrow and high
From the admonitions to the Longobards, the story of Alta Brianza.
The Middle Ages rebuilt on the Po.
Its façade closes the fourth side of Piazza Ducale.
A trace of the reclamation in town.
A medieval abbey hidden in the bottom of a gorge.

Next to the former convent of the Dominican cloisters, of which the well remains, it exhibits among other things an ostensory attributed to Cellini; on the upper floor there is the ancient apse of a church with frescoes from 1583 with scenes from the Old and New Testaments.

Built at 1,053 meters to control the Aniene valley, it is the nucleus around which the village developed; in 1052 it passed to the monastery of Santa Scolastica of Subiaco and in 1273 it was occupied by Pelagio by Jenne, who resisted the siege three years. In 1513 the abbot of Subiaco Pompeo Colonna had it rebuilt. From the stairs around the fortress opens the panorama of the valley.
From Peschiera starts the bike path to Mantua along the Mincio, through the park of the river valley suitable for walks in nature.
A border of Earth history marked in the river.
The ancient city above the new one.

Small agricultural municipality of Lomellina, the plain between Ticino, Po and Sesia; around the medieval castle, with the south facade of the eighteenth-century villa, is the Museum of art and peasant tradition.
A millenarian abbey at the entrance of the throat.
A walk through fountains, Liberty greenhouses and exotic trees.

The museum is a first attempt to reconstruct a part of the health history of South Italy at the beginning of the twentieth century through the story of a hospital in a small town of the Calabrian Serre. Booking not required; MiC (2020) does not report up-to-date times.
Our Lady of Loreto in cedar.
Fortified village of Siena after Montaperti (1260), between the hills of Chianti and Crete Senesi, in a territory full of castles and Romanesque parishes.
The Lombard masterpiece of the UNESCO site.
The walls with the Rivellino castle, among the medieval jewels of Tuscania.
Rare example of a baroque residence in the Valle d'Aosta, in the restoration phase.
A hunt for solar clocks between the houses of the country.
The works of the diocese in the underground of the cathedral.

Museum that preserves and enhances the Cimbrian culture, with sections on history and traditions, Great War and local fauna; it is also the reference point for visits to the fort and the house museum.
Weight control in the Roman forum.

Santa Lucia in Sylvis was built in the thirteenth century on the remains of the medieval castle of Castel Gualdo and is linked to the Franciscan presence; restored after the earthquake of 1997, it is among the monumental buildings of the Marches.
€2.50 (one-time ticket, Polo and Quadreria)

Permanent exhibition inaugurated on May 26, 2012 in the Medieval Palazzetto of the fourteenth century: over 140 works by 50 divisionist artists with Giuseppe Pellizza da Volpedo (more than 20 paintings), together with Segantini, Medardo Rosso, Nomellini and Morbelli; a room is dedicated to the Dolonese Angelo Barabino. Open Saturday and Sunday 15-19, other days by reservation.
Stralled bridge of Santiago Calatrava sul Crati, with a single 104-metre-high inclined pylon, dedicated to St. Francis of Paola; the shape recalls a harp.
A hermitage dug into the rock where the Capuchins were born.
The Roman water lilies on the shores of the lake.
€11, reduced €8
Walking and cycling trails, fishing huts and the Pialassa Baiona.
The Adoration of the Magi by Filippo Paladini.
The two long theories of saints are among the most photographed mosaics in Italy.
The most central beach of the island, reachable by going down 186 steps.

The backbone of the medieval village, with porticos and noble residences with frescoed facades between the fifteenth and seventeenth centuries, with floral motifs, sacred figures, coats of arms and mythological scenes, which have earned Pordenone the name of .
The treasure of the cathedral and the ancient bells.
The partisan and peasant memory of the Sand Valley.
From the Etruscans to the modern Viterbo.
Stone and silver of the patron's church.

Medieval plant closed by the walls built by the Republic of Siena, one of the best preserved in Tuscany, with a renovated pedestrian path that looks at the countryside to the sea. You enter from Porta San Giovanni to the south and follow Corso Garibaldi to the Palazzo dei Priori, with the family coats of arms on the facade, and to Piazza della Libertà with the church of San Martino, cited since the 13th century; Porta San Martino, to the north, offers a wide panorama.
Church of the thirteenth century entirely renewed in the nineteenth century; it preserves the Nativity of the Virgin of Carlo Maratta, of the seventeenth century.

Municipality to the east of Brescia that gives the name to the precious Botticino marble, extracted from its quarries from the sixteenth century; the Marble Museum tells about its geology, extraction and processing and accompanies the nearby quarry with the itinerary      Â Landscapes of extraction Â .
Two small picturesque villages of the municipal territory, developed around the homonymous castles; the source indicates them as worthy of a visit.

Picturesque houses built to overlook the river Aso, with the walls and an access bridge; the center, perhaps ancient Roman settlement, was repopulated in the fourteenth century. On December 26 there is the living nativity scene and in the village there is the Mazzumaja, a three-day feast around the crazy thrush.
An empty village and an ancient stone bridge.
The sacred viewpoint above the roofs.
The study of a 20th century sculptor.
A noble villa with a centuries-old ginkgo.
Circular stone village with towers and walls of the fifteenth century, at the foot of the Sienese Montagnola.
The 11th century castle above the village.
Borgo Walser Orange Flag at 1154 meters at the foot of Monte Rosa, in the Natural Park of Alta Valsesia, with traditional wooden and stone houses.
Where the Franciscan Rule was born.
€10 in full (+€1 online); €6 from 12 to 17 and students; €10 family (under 18 free with parents)

On the edge of the Agro Pontino along the Via Appia, the ancient Tres Tabernae where St. Paul stood was the center of the Caetani fief and was almost destroyed in 1944; today it offers Palazzo Caetani with its caves, the Biondi Fountain in Piazza XIX Marzo and, in its territory, the Garden of Ninfa, a natural monument among the ruins of a medieval city.

The central square of Strada in Casentino is surrounded by the Vector and Vector-Tommasi palaces and dominated by the Logge del Grano, five round arched bays in serene stone with the ancient roof; next, the former municipal seat today library and the sixteenth century Chapel of the Visitation with a Virgin with Child and Saints of Giovan Francesco Guerrieri (about 1600). Higher up, in the panoramic part of the village, the eighteenth-century "Collegio" is already a seminary of Jesuits, Salesians and dioceses of Fiesole.

In the former Alfa Romeo factory, Arese houses the historic Museum of the brand, reopened in 2015; in the Valera area remain the eighteenth-century villa La Valera and the church of San Bernardino, the oldest sacred building in the country.
The only National Museum of Naïf Art.
Free Outdoors; paid exhibitions according to the program
The portrait of Saint Francis still alive.
San Lorenzo was the first parish church in the village and has a wooden ceiling decorated with heads of lions and dragons; also San Pietro and San Rocco are medieval churches.
The equestrian culture of the country of Ardia.
The Palace of Margaret of Austria.

Built in 1580 as the summer residence of the prince bishop of Bressanone Johann Thomas von Spaur, once with aviary and deer park; purchased by the Province of Bolzano in 1978 and restored in 1979-83. Ten rooms with wooden walls and wall paintings make it one of the best preserved Renaissance residences in the Alps; on the first floor the archaeological museum with finds of Velturno and the Middle Isarco Valley, temporary exhibitions on the ground floor and in the Schreiberhaus.
For a piano ride.
Roman villa on the hill of Varano, on the site of the excavations of Stabia.
The city of the Etruscan dead.
Bunker near the spring of the Adige at about 1550 meters, partly dug in the rock and partly in concrete, about 20 meters long with about 450 m2 visitable; managed by the association Oculus.

Valley without road access but inhabited all year round, rare case in the alpine arch. From the parking lot of Novate a staircase of 2,500-3,000 steps in the centuries-old chestnut grove, with views of Lake Mezzola and parapets in the exposed points, climbs to the village of Codera; then the path continues sweet up to Bresciadega and to the Rifugio Brasca (10 km, 466 m of difference in altitude, about 2 hours and a half, medium difficulty), between ancient stone houses and the granite quarries of San Fedelino.
damaged by the earthquake 2016 with collapses located in the vaults, safety and restoration in design (MIC USS Sisma, January 2026)

Villa built in several phases between the 1st century BC and the 4th AD, one of the most important late ancient villas in northern Italy, famous for the polychrome mosaic floors with pagan scenes; the client of the last phase could be Flavio Magno Decenzio, brother of the emperor Magnenzio, perhaps at the origin of the name of the city. The Antiquarium exhibits a second century marble Hercules, a late 4th century glass cup with Christ and the rooster and a teenage bust. Tuesday-Saturday 9-19.30, Sunday 14.10-19.30, Monday closed; cumulative ticket with Caves of Catullo and Castle of Sirmione €14 and annual pass Garda Heritage €21.

Ethnoanthropological Museum recognized as Museum Collection by the Lombardy Region in 2007, born from over two thousand objects from the peasant world collected from the eighties by the farmer Andrea Baraldini and set up in a factory abandoned along the avenue of entry to the village. Agricultural and artisan tools (falegname, cardatore, blacksmith, shoemaker, saddlery), domestic furnishings and toys on 300 square meters covered, plus two outdoor areas with wagons, calexs, ploughs, harrows and a military field kitchen; library, archive and photographic fund. Free admission; open Tuesday, Wednesday and Thursday 8.30-11.30, Saturday 9.30-11.30 and 14.30-17; extraordinary guided tours on request.
The silvers and vestments of the Anglona religious tradition.

The fourteenth-century door with sharp arch in local stone is the only surviving of the two of the Norman walls. The center, with the remains of the Town Hall and the Archimandrital Palace and the synagogue documented until 1470, has seven districts with medieval, Renaissance, Baroque and rural buildings of the early twentieth century; at the entrance panels in ceramic bas-relief of Salvatore and Giuseppe Zona tell the history of the village.
Museum dedicated to the promotion and dissemination of contemporary art.

The only complex nuraghe of Suni, on the plateau of Pedrasenta at 350 meters, of the Bronze Age (XIV-X century BC): the central tower exceeds 14 meters, with two rooms in tholos, and is surrounded by a bastion with three towers around a pentagonal courtyard.

Square tower of the XII-XIII century, about 29 meters high, fulcrum of the Malaspina fortified complex, documented as a prison by the Statutes of 1320 and used as a prison until the sixties of the twentieth century; the name comes from the tradition according to which in 1460 there were locked up women and men accused of witchcraft before the burning in the square. With 130 steps you can climb to the panoramic terrace overlooking the village, the Staffora and, with the serene, the Castle of Oramala. The adjacent private castle combines an eighteenth-century facade with sundial, a fifteenth-century wing with the coat of arms of Spino Secco and a part of the thirteenth century.

About 300 hectares between Andreis, Barcis and Montereale Valcellina, managed by the Friulian Dolomites Park: the largest limestone gorge in the region, with perennial water, waterfalls, erosion forms and rare plants. It crosses the old Valcellina road between Monte Fara and Pala d'Altei; there is a 55-metre Tibetan bridge. The visitor center is in Ponte Antoi (Barcis).
A panoramic ring between village, vineyards and woods.
The baroque sanctuary of the seventeenth century with the Crucifixion of Guercino and the cycle of frescoes dedicated to the heroines of the Old Testament; next to the museum of the sanctuary.
One of the great Roman amphitheaters of the South.
The stone beasts in front of the giants' graves.
Corridors dug into the tuff by the Etruscans, some over a kilometer long with walls up to 20 meters high; at the Gradone the open-air museum with the routes of the city of the living and the dead.
The loggia that unites palace and mother church.
The promenade on the gulf.

Walled village of the Metauro valley: in the Palazzo del Feudatario the Collection of contemporary graphics and the Museum of the ancient itinerant crafts with the bicycles of the street vendors; remains the cistern of the fortress of Francesco di Giorgio Martini, and in Monte Montanaro a shovel of Gianfrancesco Guerrieri.
Bientina's holy silvers.

Church of the XVI century just outside the walls, with a golden wooden altar and painted in late Baroque style that has in the center a terracotta altarpiece of the Madonna with Child, work of a pupil of Silvestro dell'Aquila.

In the Palazzo Agostiniano, it preserves among other things a crucifix in inlaid mother of pearl of the eighteenth century, a series of piviali and antiphonari miniati of the sixteenth century, seventeenth and eighteenth century.
The great Romanesque abbey with frescoes and crypt with columns.
€14 whole; €7 from 6 to 18 years; family €32

At the foot of the Asolani hills, Cornuda houses the Italian mortgage, museum and typographical culture center; on the hill of the Fortress the Sanctuary of the Madonna della Rocca and the ossuary of the fallen of 1848, not far from the Romanesque church of the Saints Vittore and Corona.

High Irpinia country, 850 metres above the Upper Ofanto valley, fortified in the middle of the 6th century according to a Byzantine scheme, with the Baroque mother church of the Assumption, the museum of peasant civilization and the sanctuary of the Madonna Stella del Mattino alla Mattinella.

Center of the Cremona plain with a heritage of churches between the sixteenth and seventeenth centuries, rich in canvases of Genovesino and Malosso, starting from the prepositural of San Siro; in the village there is also the museum dedicated to the Sorese statesman Francesco Genala.

City of Giotto and Sant'Antonio, with frescoed cycles of the fourteenth century "Padova Urbs picta" and the oldest botanical garden in the world, both UNESCO World Heritage, the University since 1222 and Prato della Valle.

According to tradition in 1480 a source considered miraculous sprang up under an ancient tomb, making the place a pilgrimage destination; in 1486 the Servants of Mary arrived from Bergamo built a new church there and in 1510 the convent began. The nave was enlarged at the end of the sixteenth century; the damage of mercenaries in 1629 closed the period of prosperity and the complex was restored at the beginning of the two thousand years. Today it hosts exhibitions and concerts; festivals on 25 March (the ...Fera dei Cavagnöi) and 8 September. There is an integrated ticket with Villa Monastero di Varenna (full €16 with the house museum, €13 with the garden only), valid for 15 days.

Baroque and Rococo church of 1679 by the De Bortolo brothers, with facade in tuff of Mendicino, marble altar and inlaid wood, nativity scene with Neapolitan statues and organ of the eighteenth century.
MiC card reports every day as closed and no time; location indicated as provisional
A village of transhumance remained medieval.
Rosalba Career on the Amiata.

Granite village of the Upper Gallura, Orange Flag for its ancient harmonic and intact core, famous for its carpets and choir: the ethnographic MEOC museum, the Banditism Museum in the old Pretura, the AAAperto open-air museum and, in the surroundings, the Valley of the Moon with the Nuraghe Izzana.
To the intermittent source of the Lambro.
Climb the mastium and see the walls from above.
The wine in the traditional cellars.

The 19th century theatre entitled to Vincenzo Pagani; the curtain, painted by the stage designer Alessandro Bazzani, portrays the painter at work on a terrace overlooking a coastal landscape with pine trees.
A small sixteenth-century temple in the center.
From Santo Stefano Lodigiano, a village crossed by bike paths in the open countryside, starts a cycle route that touches Fombio, San Fiorano, San Rocco al Porto and Guardamiglio.
The route of the old Spoleto-Norcia railway line is today a route for hiking, trekking and cycling.
Rogge, prehistory and castle on a hike.
A Renaissance cycle of the Passion and the treasure of the Collegiate.
The Crucifix of Umile from Petralia.
An easy ring on the hills above the village.

Ancient Romanesque parish church of the 12th century next to the old cemetery, dedicated first to Santa Maria del Prato, then to San Pietro and finally to San Rocco; several times renovated for the Rio della Rossa, which buried the first floor of the bell tower, had the orientation reversed before 1643. From the excavations fragments of the fresco of the triumphal arch and the ancient apse have emerged, perhaps the oldest in the Val di Susa.
The memory of mining work.
The museum of peasant life of the village.
The Della Rovere castle between alleys and washrooms.
The cathedral built on a bridge.
Scandiano's porticoed heart.

Remains of the fortress at the top of the country, whose first mention is in a letter from Pope Lucius III of 1181; it was demolished in the mid-500s by the will of Paul III Farnese. After four years of excavation, funded by the Region with 300,000 euros, the site was inaugurated in May 2011. The viewpoint dominates the village with a view of the territory to the sea.
In the basement of the church of St. Pius X are exhibited during the year the statuary groups of the procession of Holy Thursday.
The living room of Monte Regale.
View of San Leo and Montefeltro.
On the top floor of the spa complex at the top of the mountain, it exhibits prehistoric and historical finds of the excavations conducted in the caves between the sixties and eighties.
Romanesque late Umbrian church with 13th century façade and stone portal of Assisi; it is the only building of Cannara to have preserved the medieval appearance.

In Gaudimare district, about 3 km from the village: church of Byzantine origin, remodelled in Norman age, finished under the ground level for landslides or floods and discovered in 1874 during the works of the above church of Madonna del Carmine. The frescoes, dating back to the seventh century, include the Annunciation on the sides of the apse, a group of saints with perhaps Mary Magdalene in the center, the Virgin Galaktotrefouse who feeds the Child with a pomegranate, St. Anthony Abbot and fragments of the Christ Pantocrator.

A sixteenth-century complex of shrine, convent and bell tower, with frescoes, paintings and wooden statues and a life of travagliata in the last centuries. The library of the convent contains about 30,000 volumes, including medieval illuminated codes, five hundred and six hundred, escaped from Napoleonic and post-unitary dispoliations; the convent also has an internal garden.

Municipality of the Mòcheni valley, the valley of German-speaking settlers established since the thirteenth century: here the farm Filzerhof of the fifteenth century and the sawmill De sog van Rindel, sections of the Museum of the Mòcheni valley, and the paths to the Gronlàit, the Fravòrt and the Valcava.

In the church of San Nicolò di Bari were transferred from the Roman catacombs the remains of Saint Faustina, transport attributed to Maratti; works of the painter are preserved in the churches of Santa Faustina and the Immaculate Conception.
The medieval living room.
The Liberty Reclamation Pumps Room, a monument of industrial archaeology, and the Civic Museum in the church of San Domenico with Scarsellino and Garofalo.

Ancient farmhouse of Strombiano, central building of the Ecomuseo, with intact interiors: the wood-covered stove and the open fireplace kitchens illustrate the evolution of the peasant living; on the whole also the permanent weaving laboratory Rigouts.

In 1604 Camillo de Lellis, at the invitation of the University, decided to establish here a convent of his Order, completed in 1615 by seven masons from Rome, probably on a project by Francesco and Orazio Torriani; it is brick with stone cantonals. Came to the Commune in 1809, he returned to the Camillians in 1819. The shrine preserves a polychrome and golden wooden bust of the saint. Touring hours: 7.30-12.30 and 15.30-19 (daylight saving time until 7.45).

On a rocky spur under control of the mouth of the Judicarians, it is probably the "castrum de summo lacu" mentioned in 1086; from the thirteenth century it was a fief of the Counts Lodron, who held it until the twentieth century, and with the arrival of the gunpowder became a small Renaissance fortress in granite of the quarries of Daone. Fallen in ruins, it was purchased in the fifties and restored; today it is of the Municipality and is open to the public, with door nailed on drawbridge and courtyard semicircle towards the valley. You can only reach it on foot: about 15-20 minutes by dirt road from the parking lot on the Baitoni-Bondone road, or 20-30 minutes by path from Baitoni (Miralago parking).
Fabrian art in a Gothic hospital.
A fragment of the medieval walls.

Medieval village of Mandrolisai, on the south-western slopes of Gennargentu, with the urban installation of the Catalan era and the low granite houses; portrait by the Spanish and Sardinian painters of the early twentieth century, today collected in the MAMA museum, has the Gothic-Catalan parish church of Sant'Antioco and is land of Mandrolisai wine.
A fresco of Mithras underground.
The Doric temple intact in a wild landscape.
The castle of bishop princes.
The viewpoint next to the Duomo.
The peasant civilization and wine in a cellar of Franciacorta.

Sanctuary on Mount Falerzio, born in 1485 when the pastor Gabriel, after a dream related to the Virgin, had an altar built in a cave and became a hermit; followed the chapel, a small church with three naves, the hermitage and then a church on the rock above with the bell tower. Recto da hermiti e poi dai Camaldolesi, was closed in 1807, rebuilt at the end of the 19th century and bought in 1913 by the Badia di Cava. In the cave frescoes with the Virgin, the Annunciation and the Last Supper; on Pentecost Monday is the destination of a pilgrimage with traditional songs and dances.
Built in 1850 on a project by the architect Giuseppe Maggiore, in the town. It is appreciated for its stuccoes and decorations in Corinthian style.
The path of the chamois.
Tower built in the 15th century in the center of the village; once used as a prison, today hosts cultural events.

Olbia became Roman with the conquest of Sardinia and in the imperial age it was a commercial center and naval base. The forum was located in the area of the current town hall, near the port: a stretch of the original pavement is visible at the intersection between via Dante and corso Umberto I. The Carthaginian walls are partly visible in Via Torino; in the ancient port, in Via D'Annunzio, the remains of the Roman port and the wrecks of 24 boats were found.
A theatrical season in a vintage building.

Medieval village founded in Lucca, with a single road that spirals up the hill to the archaeological area of the Fortress; among the main places the Collegiate, the Clock Tower, the tunnels of the underground city, the Civic Museum of Blessed Diana Giuntini and the Casa Carducci, where the poet lived when he was young.

Natural sites equipped with picnic areas under the village: on summer evenings the lights of the village are reflected on the artificial lake of San Pietro, and the unspoilt environment houses the nesting of the rare black stork.
The weaving by hand that won medals in Europe.
Born around the monument to Winckelmann, killed in Trieste in 1768, with finds from Egypt, Cyprus, Greece, Magna Grecia and Etruria and a small collection of Mayan ceramics.
The Museum of Sacred Art of the Diocese of Trivento, inaugurated in 2001, preserves works from the 14th to the 19th century, including wooden statues and sacred vestments.
See the cockpits of Fratte Rosa on the lathe.
It'll be around in a few minutes.

Set up in the halls of the municipal palace, he tells the Monferrato through ten immersive stations led by the figure of Cardinal Massaja and panels with QR code on his life until the African years. A second room presents a path between Romanesque and Baroque Alfierian churches, the music of Giovanni Battista Polledro and Monferrato figures such as Giuseppe Govone, Umberto Cagni, Giacomo Bove, Cosma Manera and Giovanni Pastrone. Open for parties and events and always by reservation (tel. 0131 996603).

Managed by the Istituto Internazionale di Studi Liguri, it occupies ten rooms (a multimedia one) on the second floor of the Palazzo del Parco and traces in chronological order the human presence between Capo Berta and Capo Cervo, from the bronze age (XVIII century B.C.) to the late antiquity and the first barbaric invasions that led to the birth of Diano Castello on the hill. The fifth hall is dedicated to ancient routes, goods and means of transport; the wreck of a ship Â"a doliaÂ" sunk in the middle of the first century AD in the Gulf of Dianese stands out. There are also the archaeological sections "Lucus Bormani" , Risorgimento "Andrea Rossi" and mineralogical "De Cavero" . Winter time: Mar 9-14; mer-ven 9-12 and 15-17; Sat 10-12 and 15-17; in summer evening openings Mer and Fri 21-23; closed Sun and Mon. Tel. 0183 497621.
In the hamlet of Torrepaduli, less than a kilometer from Ruffano, a well-kept museum of rural civilization occupies the halls of Palazzo Pasanisi.

Mining village born in 1864 on the Costa Verde, among the sites of the Park Geominerario of Sardinia: the Henry Gallery, crossed by train overhanging the sea, the mine of Malfidano, the memory of the slaughter of miners of 4 September 1904 and, to the south, the beach of Cala Domestica with the Spanish tower.

Opened in 1882 in the neoclassical villa Cassis Faraone, re-assembled in 2018 on the Roman city: mosaics such as the unsaved floor, the Pudica Venus, portraits and the Giulio-Claudio statuary cycle, with stone galleries, historical garden and deposits open to visitors with over 5,000 artifacts.
caution in case of flood of the stream (Valchiavenna)

Piazza Tasso, the living room of the city with the statue of Torquato Tasso, can be reached from Corso Italia a few steps from the station. Palazzo Veniero (XIII century, late Byzantine style), Palazzo Correale (XIV century, Catalan style) and the loggia of Vico Galantariaro (XV century, Aragonese age) are located in the Vico di Santa Maria della Pietà.
Founded in 1703, a place of Marian devotion, with interiors with elaborate decorative details and luminous frescoes of sacred scenes.
More than 650 meters below the Hospital of Ceppo, where the river Brana flowed: the longest underground path in Tuscany, accessible also to those with disabilities.
The living room under the arcades.
Hundreds of graves in the rock.
A page of the anti-French uprising.

Alpine village at 1,753 meters in the Valley of Viso, with wooden and stone huts with medieval origins overlooking the stream; long isolated and linked to agriculture and breeding, he was struck by Nazi reprisals in the Second World War. View of the Ortles-Cevedale and Adamello groups; it is a base of excursions to the plain of Ercavallo.

Borgo della Marsica on the slopes of Monte Civita, with Piazza dell'Obelisco, the Doge's Palace of the Orsini with frescoes, the church and cloister of San Francesco and, outside the village, the sanctuary of Santa Maria dell'Oriente with the Eastern Museum.
2 hours and more
The heart of the village of the Gardenian carving.

The 14th-century crenellated tower of the walls, on the south-east side towards Todi; it houses a collection of local relics with ancient weapons, noble coats of arms, cadastral maps of the late 18th and early 19th centuries, Roman finds and an autograph letter of Garibaldi from 1862. From the top you can see Todi and the Middle Valley of the Tiber.
A Sienese triptych on the Dauni mountains.
The autonomous parish.

Borgo della Riviera spezzina at the gates of the Cinque Terre, with the ancient village surrounded by medieval walls, the 13th century Town Loggia, the Gothic church of Sant'Andrea with white and green bands, the convent of the Annunziata, a long seafront with beaches loved by surfers and the promontory of Punta Mesco towards Monterosso.

Objects and photographs chronologically ordered from about 1850 to the end of the fifties: branches, pitchers and jars in terracotta, grinders, irons in coal, plow, shoemaker's counter, pails, cones and spindles, a room that reconstructs a domestic interior, a mantle from mourning of 1900 and clothes in broom fiber. Among the documents the first identity card of 1902, the year of municipal autonomy.
The lake to live on foot or by boat.
Reachable with a path, it holds an image of the Assumption; from the square you dominate the entire Gulf of the Cinque Terre. It is the departure of the Via dei Santuari.

Born in 1449 on the concession of Alessandro Sforza, it is one of the largest in Emilia-Romagna: about 200 benches every Sunday (except Easter and Christmas), with the agricultural market AgriCultura at 0 km in Piazza Garibaldi. Three fairs a year: Spring Fair (May), September Fair and San Martino Fair (November).
Of ancient Lombard origin, it rises on the homonymous hill and is dedicated to the Madonna: it preserves a sixteenth-century wooden statue of the Madonna della Cintola and remarkable frescoes.
The tree-lined promenade along the Adige that embraces the center, with the "regasts," ancient stone barriers built to defend the city from the floods.

The village is located in the south of the Fiastra stream, with the historic centre almost intact, except for the area near Porta Pia near the castle, modified in the 1980s of the twentieth century; in the thirteenth century the free municipality entered the orbit of the castles of Fermo. Along the winding streets the noble houses retain architectural elements for pressing the grapes and boiling the must in large copper boilers.
Woods and traces of a ducal road.
30 min
The Baron's house and modern art.

The house-museum designed by Fortunato Depero, restored by Renato Rizzi: on three floors about 3,000 objects including paintings, posters, furnishings, puppets and tarsias in cloth sewn by his wife Rosetta, with The procession of the great doll of 1920.
The symbol of Italy worldwide.

Museum run by the village committee of Cologna, dedicated to chestnut as raw material and food: it retraces the cycle of chestnut (collection, drying, processing and food uses) and the trades related to the wood. An open-air walk in the village touches a metato, a carbonaia and a straw hut. Open on holidays 15-18, closed in winter.
One of the oldest mosaics in the South.

Founded in 1146 by the Cistercians on a previous Benedictine settlement; the Latin cross basilica was built between 1305 and 1335, while the cloister, completed in 1268 according to the inscription on the north side, is older than the church; the Romanesque bell tower is the oldest structure of the complex, and cloister of the Abbot and loggia are of the sixteenth century. It preserves the sandstone statue of Our Lady of the Sacred Chalice (VI-VII century, attributed to the Nubian art) in the neo-Gothic wooden altar of 1921, the fresco "Madonna" with Child and Saints" by Francesco da Milano (1527) and a wooden Baroque crucifix. Open every day 7-12 and 14.30-19; no groups during the functions; guided tours through the abbey's fathers (tel. 0438 970231).
The violet bloom of October.
The dome you can see from the sea.

Wanted in 1684 by the Venerable Company of the Blessed Sacrament and today museum space; the restoration of 1994 brought to light a fragment of Roman mosaic of the first century believed to come from Carsulae and recovered a Last Supper of the eighteenth century.

The largest and most famous neighborhood of the trulli, with 1,030 dry stone houses and conical roofs according to the UNESCO site: once the most popular district, today almost only dedicated to tourism. In the evening, illuminated trulli create a crib effect.
High altitude pilgrimage with lake and Dolomites.
The findings of Ocriticum before the visit to the site.
Pavarotti in his house, told by his voice.
Statues, frescoes and paintings by Carlo Cane.
The Rucellai castle and then the Acciaioli; the park hosts concerts, shows and exhibitions in summer.
Green and panorama at the top of the city.
On the trail of Mozart's rival.
Borgo Bandiera Arancione della Valle Pesio, between centuries-old chestnuts and fir forests up to the Marguareis massif, with the great Certosa founded in 1173.

It is located in the former prison of Via Trilussa and preserves the historical and archaeological memory of Corato. Since 1 July 2025 it is the center of the Integrated Museum System (with Necropolis of San Magno, Dolmen dei Paladini and Underground Corato), managed by VIVARCH APS with events, workshops, guided tours and temporary exhibitions. Contacts: corato@sistemamuseo.it, tel. +39 080 8720861.

Over three kilometers of wide white granite sand beach, one of the few stretches of the Calabrian coast without intensive construction and not crossed by the railway, with spontaneous vegetation, wildlife and marine lilies; threatened by building projects, has been defended by the mobilization of the Places of the FAI Heart since 2006.

Church of the fourteenth century, probably the first mother church, reached by a double stone staircase; the wooden altar, called the biscuit of the abbess, was traditionally designed by the nuns of the convent.
A kilometer from the village on the stream Scoltenna, stone bridge with donkey back with asymmetrical arches, indicated as the only stone bridge with two arches of Emilia.
Listing in extension: the guide covers 9 of the 18 places of culture recorded by the Ministry of Culture in this municipality, as well as churches, squares and nature.
Romanesque church rebuilt in the fifteenth century, with frescoes.
The city cathedral, a reference point of the route between the historic buildings.
The church of the village.
Nature and sports on the lake.
The most representative monument of the city: an eighteenth-century church and a Gothic-Renaissance palace with a fifteenth-century statue of Ovidio, seat of the Civic Museum and the Costume Museum.
The gravelly handles of the Tagliamento.
historical center, monuments and museums can be visited only partially according to the regional portal
The entrance to the village.
Palace €5 whole; Museo dei Ferri Taglienti from €4 to €7

The church was built between the fifteenth and sixteenth centuries in an elevated position on the remains of the ancient castle, with a nineteenth-century staircase; the worship of the saint was introduced by the Knights of Malta, whose cross remains on the pediment of the high altar. Damaged by the 1638 earthquake, it had a barrel-shaped dome around 1700 and a restoration in 1850; in 1964 it was profoundly modified. At the center of the vault is the Baptism of Jesus of Joseph Count; it preserves pulpit, ancient baptismal font and saintly water.

In the lower part of the village, it was born from a miracle of the seventeenth century: after a flood of Meria the waters deposited a lot of wheat, carried away by a mill, in front of an image of the Madonna with the Child painted on the wall of a vineyard. To welcome the image the archpriest Giovanni Battista Sambuca promoted the construction with the offerings of the community; the interior has a rich Baroque decorative apparatus.
The peasant life of the greenhouses.

The medieval quarter was built in the 10th century on the Greek acropolis, which became an island in 1480 with the cutting of the isthmus: alleys, stairs, palaces on the back and Byzantine walls along Via di Mezzo.

Founded in 1418 by Teodoro II Marquis of Monferrato, in late Gothic, consecrated in 1625 and Franciscan monastery until the Napoleonic age; parish since 1828. It is buried there by Empress Sofia, daughter of Theodorus II and wife of John VIII Paleologist, crowned in 1421 by Basilissa. It preserves a large canvas of the Assumption attributed to the Spanzotti, the altarpiece of San Diego at the Counts Vidua, the funeral monument of Carlo Vidua and an organ Mentasti; the cloister has frescoed lunettes among the oldest in the area.

Country of the Cosentine Coast Chain with the Lakes of Fagnano, the only natural lakes of Calabria, in the Natural Park of Monte Caloria and Natura 2000 site; in the hamlet of San Lauro, overlooking the plain of Sibari, the Palace and the church of San Nicola di Bari.

Stone alleys and ancient houses between churches and palaces; the medieval gate dates back to the middle of the ninth century with the walls and was restored in the second half of the fifteenth century at the behest of Pope Pius II. In Piazza della Rocca, the former 19th-century factory of Palazzo Pannicelli hosts the multimedia tourist office.
The church of the pasta makers, with the frescoed ceiling of 1907.
The 130-metre-long monumental cemetery with 43 blind arches, Roman sarcophagi and the frescoes by Buonamico Buffalmacco, including the Triumph of Death.
Borgo from its origins in the Bronze Age, with the Roman amphitheater dug into the tuff, the Etruscan necropolis, the mitreum and the ancient walls.
Via Tommaso Maier with Renaissance houses, small patrician buildings and ancient churches, including San Carlo, Santa Maria and San Rocco.
A house of literature left intact.

Spa resort of the Val Brembana, symbol of the Belle Époque and Liberty in Lombardy: the Grand Hotel opened in 1904, the Casino, the spas reopened in 2014 and the funicular of 1909 that goes up to the Vetta; in the surroundings the Grotte del Sogno and the cycle path of the Val Brembana.
From 7 January 2026 closed for renovation works, except the halls of temporary exhibitions
The cathedral in the medieval old town, among houses and winding alleys.

Itinerary of the Municipality from viale dei Belgi along bastions and wounds of the municipal park to Porta San Martino, main door before the thirteenth century on the ancient Flaminia, and to the Palombara tower, the oldest defence tower, circular like the Byzantine towers; then Largo Porta Santa Croce, Palazzo Olivieri Benigni, the Water Garden, the Monument to the Fallen of 1925 by Turillo Sindoni, merged with the bronze of the cannons of Vittorio Veneto, and the sixteenth century Porta Nuova, the vault of which was removed in 1929 for the Mille Miglia. One stretch is narrow and steep.
The stone of the Karst.

On a rocky spur at over 1,500 meters, in the area of Mezzana, the Marian complex dates back to about 1700 and includes church, clergy and guardians rooms and pilgrim's house; it houses the wooden statue of the Madonna with Child, which in summer rises in procession from the village. Accessible on foot, by bike or by car; open from early June to mid-September.
A fortified village with views of the Spoletina valley.

On the rocky spur of the ancient Turris Paola, built in 1086 by Goffredo di Conversano: Benedictine monastery, then hospital of the Giovanniti and feud of the Knights of Malta until the early twentieth century; walls, moat, mast, a Romanesque church and a rock sanctuary. Today it is privately owned (family de Bellis): visits to check.
The relics of the poet's villa, just a few steps from the excavations.
The Futurism of Doctors in Church.

Iron and fluorite mine opened in 1886 and closed in 1972, among the first realizations of industrial archaeology museum of the valley. A small train leads to the heart of the mountain, then you walk along with the guides for about 700 meters of tunnels between the explosive's reserve, the room of the geodes covered with crystals, the altar of Santa Barbara and the system of the flying machine; silhouettes of miners and visual reproductions and sound animate the side galleries. The visit (about 1 hour and 30) includes the external museum with exhibitions, exhibits and the Mine Archive; inside there are about 12 °C and 95% humidity, serving warm clothes and closed shoes.
The village of Dino Campana and the chestnuts, with piazza Le Scalelle, the Teatro degli Animosi of the eighteenth century and the church of San Lorenzo with the paintings of the Master of Marradi.

The Etruscan shrine of Pyrgi dates back to the 6th century BC and included temples dedicated to Eileithyia-Leukothea, Apollo and Uni; there were found gold sheets in Etruscan and Phoenician- Punic. Above part of the Etruscan city arose after the third century BC a rectangular Roman fortress in polygonal work, used until the V-VI century A.D. The Antiquarium, near the sanctuary, preserves the materials of over forty years of excavation.

In the eighteenth century Palazzo Baldari, used by the Bourbons as an armory, tells Métauros, a settlement founded by the people of Zancle (Messina) and passed in the sixth century BC under the influence of Locri. Most of the finds come from the necropolis excavated along the coast (VII-V century B.C.); also exhibits funerary furnishings of Roman age (II-III century A.D.) and medieval and Renaissance ceramics. Re-opened on October 11, 2024 after the restoration of the palace.
Small center of the Iblei at 760 meters, rebuilt in Baroque style after the earthquake of 1693, known for the museum spread
Ancient northern gate of the city, built in 1290 with sandstone blocks recovered from the ancient Tharros; 28 meters high, now isolated in the center of Piazza Roma, is the stop of the Sartiglia.

Late-Gothic church consecrated in 1489 on an earlier Romanesque church, symbol of the village, with the 67-metre-long bell tower covered with larch stairs; in the apse frescoes by Ruprecht Potsch (1498) and paintings by David Solbach (1578). Nearby stands the Ciasa Soldà, national monument of the sixteenth century.

The main center of the Upper Stura Valley, dominated by the Albertino Fort wanted by Carlo Alberto (1834-1847); from its territory you climb to the Sanctuary of Sant'Anna, at 2,035 meters, starting point of the tour of the alpine lakes, and you reach the thermal baths of Bagni di Vinadio.
The fish from the lake at the table.
Walk among the nuts of the Bleggio.

The two historic buildings on the lakefront house the municipal offices; the atrium is frescoed by Angelo Landi and under the porch that unites them there are ancient coats of arms and memorial plaques.
Building of the early twentieth century, already Palassiu and House of the Proletariat (1920-22).
The sunset from the dock.
Byzantine mosaics a stone's throw from the Four Songs.
The Duke's private rooms and his long gallery.
Short route (1.5 km, about 30 minutes, suitable for all) from Barchi Sottana (664 m) to a knife of quartz rock (893 m) on whose top remain the ruins of a stone watch tower tied with live lime.
The sanctuary of the village reported by Touring.
Our Lady of the Rosary in the Castle.

Built in 1801 on a project by the architect Lucatelli and financed by a company of families from Treais, with wooden stages; the curtain painted by Silverio Copparoni in 1865 represents the battle of Vallesacco. Visits are booked through Pro Loco.
Built on the remains of the medieval castle, center of shops and cafes.
The Cathedral on the ancient temple.
An octagon attributed to Bernini.
The shrine-fortress overlooks the valleys.
The smallest village in the Matterhorn valley, five hamlets at 1650 meters between forests, rascards and greniers, with eight mills lined up on the slope.
The frescoes of the lady of Dante.
The 200 Asti.

Baroque church designed by Gerolamo Buniva and built between 1760 and 1770, with wooden choir behind the main altar. It preserves an organ of the fifteenth century, one of the oldest of the Pinerolese, inserted among the seven organs to be saved of the provincial project "Organalia" .
The church at the top of the village.

Every Wednesday, from morning to late afternoon, more than 350 stalls occupy the streets of the center and the lakefront: it is indicated as the most important market in the area of Lake Maggiore. The market privilege was granted to the Rusca accounts by Emperor Charles V on September 5, 1541.

Set up in the historic factory where the brand was born in 1921, with a new wing of 3,000 square meters from which you can see the current assembly lines, exhibits more than 160 series motorcycles, sports, prototypes and restored engines. Among the unique pieces the first bike built by Carlo Guzzi in 1919, the only one signed G.P. (Guzzi-Parodi), the Otto Cylinders 500 of 1957 by Giulio Cesare Carcano, Norge of 1928, the Guzzi 4V of 1924, the 350 World Champion in 1955 and the V7 record of the 19 record speeds in Monza in 1969; sections on cinemas, races, travels and military and police vehicles.
Medardo Rosso and Sassu in a 16th century building.
Stone alleys on the ravine.

In the area of Sant'Alessandro, about 800 meters from the port: little more than 200 meters of pebbles and sand, partly free and partly equipped, sheltered and with seabed that gradually descends. You can walk from the hill of Sant'Alessandro, from the Olympic Bank or by taxi boat.

Monument to the fallen of the two world wars, 5 meters high: the first, erected in 1919-1920, was destroyed in the Second World War; the current (1972) has a high base with the plaque of names and a bezel with helmet between branches of laurel and oak, surmounted by the marble statue of a soldier in combat by the sculptor Alberto Sparapani.
The palace of taste.
The dome of majolica on the historic center.

Inaugurated in 1995, it collects the finds of Entella: the casts of the famous decrees of Entella, bronze tablets inscribed; ceramics from prehistory to the fourth century B.C., including an amphora of the VII century B.C. with plastic and geometric decoration; the materials of the granary and necropolis with the reconstruction in real scale of a Hellenistic burial; the medieval phase, the daily life and the finds of the sanctuary of Demeter and Kore of contrada Petraro. In the final hall of the barn, amphorae, epigraphs and coins.

Fortress of the Doria and court residence, probably built in the 13th century (the tradition indicates 1102) with the name of Castelgenovese to control the routes to Genoa; it was for some years residence of Brancaleone Doria and Eleonora d'Arborea. Taken by the Aragonese in 1448, which extended its towers and bastions, it became Aragonese Castle until the eighteenth century. Today, the museum occupies nine rooms on two levels with objects woven into vegetable fibers of Sardinia and the Mediterranean, including the junk boat on fassoi, baskets, sieves and bridles.
The sacred treasures of the sanctuary, a stone's throw from the frescoes of Annigoni.

The ancient church of the Hermits transformed between 1659 and 1663 into the Pantheon Atestinum, with stuccoes, coffered ceiling, the Madonna of Tommaso da Modena and the Terracotta Deposition of Antonio Begarelli.

Three-nave Gothic church built around the year 1000 on the remains of a Roman temple dedicated to Ceres (or Bona), of which remains the fishbone floor; it preserves statues and ancient frescoes, a plaque dedicated to Helvia, priestess of Ceres, and a bas-relief that portrays it during a rite.

Symbol of the city, is a Romanesque-Gothic building of the fourteenth century in brick, with an elaborate Gothic façade linked to Bartolino da Novara, which painted it at the end of the fourteenth century; the interior with three naves is described by Italia.it as a sort of small museum of sacred art, with paintings especially of the sixteenth and seventeenth centuries. In the chapel of the right aisle there is the large table of Cerano with the Crucifixion with the Magdalene and the Saints Ambrose and Lorenzo; there are then the fifteenth-century Polyptych of St. Joseph of Lorenzo of Mortara, wooden crib with 80 bas-relief figures, the Madonna of the Rosary by Gerolamo Giovenone and works by Bernardino Lanino and Julius Cesare Procaccini.

The city of Juliet on the handle of the Adige, a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 2000 for Roman monuments merged with the art of Scaliger and Renaissance: the Arena, the squares, Castelvecchio and San Zeno.
Set up in the church of San Giuseppe, it contains sacred silvereries, paintings and liturgical vestments of different eras and workshops from the cathedral and the churches of the territory.
Industrial archaeology between gorges and woods.
Latin sailboat built in 1925 and re-launched in 2021, witness to the leuds with which goods were transported in Liguria.
The cargo of a Roman ship found at the beach.
Sea at the mouth of the river.
The most populous neighborhood of Villa San Giovanni, where you can swim in the narrowest point of the Strait of Messina.
Visitable only by reservation required or during events of the Reserve (tel. 0776 8887276, 331 6728772)
Romanesque church of the historic center, on the path that goes up towards the castle.
Dante's friend's house.
A century of Val d'Alpone wine in a farmhouse.
Long porticoes of the historic center among the places not to be missed.
Umbriatourism: the museum is currently closed to the public
A walk between buildings and ancient walls.
The oratory to visit next to the castle.
A Sardinian primacy and the Logudorian epigraphs.
Small church of the convent of the Clarisse, with a Neapolitan majolica floor and a wooden work of the eighteenth century.

On the first floor of the Long Channel of the castle, it exhibits more than 1,200 exhibits in four rooms, from prehistory to the Roman age, with illustrated panels and a large archaeological map of the Lomellina. Open on Sundays; on other days visits by reservation with at least 15 days in advance for schools and groups.
A Sabauda church with the original organ of 1844.

Borgo sul'Oglio entered the Gonzaga domains in 1414, in the Regional Park of Oglio Sud; to see the sixteenth-century castle with the remains of the synagogue, the parish church of San Michele Arcangelo with the paintings of the Chiaveghino and the parish church of San Gaudenzio rebuilt by Vespasiano Gonzaga.
The only two-story trullo.

Mother church with fifteenth-century portal and quadrangular bell tower with helical stone staircase; Baroque interior with wooden statue of the patron saint and stone stove dated 1600. Patron celebration on August 10.
MiC card (updated in 2020) indicates "Closed" every day; contacts 348 8057383
The historic heart of the country.

Doric Temple dedicated to Hera, on the right bank of the Bradano about three kilometers from the ancient city: there are 15 of the 32 original columns, 10 on the north side and 5 on the south side; dug in 1926 and restored in 1961, in the Middle Ages it was called "Mensae Imperatoris."

Centro dell'Alpe Cimbra marked by the Great War, with the Austro-Hungarian forts of Supreme High and Cherle and the military cemetery, and by the Cold War with the Base Thunder missile base; among the hamlets the eighteenth-century Maso Spilzi, the sanctuary of the Madonna delle Grazie and Guardia, the painted country.
The most intact barbaric village.

One of the best known places in Pinasca, with waters appreciated also by those who come from afar to draw them; the first official documents on the source date back to the early twentieth century. The name recalls the bear, common in the valleys until the nineteenth century, and a legend on a bear that went down every evening to drink; in 1933 an attempt of the podestà to divert the water towards the town hall failed after the letter of a young woman from the village to Mussolini.
Sacred art, especially sculptures and paintings from the 15th to the 18th century, with rooms of contemporary art; visits by reservation.
The post-macchiaiola Livorno painting.

Collection on emigration and work in mines, especially in Belgium but also in Brazil and Italy: tools, helmets, lamps, a track with vagoncini, ventilation tubes of galleries, photos and samples of minerals, with recordings of former miners, documentaries on life in mines and Marcinelle and documents of the Italian Association Ex Minatori. Visits on request.
The mountain house of a prince bishop born in Anterivo.
Built in 1761, with stuccoes, paintings on the life and miracles of the saint, a fresco on the ceiling and a wooden statue on the high altar.
A walled village to walk between castle and churches.
Over 120 hectares along the Fiora: the walls in tuff of the IV century BC with five doors, the Great Temple, the domus with mosaics and necropolis, including the François tombs and the Inscriptions.
Sunny hill of orchards and vineyards 3 km from Aosta, with the castle of the Counts Passerin d'Entrèves and a fifteenth-century crucifix among the masterpieces of the Val d'Aosta.
Walk inside the walls of a Messapian city of 2500 years ago.
The walk on the sea and the fishing village.
Documented already in the IX century and substantially transformed since 1642, it rises near the Naviglio; in 1998 a new bronze portal and a new altar were placed.
Excursions and horses on the Catria.
The square of the sanctuary.
Nun desserts.
The Gothic church among the stages not to be missed in the historic center.
15th century convent with a loggia of forty arches; it houses a baroque processional vara in silver by the Juvarra, Messinian silversmiths.
Formicle city of engraving.
Parish church consecrated in 1488, with Romanesque bell tower, completed by Federico Borromeo in the seventeenth century: six paintings by Morazzone and a polyptych by Gaudenzio Ferrari in 1511.
The Sardinian black truffle.
The tour of the castle walls.

It is located in the seventeenth-century former church of Saints Mary and Jesus of Borgo Cerreto and is dedicated to the doctor and surgeon Baronio Vincenzi, lived in Cerreto between the end of the sixteenth and the beginning of the seventeenth century; in the catalogue of the Ministry of Culture is registered as Mummies Museum of Borgo Cerreto.
Collections of a nineteenth-century benefactor of the country.
The culture of the Apuans.
The palace of the Florentine vicar (1306), with the facade covered with coats of arms also Robbiani, and the Museum of knives of Scarperia with the workshop of the knifemaker.
A Byzantine fresco of the fourteenth century.
The walls of an Italian town overlooking the Majella.

Born around 1600 as Casino Cesi, it was bought in 1648 by Camillo Pamphilj who expanded it to the present form; it preserves a cycle of frescoes by Pier Francesco Mola. In 1697 the pontifical court of Innocent XII stayed there, of which the coat of arms remains.
The history of the village and its procession.
The four-metre stele, symbol of the park.
The glazed terracotta of Benedetto Buglioni.
In Stia the steep square surrounded by beautiful palaces; between Stia and Pratovecchio, in Via Londa, the park where in summer you take a bath in the Arno.
The English garden of Russell Page.
Typical taverns in the alleys of the center, called by the name or nickname of the owners (such as "a dua Sarbaturu" or "a dua Cicciu") where the local wine is served in the traditional cup.
From sea to crater.

From the square of the hamlet of Raino, on the southern side of Mount Fusco, the CAI 949 trail climbs to the sanctuary in about 3.5 km and 370 m of difference in altitude (one hour and a half) between terraced olive groves of Itrana, dry walls, stations of the Via Crucis and, in the final section, a holm oak wood.

Borgo della Valdichiana aretina who lived his golden season between the fifteenth and sixteenth centuries with the family Di Monte and Pope Julius III: along Corso Sangallo the Palazzo Di Monte di Antonio da Sangallo the Old, the Logge dei Mercanti di Nanni di Baccio Bigio and the Palazzo Pretorio with the civic tower; then the Cassero Senese with the ceramic museum, the church of Santa Chiara with the shovels of Andrea Sansovino and the former synagogue of the ghetto.
closed from 5 October 2026 for redevelopment work, reopening scheduled in spring 2027

The large crenellated building that dominates the village was the fortified residence of the counts of Caldonazzo: Visit Trentino traces its origins around the Mille, the card of the APT given the building in 1319. Justice was administered there, trials were held and the tithes of the peasants were preserved; the wall towards the church has blackbirds tailed by swallows, ghibellines. Today it hosts events, a riding school and stables.
The history of cast iron in an old foundry.
The 11th century Romanesque building overlooking the two medieval districts, with interior decorations of different styles.
A Liberty Theatre in the heart of the country.
A balcony on the olive groves to the sea.

One of the few original cylindrical bell towers left, of the 11th century, 48 meters high and slightly inclined to the east; it recalls Ravenna models of Byzantine tradition with Romanesque elements and for centuries has been a watchtower over the sea. Recently restored, you can visit by reservation; from the top you can see the sea and the lagoon and in summer you can also climb in the evening, at sunset.

Founded in 1977 in the former dormitories, library and scriptorium of the monastery, it is one of the major ethnographic museums in Italy: about 12,000 objects of peasant life, rural crafts and devotion, graphic and painting works by local artists of the twentieth century, a collection of puppets and ancient puppets, an archaeological section and a collection of Padan farm wagons.
Where the Black is born.

Pieve of the middle of the 11th century, recently restored, in the heart of the village with a balcony-square overlooking the river, suggestive at sunset; according to the tradition Sant'Antonino, patron saint of Piacenza, would have been martyred in Travo in 303.

Village at 633 meters on the ridge with 360 degrees views of the Apennines, stone underpasses and portals of 1694 and 1770; the church of Saints Peter and Paul, documented from the thirteenth century, has for bell tower a medieval tower of the ancient fortress, where the legend places the golden cast of Matilde di Canossa. Near the oratory of the Madonna di Montalto, before 1300, and on a hill to the west the seventeenth-century oratory of the Nativity of Mary, called "della Formice" for the swarms of winged ants that manifested there every three years about.

Built between 1833 and 1838 at the behest of Emperor Francis I of Austria and inaugurated by Ferdinand I, it was the largest construction site in Europe at the time, with 3,500-5,000 workers, about 20 million bricks and 250,000 cubic metres of granite. Never besieged, soon lost strategic importance and was a warehouse of weapons and barracks until 2003; opened to the public since 2005, it hosted the biennial Manifesta 7 and the provincial exhibition of 2009. Over 65,000 square meters it is divided into lower and upper forts, connected by an intermediate level and an underground staircase of 452 steps; inside a neo-Gothic church of the garrison and a provincial museum with the history of the fort, including the gold treasure of the Italian national bank hidden here in the Second World War.

The village was born around the medieval castle, of which there are visible traces; in the village the church of San Francesco di Paola (of the Blessed Crucifix), next to the former convent of the Minimi friars that now houses the municipal seat.
A waterfall a few steps from the center.

The bridge over the Ovesca stream, on the ancient Via Francisca, has a history of collapses and reconstructions: a contract for a bridge with three arches in 1442, the great flood of 1588 that buried the crypt of Santa Maria del Piaggio, the reconstruction with two arches of 1627. In 1800, with the Napoleonic road of the Sempione, it was enlarged with a new arch flanked; until 1930 the road of the Sempione passed only from here.

Historic center declared National Monument in 1965, with palaces and noble residences from the 11th to the 18th century, rebuilt for anastylosis after the earthquakes of 1976. Among the buildings: Casa Marcurele, the oldest (XI century, Romanesque), the fourteenth-century Palazzo degli Scaligeri, Palazzo Zinutti (13th century) with wrought iron balcony, Casa Calderari (14th century) which houses the tourist office and Palazzo Radiussi with Gothic-Vezian trifora.
It keeps the simulacrum of Christ used in the rites of Holy Week, s'Iscravamentu and s'Incontriu.
A brief exit to the country to the church of the holy doctors.

Inside the 15th century walls, cobbled alleys with stone portals; in Piazza della Podesteria an octagonal fountain, the seventeenth-century Latin Palace, recently restored, and the Villino Latini.
A scientific garden next to the Ducal Garden.
Romanesque and frescoes not to be missed.

Church recently renovated, perhaps of pre-Romanesque origin, with traces of Carolingian and frescoes of the fourteenth and fifteenth centuries; it is reached leaving the provincial 513 to Rosano, about three kilometers before Castelnovo in the mountains.
A private collection of vintage bikes curated and restored by those who collected it.

The hilly village of Teramano known for the abbey of Santa Maria di Propezzano, linked to a Marian apparition of 715, and for the fourteenth-century church of San Salvatore in the center of the village.
The summit of the Fammera with sea view.

Of Norman origin (gate and two monofores on the right side), rebuilt in the fourteenth century and restored in Baroque forms in 1690. It preserves the triptych of the Madonna and Child attributed to Rogier van der Weyden, who arrived in Sicily at the end of the fifteenth century after a shipwreck, works of Giuliano de Matta and of the Zoppo di Gangi, a Virgin of Giuliano Mancino of 1508, the sarcophagus of Domenico Gagini in the chapel of San Gandolfo and, in the Treasury, the silver urn of the saint and a monstrory of Niblio Gagini (1586).

The original building dates back to the 12th century; it was rebuilt in the 18th century and has a neoclassical 19th century façade. During an extension a burial stone was found with relics and parchments that attest to the year of construction. Nearby stands the oratory of Santa Croce (XVI-XVII century), with a red stone façade.
A seventeenth-century villa of the Richini that incorporates the old castle.
A Romanesque church with works of the sixteenth century Marche.
The great Romanesque-Gothic parish in terracotta.
The center of jazz music in a park of about 2.5 hectares open from sunrise to sunset.
The Museum of the Puglia Region traces the history of Salento from prehistory to Messapian civilization.

Consecrated in its present form in 1521 (an earlier church has been documented since 1234); the 1520 stained glass windows depict scenes of the miners' life. Altars of 1884 and 1903, pulpit of 1867, Madonna of the Baroque Rosary of about 1700 and the canvas of the stoning of St. Stephen by Franz Sebald Unterberger; the neo-Gothic decoration of the vault followed the fire of 1900.

Two churches on the same site, each with its own bell tower: the old San Lorenzo, attested in the parish church of Porlezza in the 13th century and became parish church in 1575 by the will of Carlo Borromeo, who visited it in 1582; and, little down, the new parish church, which preserves a altarpiece of the 16th century and a fifteenth-century statue of San Lucio from the oratory of the pass.
One of the best preserved deposits of Pliocene fossils in Liguria.

Complex with church and bell tower in Romanesque style, built in three phases and born to welcome abandoned children, for the impulse of Father Ciro Soccio, remembered by a bronze monument in front of the cemetery. Inside a dome illuminates the frescoed presbytery; in a canopy the seventeenth-century statue of the Virgin and on the altarpiece the Last Supper in high relief.
The ancient canal that connected Modenese to the Adriatic, fed also by spring waters; along the banks runs a bike route and run about 3 km towards Bomporto.

Country of the Lower Monferrato in the Versa valley, about 10 km north of Asti, dominated by the castle of the Counts Amico, transformed into a Baroque residence by Benedetto Alfieri, with the museum 'L Ciar in the underground; in the territory the Romanesque Madonna della Snow and, in Serra Perno, the Roseto della Surpresa with over 500 botanical roses. Here he was born in 1774 Giovan Battista De Rolandis, creator of the Tricolor.
Beach in the village with view of lighthouse, tower and St. Peter.
The traditional life of Bagolino.

Wood with seven tombs of giants, a megalithic tomb, 17 nuraghi and ten Nuragic villages, where at the beginning of July the saint's feast is held; from the park a path leads to the waterfall of Sothai, formed by the Flumendosa that pours into the canyon of Bau Vigo.
About ten narrow tunnels between rocks overhanging, for about 650 meters total, humid and rich in mosses, ferns and wildlife. The source recommends the guided tour.
Duke's residence of the sixteenth century in rectangular stone, with windows in Gothic style; the side watch tower is now clock tower.
Monument to the fork for Salt and Guazzora, formed by granite blocks with a stylized brain and a marble slab with a song by Bandello dedicated to Castelnuovo.
The eight-nineteenth-century face of the country.

The 14th-century Palazzo Pretorio, in the historic centre, 3 km from the mine, houses the Documentation Centre of the Museum of Mines. The first floor is dedicated to the copper mine of Camporciano, the second to the mineral richness of the valley, with salt on copper, salt, alabaster, geothermal and limedonia.

Faithful reconstruction of typical environments of rural houses, renewed and expanded, with tools of peasant work, objects of daily use, the work cycles of the baker and lumberjack set up on original wooden structures and photographic documentation.

A village walled on the Fiastra valley, heir to the Roman colony of Urbs Salvia, whose archaeological park of about 40 hectares is considered the most important and spectacular of the Marches; on top of the village dominates the Fortress, completed in 1507.
Shells, flowers and a large botanical garden on the sea.

Holiday center at 447 meters in a basin above the Enza, in the Reggiano Apennines, with the parish church of San Lorenzo mentioned in 1142; the territory is a mosaic of medieval villages linked to the Da Palù (Dalla Palude), lords loyal to the Canossa, from Legoreccio to Gottono, Crovara, Pineto and Spigone, crossed by the Path of the Ducati and the valleys of the Tassaro and the Tassobbio.

It exhibits Etruscan finds from excavations of the 1950s-1970s and about 600 objects from the rural world. The section "Il Cavallo e l'Uomo" opened in 2002 with audiovisual, dioramas and environmental sounds, tells the relationship between man and horse in the Lazio Maremma: prehistory and protohistory on the first floor, modern age and folklore of the Maremma and the Roman countryside on the lower floor and outside.
A 19th-century workshop just as it was.

Founded in the 8th century and rebuilt in the 10th century as a Benedictine monastery; cloister, church and tomb of the Doria of the 13th century, with the tower of 1562; well FAI reachable only on foot or by sea.
Real shadow in the middle of town.

4,8 km hiking ring (about 2 hours, 250 m of difference in altitude, difficulty E) curated by CAI di Mondovì, starting from the Caudano Caves ticket office: along the water pipeline to the Davì Rock, wall used for climbing, then to the village Crevirola (879 m), with views of the Monregalese to the dome of the Sanctuary of Vicoforte, and return between mule tracks and chestnut trees. Recommended from March to October.
An imperial marble theatre.

A medieval building overlooking the ancient canal port, mentioned in the statues of 1377, with decorations from the XV-XVI century on the first floor; from 1600 Augustinian convent, then hospital and school, was recovered for the Jubilee of 2000 and hosts the Hostalia del Mare hostel, an auditorium and the permanent exhibition of material culture. Opened in 1981, it exhibits about 300 objects of peasant work in six cycles (e.g. tools, vine and wine, mills and mills, breeding, home, games and traditions), with a section on the dialect and reconstruction of the canal port. In the summer open in the evening, 21:30-23:30, on Friday and Saturday (and also on Sunday in the second half of July). Tel. 0187 817776.

Monastic ruins in the woods of Pollino.

Dedicated to San Massimo, the first bishop of Turin, has origins in the first centuries after Christ: the restoration of 1949 revealed a primitive phase of the fifth century, a Romanesque (X-XI century) and a Baroque (XVIII century). He keeps a wooden statue of the saint.

Borgo del Monferrato is dominated by the castle with the chapel of Sant'Andrea, which preserves a large cycle of fourteenth-century frescoes on the life of Christ; in the village 57 sundials and the Romanesque parish church of San Lorenzo, in the hamlets the baroque castle of Colcavagno and the frescoed Romanesque church of Scandeluzzo.
Hesagonal tower of 1476 among the vineyards of the Faenza hills, with panoramic terrace at 360 degrees.
