Begin in 1641 on a project by Martino Longhi, blessed in 1684 and consecrated in 1779, it became a cathedral in 1841 when Gregory XVI raised Poggio Mirteto to a diocese. Facade in brick; inside with three naves rich in stuccoes, with altar in red marble of Cottanello, the altarpiece of the Assunta by Giovanni Baglione (1613), paintings attributed to Giacinto Brandi and Antonio Gherardi and, on the vault, the canvas of Metello Helzel (1931) with Saint Gaetano of Thiene; organ of the brothers Martinelli (1847).
Bathrooms in a Blue Flag lake.

Borgo dell'Alto Molise once called Caccavone, from the "caccavo" , the large copper container for milk processing, medieval fief dei de Petra, de Sabran and Carafa born around a castle in the upper part; to see the mother church of Santa Vittoria and the medieval underground mill of Palazzo Iacovone.

The oldest part was built in 1185 by Jacques de la Porte de Saint-Ours, founder of the lords of Quart; together of buildings within a belt that follows the rocky spur, with the donjon on the highest point.

The medieval village, built under the Normans after the thousand, is a plot of alleys and courtyards with traces of caves. From Piazza Umberto I, one of the largest in Sicily with marble fountain and bronze statues, to Piazzale Angelo, one of the most beautiful views of the Sicilian hinterland; via Giudea recalls the Judia, the district of the medieval Jewish community.

Built in the 13th century on the remains of the oldest fortifications and renovated in the 18th century, it dominates the village from the top of the hill with a high tower and is visible from kilometers in the Alexandrian plain. Ceded in 1180 by the Bellingers to the Municipality of Alexandria, disputed for centuries, infeudated in 1535 to the Milan Press and Sabaudo since 1707; in 1745, during the Battle of Bassignana, Charles Emanuel III fixed the headquarters there, and Charles Albert stayed there in 1842-1843.

Baths transformed into museums, with a tomb of Mycenaean origin; they can be reached with a challenging trekking from the quarries of the Pleasant, passing through the sulfur fumaroles and a geo-park.
The tower of the balivo.

The first museum in South Tyrol dedicated to the ancient Romans: on three floors exhibits finds of San Lorenzo and surroundings on the history of the station of Mansio Sebatum, in the land of the Saevates, from 100 BC to 600 AD, with the results of researches on the Iron and Roman Age and on daily life. Closed on Sundays and holidays.
The Town Hall which was the residence of the Montefeltro.

Among the oldest fortifications in Casentino, it dates back to the 10th century: it belonged to the counts of Chiusi and from 1261 to Ubertini, who kept it almost uninterruptedly until 1830; there was lord Bishop Guglielmino Ubertini, who died in Campaldino in 1289. A driveway between the cypresses leads to the arms square with the bell tower and a bell tower of the fifteenth century; inside the court with frescoes, guard body with the arms of the Ubertini, Room of Arms with coffered ceiling and fireplace in serene stone, baroque chapel, bishop's room and, on the top floor, the room of the judgments with a small prison.
More than 3,000 hectares of meadows and forests: Europe's largest fenced and protected environment, with Borgo Castello and the curious Bizzarria.

Small town of the Val Cavallina on the right bank of the Cherio, about 18 km from Bergamo, gathered around the Castle Giovanelli that houses the Museum of Contemporary Art - Donazione Meli; a popular museum leads to the works of Alberto Meli in the village, to the bas-relief of the Giant carved in the rock by Joshua Meli and, going up, to the sanctuary of St. Anthony and the Prati Alti.

Large area at the castle with picnics, games and sports in a forest of oaks, cherry, birch and ash trees; from here starts a loop bike of over 5 km.
Artificial lake between pine and fir trees with views of Monte Rosa, with playground, summer fishing and winter skating.

18th century church in neoclassical style with longitudinal plan, with three-part bell tower and single nave interior with barrel vault; in façade frescoes with San Michele and San Giovanni. It rises in the center of the village, about 1.5 km from the village.

The largest wine-growing municipality in South Tyrol (941 hectares of vineyards) and the richest area of castles in the province, with more than one hundred castles, noble residences and ruins: above Missiano Castel d'Appiano with the Romanesque chapel called "Cappella Sistina delle Alpi" (Sistine Chapel of the Alps), Castel Boymont and Castel Moos-Schulthaus, in São Paulo the large parish church called "Duomo di campagna" (country dome) and in the wood of Monticolo two emerald green lakes.

One of the great Benedictine monasteries of Veneto, still inhabited by monks.
On the Mascagni Terrace, in front of the Cetacean Sanctuary: reconstructions of marine environments, a dozen tanks, turtles, sharks and tropical fish.

The reserve, established in 1983, covers about 300 hectares between Ceto, Cimbergo and Paspardo and is one of the eight stages of rock art camuna, UNESCO heritage since 1979. In Ceto there is the area of the Foppe di Nadro, with 84 engraved rocks identified, about twenty along the visit: a ring of about 2 km, largely cobbled, between thick surfaces engraved from the 5th millennium BC to the high Middle Ages, with weapons of the Bronze Age and warriors of the medium Iron Age; along the path a Tibetan bridge and, at the entrance, an educational area with simulated excavation and reconstructions of a neolithic hut and a retica house. Simple but not equipped for disabled engines, about 3 hours; starting from the museum of Nadro, with free parking at about 200 m; single ticket - Vale Camonica Pass Engravings is available online.
Four centuries of sacred fabrics in a church in the village.

Area of ecological rebalancing with typical flora and fauna of the Po Valley.

It rises on the site of a medieval oratory dedicated to St. Silvestro Pope (whose stone image is above the door), rebuilt and rebuilt several times in 1909; it houses frescoes from the 15th century on canvas, including the Madonna on the throne with Child, Christ Crucified and St. Anthony Abbot, the venerated image of the Virgin with the Blessed Child and a rich collection of ex-vote. In the historical centre, born as an oratory and modified in the nineteenth century; it houses a wooden crucifix of the fifteenth century considered miraculous and still venerated. The apse was painted by Luigi Agretti, the same painter of the theatre.

The main square brings together the medieval Palazzetto del Podestà, of the fourteenth century, renovated after a fire of 1496 and 1854, Palazzo Lazzarini, the Civic Tower and the nineteenth-century Palazzo Comunale, built on an area purchased by the community in the fourteenth century.

In the hamlet of Quadrelli the church of Santa Maria Assunta is Romanesque; the seventeenth-century church of the Confraternita del Santo Rosario has a trusse ceiling with terracotta tiles decorated with the coat of arms of Cardinal Nicola Canali.

Municipality of Lower Brianza oriental gathered around Palazzo Rasini, villa with two towers and courtyard of honor today seat of the town hall and the miniature Museum of peasant life, and the Romanesque church of Santa Maria in Campo.
A walk under the arcades of the medieval merchant village.
Sacred art at the Seminary of Giovan Biagio Amico.
Large hilly park along the Rhine, connected to San Luca by the Bregoli path.
Natural oasis with marked itineraries for horseback riding or mountain biking on ancient roads of shepherds and disused railways; in the park 11 nuraghi, four villages and two tombs of Giganti.

About 600 hectares of wetlands of fresh water and 100 hectares of forest, with one of the largest colonies of cormorants of Italy; the Museo delle Valli in the Casino di Campotto tells about the reclamation.

The first and only National Museum of the Naïves in Italy was established by the national prize created by Zavattini in 1967; it is located in the fifteenth-century convent of the Augustinians, linked to Rodolfo Gonzaga the first lord of Luzzara, next to the church of the Annunziata, transformed by the Municipality into an exhibition space.
Beach of dunes and the lighthouse of 1928.

Three rooms in a noble palace built by the Bevilacqua family between the late seventeenth and early eighteenth centuries: the first documents the chamois (with two naturalized specimens, panels, footprints and a plastic of the Park), the second documentary project on the Park, the third is dedicated to other protected areas. Outdoors a wildlife area of about 20 hectares with camos in semi-freedom, observed by two belvederi in the upper part of the country. Along the only road of the village there are arcades with arches and pillars of different shapes, closed by the Gate of Neva Bridge and the Gate of Molino flanked by towers.

Final destination of the Don Bosco Way from Turin.

Medieval village (X-XI centuries) with concentric streets connected by stairs, surrounded by walls that had several doors: only Porta San Rocco remains intact, entrance to the historic center. From the village the view reaches the Abbey of Montecassino and the mountains of Abruzzo.

Behind the Sanctuary of Monte Castello, a narrow passage leads to the stone pyramid dedicated to the Garibaldi hero Pilade Bronzetti, who is also tomb of the Garibaldini fallen in the battle of October 1860.

In the village the Town Hall on the main square, the castle of the fourteenth century, the church of Santa Caterina with Gothic portal and Romanesque façade, and the church of Santa Maria, which preserves a fifteenth century Pietà and a baptismal font of the sixteenth century; the Arch of the Finocchioli, rest of the ancient walls, opens onto a viewpoint on the river Campiano.

On the Gennargentu massif, over 1800 meters, the ski lifts of Monte Spada and Bruncu Spina for winter skiing, the only ones of the island according to italia.it; in the summer hiking trails among woods, springs and wildlife reserves.

A symbol of the city, a jewel of Romanesque-Gothic architecture with its façade illuminated by golden mosaics; in the Chapel of San Brizio one of the greatest painting cycles of the Renaissance, begun by Beato Angelico and completed by Luca Signorelli between 1499 and 1504.

About 10 minutes drive from the village: winter ski slopes, trails in the summer woods and an adventure park with suspended trails.

Founded in the 17th century, it is a small tufa building with a hut façade between the Tuscan parasts and the square bell tower with a dome. In the park there is the large sandstone peripteral temple (470-460 BC), whose remains seem to rise from the waters of the Ionian Sea, the House of the Dragon and the Baths of Nannon, house transformed into a bathroom in the fourth century BC with the polychrome mosaic of dragons and dolphins, discovered in 2012 and among the largest in southern Italy. The palace where Giacomo Leopardi was born (1798-1837), still inhabited by the descendants: the rooms where he grew, the library of rare volumes and the room overlooking the house of Silvia.

The prepositural church, now a minor basilica in the historic centre, was built by the Visconti in the 15th century and renovated in the first half of the 17th century by Francesco Maria Richini, who introduced elements of the Roman Baroque; it has rich decorative apparatuses. Opposite is Palazzo Viani Visconti, former residence of the noble Visconti Viani and municipal seat since 1897.
The Etna tour by train.
The pirogues of the Lombard rivers and the frescoes of the refectory of St. Augustine.
The historic capital of the San Martino Valley among palaces and gardens.
A Gothic portal and a Gaginian Madonna.
A museum and a path on the water in the mountains.
A megalithic monument of over three thousand years ago.
The crypt above the Roman baths.
Small fortified village on the Metallifere Hills, born around the abbey founded by St. Walfredo in 754.
The work of fields and tanneries in a Venetian villa.
The medieval village in dark pepper, with the external stairs called proffers, balconies and arches; Monicelli shot scenes of the Brancaleone Army.

In the seventeenth century Palazzo Patigno, since 1927 it has collected fossils of the ancient sea and finds that tell the origins and history of the Colle di San Colombano. The paleontological section includes shells of small molluscs and marine invertebrates, remains of Homo sapiens, the skull of a rhinoceros of steppes, remains of elephant, Bos taurus and Bison priscus; the archaeological one goes from the age of Copper to the Roman, medieval and post-medieval age, with the partial reconstruction of a Roman chamber tomb. Visits by appointment (tel. 0371 2931).
The heart of the village.

Country of the high Marmilla at the foot of Monte Arci, Masullas has in the former convent of the Capuchins the GeoMuseum "Stefano Incani" and the church of San Francesco, in addition to the Romanesque San Leonardo, the oldest in the country. In the territory of the park of Monte Arci there are the forest of Taraxi and the park of the obsidiana of Conca 'e Cannas.

In the recovered buildings of the abandoned village of Castelnuovo dei Sabbioni, it preserves finds and documents of the lignite mine of Valdarno, which during the First World War employed up to 5,000 miners and since 1955 passed from the galleries to the open-air mine. A multimedia path tells the mining history, the transformation of the landscape and the life of the miners; the documentation centre has photos and audiovisuals, with workshops for schools. From the terrace you can see the mining village of Santa Barbara. Free under 12.

It is located in the House of Meridiana, an example of Alpine architecture so called for the solar clock painted on the south façade. It reconstructs the phases of hair processing, a trade that was widespread in Elva in the second half of the nineteenth century: the hair, collected in exchange for little money or for fabrics and scarfs, were worked in the country to make wigs sold also in England and in the rest of Europe. Displays testimonials, photographs and commercial documents; opening to be checked with the Ecomuseum (tel. 340 9846508).

It rises on a rocky spur between the Duina stream and the Ruzola river, just outside the village; cited in documents of the twelfth century, it was long linked to the family from Campo and was rebuilt after a fire in the fifteenth century.
only by reservation (tel. 378 4165988), descent into the forbidden quarries
Doors, towers and baked of a Canavesian recipe.
In the valley of Crèmera, inside the Park of Veio; it preserves a painting of the 13th century of the Madonna and Child and around remain the buildings of the ancient convent.
For lovers of ancient music.
The ancient village overlooking the Conero.
The Church of the Knights of Malta on the hill of the castle.

The parish church of Godego is one of the oldest in the diocese of Treviso; in 1754 Pope Benedict XIV raised it to abbey church on the initiative of Archpriest Nuzio Quirini. Next to the eighteenth-century church was built a larger one in the mid-Twentieth century, designed by architect L. Candiani.

In Pieria's former dairy, the collection collected in thirty years by Odi Gonano: dozens of cameras, cameras and amateur projectors, large projectors of the cinemas of Pesariis, Comeglians, Tolmezzo and Udine restored by the owner and 35 mm professional cameras. Visits on request.

One of the largest ports on the Riviera di Ponente, protected by a long pier with two large docks divided by a pier at . L. L., with marine active all year round; in the port area the small church of the Madonna of Loreto, protector of the sailors.
A reborn monastic complex as a university.
The easiest nuraghe to reach, on the state road to Olbia.
A medieval watchtower over the valley.

Erected around the year 1000 by Giovanni Shinto, lord of Aquino (cited in 1049 as  "Castrum qui nominatur Pika"), he passed to the D'Aquino, the Angioini, the Della Rovere and from 1542 to the Farnese. Today it is largely in ruins over Largo Carbonaro, but some towers are open to visitors, including the one with the Renaissance clock still working.
The heart of the village fliscano in a few steps.

Gorges excavated from the river Verdura among citrus groves and orchards, about 2.5 km from the city and close to the Castle of Poggidiana; from the area you can see the sea of the stretch of coast of Seccagrande.

Castle of medieval origin (around 1340, as shown by the watchtower of Carrara), also called Villa Zaborra from the counts that adapted it to villa in 1775, museum since 1980; during the restorations a Roman spa has emerged. The museum tells the story of the flight from Leonardo's drawings to space exploration with over 300 models of planes, airships and balloons, original uniforms, engines and relics, including the Lindbergh plane for the Atlantic crossing and, in the cellars, the space section with models of the LEM and Space Shuttle Columbia, the Solar Sailing of the University of Padua and the images of the Giotto probe. On the noble floor, the section dedicated to D'Annunzio, which from here took off on 9 August 1918 with the squadron "La Serenissima" for the flight to Vienna: the frescoed rooms where he lived for a year keep original furniture, uniforms and personal objects.
The Redeemer of Mantegna.
The church of origin.
To understand Majella before going up there.
The Lengue Castle.
€3 (6 years); cumulative 4 museums €8, reduced €5
The crypt of the basilica of Constantine.
The residence of the Knights of Malta on the main square.

On the plateau of Chentu Mannas, about 500 meters at the foot of Mount Cuccu, overlooking the coast from Capo Caccia to Capo Marargiu: quadrilobed nuraghe with 15 meters high mastium and two overlapping rooms, covered courtyard, village of about 200 huts of the beginning of the Iron Age (X-IX century BC), tomb of giants in the cork grove, single tower nuraghe Punta 'e su Crabile, two dolmen, menhir and megalithic enclosure with megagon temple. Entrance fee; located 150 meters from the car park on easy path.
Art and archaeology in one complex.
Anzio's landing told by the soldiers.
In the village where the Leopoldino Aqueduct begins, it preserves perhaps the oldest positive octave organ in Tuscany, at the end of the sixteenth century, with the original decorations.

The highest municipality of the Natisone Valleys, on the ridge at the border with Slovenia at the foot of the Kolovrat: villages of rural architecture such as Obenetto and Cras, the small Museum of the rural house in Trinco and the trenches of the third Italian defensive line of the Great War.
Natural area to walk, by bike or boat, between nature, history, art and zero kilometre products.
Municipal building, belonged to Balbi and then to Spinola, which since 1996 also houses the museum of puppets.
Sand, sunsets on the sea and Blue Flag.

Built between 1908 and 1912 at the top of the Cima Campo, at 1,549 meters, called "Padreterno": with the fort Busa Verle was guarding the Vezzena Pass, armed with four bikes in armored domes, two guns and stations for 19 machine guns; in the first days of the Great War it was heavily bombarded and the garrison was close to surrender. You can reach it on foot from the village (path of the Baites, path Cimbri imaginary, path ... From stories to history) or from Malga Millegrobbe; in summer guided tours inside, passing through the Oberwiesen outpost.

Frazione sulla Via Giardini about 10 km from the capital: the church of Sant'Andrea Apostolo, a single nave, designed by Modena engineer Antonio Vandelli incorporating the oldest building, houses the oldest bell in Modena, with the inscription of the year 1262. Next is the Church of the Resistance, built in 1965 in memory of the partisan struggle of 1943-45.

Castle built in the 12th century on a hill just outside the village, then enlarged and fortified up to the maximum splendor under Pier Maria dei Rossi; then passed to Pallavicino, Sforza, Farnese and Mensa Vescovile, and was restored by the Alessandrini family. It dominates the valley between Parma and Baganza, is part of the circuit of the Castles of the Duchy and houses a restaurant and the Salame Museum.

Three biblical-themed itineraries between squares and streets of the village: ten fundamental moments in the history of salvation, the journey of Mary and the path of Mercy, with mosaics, murals, frescoes and photo-ceramics on private houses and public buildings, accompanied by verses in Friuli and Italian; the Last Judgment, the Good Samaritan and the Transfiguration stand out. The sketches are by Paolo Orlando; there are audio guides, the whole route takes about 2 and a half hours (the single routes 10-40 minutes) and it is easy, walkable and by bike and accessible to people with motor disabilities.
Views between two valleys and the legend of Fanfulla.
The village on the water before Pompeii.
One of the most important archaeological finds in Europe, with the crypt frescoed in the early Middle Ages.

In Palazzo Tori Massoni, exhibits artifacts from prehistory to the Middle Ages, with interactive and tactile places including prehistoric instruments and the cast of a Neanderthal femur; the museum project connects it to the Grotto to the Wave, to the Roman villa of Via Acquarella and to the medieval settlement of Montecastrense. Open from Tuesday to Friday in the morning, Saturday and Sunday morning and afternoon; closed on Monday. Also reduced with Carnet Versilia Museums or Edumusei Card.
15th century frescoes in a cave inhabited by prehistoric times.
17th century church dedicated to the Immaculate Church, with the convent of the Capuchin Friars, from which you can see the peninsula that separates the village from the rocky promontory.
The sunset beach in company.

Founded around 1123 by Cistercians who came from La Ferté on lands donated by Marquis Ranieri I del Monferrato; in 1457 it became commendable, in 1707 passed to the Savoys and in 1861 the estate was bought by Duke Raffaele de Ferrari of Galliera. There are still the octagonal Lombard Gothic bell tower, the cloister, the chapter hall of the middle of the thirteenth century, the Hall of the Conversi and the Baroque abbey church of 1767-1770 designed by Valente de Giovanni.
Megalites of 5,000 years between houses and vineyards.
Inside there is a wooden crucifix from the sixteenth century and a fresco by De Magistris from 1530.
Large green area inside the fortress, one of the quietest corners of the city; in the Middle Ages it was called Trans Mincio and was cultivated to gardens for the inhabitants.

Naturalistic oasis with five natural waterfalls and rare plant species on the river Bucamante, the main tributary of the Tiepid, in the valley between Monfestino and Monte Cornazzano; to the place is linked a legend.
Next to the civic museums.

The capital of the Molise in two parts: the medieval village that rises towards the Monforte Castle, with Romanesque churches and the Sannitico Museum, and below the Muratian city of the nineteenth century with the Cathedral and Villa De Capoa.

The mine, already mentioned by Pliny the Elder and exploited by Greeks, Romans and Normans, then became Royal Mine of Salgemma and closed in 1976; today of the Municipality, it has been restored and since 2010 it houses the museum with documents and finds.

Named after Father Silvestro Frangipane, who lived in the convent of Zagarise between 1570 and 1650, he was set up in 1990 by the parish priest Don Egidio Pudia; the nucleus of the collection are 36 paintings of the monks of that period. It contains frescoes and paintings from the sixteenth century and paintings and sculptures from the seventeenth to the nineteenth century, all coming from Zagarise, especially from the church and the Dominican monastery and from the parish church of Santa Maria Assunta, to which the museum is annexed.

Renaissance church on Piazza del Comune, designed by Agostino de' Fondulis (1517-1551), with facade adorned with terracotta bands. The interior with three naves contains paintings by Giulio Campi, Genovesino and Gian Giacomo Barbelli.
Example of Romanesque-Tuscan style in the historic center.
At the end of the sixteenth century, with monumental staircase in white stone: inside the chapel of the Holy Cross, a palace of 29 tiles in majolica of 1617 and a altarpiece framed by tiles of 1647.

Renaissance building just inside the walls of the village, with rectangular plan with plastered facade and rustic around windows and gates; it was the seat of the Florentine Podestà and today hosts exhibitions and cultural events.
To check the program of the exhibitions.

Housed in an old military structure, it has archaeological sections, contemporary art, postcards of artist, ceramics and photography; the permanent collection of modern and contemporary art has over 200 works donated by Italian and foreign artists.
The only Gothic church in Rome.

Byzantine-style chapel in the open countryside, built by the Basilian monks between the 7th and 9th centuries, unusually large, with a Greek cross on a square base with dome; declared national monument on August 31, 1909 and restored for some years. FAI place, open on the FAI Days of Spring 2025.
A historic stop in the square.

Walled center of towers and churches, with Etruscan sarcophagi used as urban furniture, the Town Hall in Piazza Basile and the seventeenth-century Great Fountain in Piazza Bastianini; from the walls one of the most beautiful landscapes of Tuscia.
Twelve reliefs of Cibele carved into the rock.
The park of Monte Rosa.
Ticket only museum + archaeological area: current rate on the Ministry's website (in 2022 €3, free up to 18 years); free on the first Sunday of the month

Theatre built in reinforced concrete on the water of the promenade, designed as a multifunctional space with coffee and exhibition halls, then cinematographer; in restoration to become a place of entertainment and the center of the Polo delle Arti Contemporanee.
The Romanesque mountain.

The village is a natural viewpoint over the Valle dei Calanchi, landscape of volcanic rocks, sandstone and clays among the most famous in Tuscia: from the small maze of arches, steps and medieval squares suddenly open views of the calanchi and Civita di Bagnoregio.
The dome can be seen from afar.

In the house where Achille Ratti was born and spent his early childhood, then a spinning mill Gavazzi, orphanage (1925-1971) and high school (until 2004), the Pius XI Museum, established in 1939, preserves 459 objects declared of exceptional cultural interest by the Superintendence, including a radio device designed by Guglielmo Marconi and donated to the pontiff in 1931. It is open for individual or group visits.
Two hundred steps leading to the oldest neighborhoods of the city, at the foot of the hill of the Masegra.
The symbol of the village, overlooking the valley of the Miscano.

The island of about 650 meters perimeter with the Via del Silenzio and the Meditation and the Benedictine abbey; the basilica founded in the fourth century, Romanesque plant, with the serpentine ambo of Oira and the crypt with the silver urn of 1697 with the relics of the saint.
Etruscan liver, unique object in the world.

Under the palace in front of the Forum of Traiano, the remains of aristocratic domus of the imperial age discovered in 2005, with mosaics and thermal environments told by the multimedia reconstruction curated by Piero Angela and Paco Lanciano.

In the former fourteenth-century church of San Sebastiano, it contains paintings from the fifteenth to the eighteenth century: two tables by Stefano Folchetti, the Pietà by Simone De Magistris (1584), a Madonna with Child and Saints by Vincenzo Pagani and works by Nicolò da Siena.

It was wanted by the merchant Pietro Montanari, who presented the project in 1910, and was inaugurated on February 9, 1911 with the comedy "Il Cardinale" and hosted also cinemas, dances and parties; the Municipality bought it in 1986 and reopened it in 1993 with the flutist Andrea Griminelli. The small elliptical hall has two orders of galleries in eclectic style, painted by Sardinian Luigi Pillitu with Musici and Comedants that form a fixed scene aimed at the public.
The parish church of the village, a few steps from the Oasis.

About 300 m2 on two floors with over 2,000 original objects, some rare: a kitchen and a room rebuilt with antique furnishings, agricultural tools on the ground floor and, on the upper floor, hunting, transport, weights and measurements, lights and lanterns, woodworking, wool, butter, cheese, wine and honey, with the workshops rebuilt of carpenter, shoemaker and blacksmith. Open all year round; the second floor is reached only by stairs.

Opened in 2003 in Castello Giovanelli, bought by the Municipality in 1989, it contains more than 220 works donated by the sculptor Alberto Meli and his wife, the painter Ester Gaini Meli. The route goes from the neoclassical sculptures of Giosuè Meli to the dada works of Arp, Richter, Probst and Valenti, linked with the work of Alberto Meli by artistic coordinator Fernando Noris; it continues outdoors with the diffused museum and has an extension in the parish church. Open Wednesday 14-18.30, Saturday 9-12.30 and Sunday 15-18; the museum indicates that visits are made by reservation (info@museoluzzana.it), guides for 20 € up to 5 people.
Arriving by train to the smallest village of Ogliastra.
An ancient craft still alive.
Plaster surfaces included in the UNESCO site on karst in the evaporites.

Permanent exhibition set up in two rooms on the ground floor of Palazzo Pignatelli, seat of the town hall: since 1994 it exhibits about 255 pieces of the territory of Lavello, including furnishings, agricultural tools, costumes and photographs related to the wheat cycle and the peasant house.
The medieval entrance still in use.

In the historic centre, it collects the works acquired by the municipality as prizes in the various editions of the National Sculpture Competition of Spinetoli; the exhibition space also hosts educational workshops on materials.
The church of the patron and the Palio.
A little canyon hidden in the Hills.

Permanent exhibition of kitchen utensils, diplomas, letters, photographs, recipes and menus of large banquets in hotels and embassies, belonged to cooks of yesterday and today trained in the Upper Livenza (Polcenigo, Budoia, Caneva, Fontanafredda) and immigrants to work in Italy and abroad. It is part of the regional Ecomuseum of the Friulian Dolomites. Visits by reservation (tel. 0434 749622, municipal library) and open during the main events.

Location of the Julian Pre-Alps Natural Park with information point and guesthouse; 8 km cross-country trail also used as a gymnico and mountain bike trail, and a path between beech woods and peak prairies towards the shelter of Monte Maggiore, Sella Kriz and Punta di Montemaggiore, with views of the Friulian plain.
A villa on the site of a castle, open one day a month.
Hannibal at the gates of the country.
A few kilometers from San Terenziano, of apparent Longobard origin; the name derives from the Roman consul Lucio Licinio Sura, who would have lived there.
the municipality indicates the village inhabited only from May to October
XV century cathedral in St. Peter's Square, in the center, with the fountain that tradition wants donated by the builders of the church.
Manzetti's automaton.

The city of the hundred towers in the hills east of Turin, a textile city from the fifteenth century: the great Gothic Cathedral, the triumphal arch of the late sixteenth century, the Jewish ghetto and, in Pession, the Martini museum of enology.
The historic marina where fishermen are seen at work, next to the village founded before the year 1000.
The Neapolitan marina.

The "door of the Dolomites" between Mediterranean and Central European culture: the Medieval Porticos, Walther Square, Ötzi at the Archaeological Museum, Castel Roncolo frescoed and the cable cars towards Renon, Colle and San Genesio.
The chessboard seen from the top of the square.
The farm of the first South Tyrolean saint.
The cathedral next to the Doge's Palace, with the nearby Diocesan Museum Albani.
The Romanesque church on the hill.
The heart of the village among the chestnut trees.

In the sixteenth century Palazzo Affaitati, more than two thousand works including the "San Francesco in meditation" by Caravaggio, the "Ortolano" by Arcimboldi and the Cremonese painters Bembo, Boccaccino, Melone and the Campi; the Rooms for Music preserve the Carutti collection of pinch instruments. In the same building the Natural History Museum.
Baroque Langarolo and one of the two bell towers symbol of the country.
The Bourbon palace between Vesuvius and the sea.
The surviving green giants of the lakefront.

€10 full · €6 affiliated · €2 from 18 to 25 years · free under 18, before Sunday of the month and with Bologna Welcome Card or Card Culture. During the exhibitions the price can change. The ticket also applies to Palazzo Pepoli Campogrande within three months
The mother church of the village.
Ancient books and finds of the country.

In the Palazzo Pretorio of the fifteenth century, restored in 1998, it tells of the human presence in the Valle dell'Albegna from prehistory to the Etruscans and the Romans. It exhibits the Hellenistic finds of Ice Strong (ceramics, bronze statuettes, objects related to fertility rites) and reconstructions of the Roman villa at the farm Aia Nova, with parts of the floors in cottage.
The village was still in the early 20th century.
The parish church of Masserano along the main road was built in 1486 because Saint Theonesto remained outside the walls. He preserves paintings, wooden sculptures and sacred vestments.
According to the Regione Marche historical center and museums are partially usable; info@visitmontaltomarche.it

Santa Croce, five-sixth-century oratory with sailing bell tower, preserves the wooden crucifix used in Holy Week; Our Lady of Itria, in via Ichnusa, is seventeenth-century and hosted a confraternity founded in 1613; from the chapel of St. Francis the Christ of the procession de s'Incontu starts at Easter.

The 120-metre-long porch has 30 arches on 29 marble columns, each different from the others for architecture and decoration: it was built in the early sixteenth century by Ludovico Gonzaga as a covered road and restored in 1933. Under the arcades there is the Teatro Paolo Giacometti, now the seat of the municipal library "Aldo Placchi"; in the center there are also the Baroque oratory of San Rocco, of the early seventeenth century, and the Preda Pescadura, the only testimony of the Gonzaga fortifications demolished in the eighteenth century (the castle was demolished in 1705).
Sabina's yellow gold.

One of the oldest rural buildings in the area, documented from the beginning of the fourteenth century, in the grassy plain between Caderzone and Pinzolo: the beams still bear the signs of the fire of 1537 and outside there is an ancient votive fresco with St. Anthony Abbot and St. Barbara. It is still used for demonstration purposes.
The miraculous Madonna.
Gift of Spanish Catholics, realized in 1935 in the garden of the kindergarten.

The historical centre is accessed by the Gothic Door of the fifteenth century, built in the walls; there are the Civic Tower, Casa Rossi Delicate and the Municipal Palace, assaulted and set on fire in 1799 by the brigands of Sciabolone, who destroyed the archive.
A hot outdoor bath, all year round.

karst cave on the slopes of the Hermada, frequented by the Neolithic and adapted between II and V century AD to the sanctuary of Mitra: casts of the two reliefs with the sacrifice of the bull and the inscriptions of the tenderers. Open on Saturday morning, visits with the Flondar Speleological Group.
Entering a farm of Mochen five centuries ago.

Cities at the gates of Turin with two complexes of great interest: the Royal Certosa, seventeenth-century monastery expanded by Filippo Juvarra and then psychiatric hospital until 1978, today the heart of the city park, and the Leumann Village, Art Nouveau Workers' Quarter wanted at the end of the nineteenth century by Napoleone Leumann. In the historic centre the Castle Provana, the civic tower and the churches of San Lorenzo, Santa Croce and San Massimo.

Artificial lake at about 1,700 m: a circuit path of 6.7 km (almost 2 hours, 206 m of difference in altitude) starts crossing the dam and runs largely in the shade above the lake, with two suspended bridges. Depending on the level of the water, the bell tower of a submerged church emerges, and in the chapel of Vernago are displayed photos of the plain and of the flooded farms. The lake has been more beautiful since mid-July, when the basin is full. Free parking and bus 261.
The millennial parish church on the Trebbia.
12th century church in the hamlet of Villa Brozzi, a single nave with wooden ceiling painted with drawers; under the building were found remains of an imperial villa.
Built in 1346, it houses valuable paintings.

The most important monumental complex in the region, residence of the bishops until 1803: Castelvecchio on the Tower of Augustus, the Magno Palazzo di Bernardo Clesio with frescoes by Dosso Dosso and Romanino, the courtyard of the Leoni, the cells of Cesare Battisti and the Italian garden.
Small hamlet that preserves Albanian traditions, Byzantine rite and Arbëreshë language.

In the ancient property Altemps and then Borghese linked to Villa Mondragone, a large Roman complex of the imperial State: an underground guided itinerary leads to a rare set of Roman inscriptions drawn with brush, charcoal and graffito on the plaster; the front with semi-colons doriche is fifth to the shows and the esplanade overlooks Rome. Guided tours by reservation on weekends.
MiC card (updated 2020) indicates closed every day: check with the museum (tel. 081 5318496)
Feudal residence of the 12th century built on an ancient Roman bastion; at the moment not visitable.

In the center there are still sections of the walls and a medieval tower; on the main square, along the promenade, the bastion (torrion) was erected in 1564 against the pirate raids, which did not prevent a barbaric raid. The parish church of Saints John the Baptist and Eugenio, rebuilt in 1637 after the plundering of the Algerian pirates, preserves paintings of the Genoese school (Orazio De Ferrari, Piola, Carlone), modern frescoes of Bonichi in the vault and a wooden crucifix with the hole of a cannon ball; next, the Oratory of Saint Catherine with a neoclassical façade.
The wall paintings of the parish.
The small temple of the plagued next to the Bassanella.
The Madonna with the airport hangars.
Industrial archaeology in the Scrivia valley.
The only museum in the world entirely dedicated to the harp.
Weaving machines in front of the visitors.

Longobard-Romanesque church of the VII-VIII century, among the oldest places of worship of Veronese still in use, restored at the beginning of the XII century (Romanesque structures of the east side and bell tower), with three naves with two opposite apses. The most precious piece is the Longobard ciborium of the Master Bear and disciples, with inscriptions of the age of Liutprand (712-736); there are also frescoes of the 11th-XIV century, a Gothic tabernacle of 1433, an octagonal baptismal font of the 12th century obtained from a single block of marble and a Resurrection of Palma the Younger. From a small door on the south side you enter the cloister.

Calanchi recognized as a good of community interest, which extend for about 3,5 km in the valley of the Alento with walls that in some places exceed 100 meters; in the territory flow streams like the Rio Seripenna, the Focaro and the Valige and survive houses of raw earth.
Two churches superimposed and oriented in opposite directions, both frescoed, with sixteenth-century loggia on the façade and the tombstone of Cardinal East East East East.
Example of Gothic-Lombard architecture with terracotta façade.

Caldirola (1,012 m), cited in documents of about 1190, rises on a rocky spur; above, at the Gioia (1,299 m), in the fifties was born the only winter sports station of the province. A chairlift also active in summer, or the mule tracks, lead to the vast plateaus between 1,500 and 1,700 m between the peaks of Giarolo, Panà, Ebro and Chiappo, with wide views.
The medieval symbol of the country.
A cellar dug into the rock, the heart of the UNESCO site.

Churches and buildings in local sandstone called "campanedda": partly destroyed by the earthquake of 1968, the center still retains 28 churches, the ancient Jewish district of the Judecca and the Islamic one of the Rabato with its alleys.
The most important Roman mosaics in the Marche region.

Along the beach of small white quartz pebbles between the sea, the pond and the ancient salt pans built in the 13th century by the monks of Santa Maria di Tergu; low and sandy seabed, wind for windsurfing and kite, track for runners and cyclists behind. To the north are the old traps and the Spanish tower of the sixteenth century; between the Saline and Monti Frattu 17 bunkers of the Second World War, which can be visited with guide during Open Monuments.
A rare village theatre of the early twentieth century.
Rock spire about 300 meters high, climbed for the first time in 1902, in the territory of the Park above Cimolais, destination of hikers and mountaineers.
The church of the wolf and snake parties.
A courthouse on an intimate scale.
A monastery-fortress.

On Piazza Statuto overlook the Palazzo Comunale, the church of the Confraternita del Gonfalone with Baroque bell tower and the Wing of the Market, imposing 19th century building. In via Mazzini run the low medieval porticos, with a capital carved from the fifteenth century of the destroyed portico of justice; from Borgo Vecchio the tree-lined avenue of the "Lea", along the river Albetta, rises to the hill of the ancient castle, conquered by the Savoys in 1487 and destroyed in the seventeenth century.
An eighteenth-century castle dedicated entirely to Dante.

Medieval mill excavated underground, today museum of rural civilization, destination of lovers of rural archaeology: preserves ancient wooden presses, stone millstones, ovens and housing of the workers.
Gothic fifteenth century and Baretta together.

The name comes from ... ..sex milia... ..the six miles from Pistoia. Medieval fortress of the Panciatichi, in 1466 was removed from the Florentines for participation in the conspiracy against Piero di Cosimo de' Medici and then became villa-farm, preserving the appearance of a fortress: quadrangular building with two tall crenellated towers and sharp hanging arches, portal in squared basins and courtyard closed by two symmetrical buildings. Today it is the seat of the Municipality and houses the library, the municipal historical archive and the permanent exhibition of the works of the Montalese sculptor and graphic artist Jorio Vivarelli.
Acropolis Volsca with polygonal walls of the VIII-VII BC centuries, among the best preserved in pre-Roman Italy, and a rare arch with acute sixth in stone.
A nuraghe with an unusual plant.

Medieval village of the upper Staffora Valley, a feud of Malaspina and entered the most beautiful villages of Italy in 2022: the porticoes of Via del Mercato, the towers of Porta Soprana and Porta Sottana, the Tower of the Witches, the seventeenth-century churches of the confraternities, the Romanesque San Germano dei Cappuccini and, in Cella, the Temple of the Fraternity of Peoples; to taste the Salame of Varzi DOP.
The peasant and mountain culture of the valley, object by object.

The village, at 1,027 meters, has a medieval structure built also with stones and finds taken from the archaeological area; the oldest part, to the north-west, is framed by the two great rocks of the Morgia della Torre and the Morgia del Castello, which give the village its profile. The centre is dominated by the Baronial Palace of the Marchesani, linked to the family's events in the insurrections of 1860 and in the Second World War; in the tower Francesco Marchesani hid the family during the nineteenth-century revolts.

The park has columns, exotic trees and Masonic symbols; inside the Clown Museum with interactive settings.

Next to the port the beach of Buggerru, of soft sand; further north, behind a pine forest, the dunes of San Nicolò with the beaches of Is Compingius and Is Compingieddus, also suitable for mountain bike excursions, up to the stretch of coast of Capo Pecora and Portixeddu.

At the intersection of via Mazzini, via Vittoria and via Steffenini, incorporated in the park of a villa, the private oratory of San Rocco (early 16th century), brick, square outside and octagonal inside, attributed to Giovanni Baptaggio and Giovanni Antonio Amadeo with references to Bramante: it is not open to the public and can be seen from the outside.
Most of the houses and palaces are in red trachyte; the Town Hall, in the early decades of the nineteenth century, overlooks piazza sas Bovedas, the center of social life.

At about 800 meters above sea level in a wood of holm oaks near the village, the remains of an extensive nuragic village with tombs of giants and a small temple with circular plan, rare example of nuragic temple in the antis.

The Roman city buried by the eruption of Vesuvius of 79 AD, with the Villa dei Misteri and the House of Fauno, is with Herculaneum and Oplontis UNESCO Heritage; the modern city is a pilgrimage destination for the Shrine of the Blessed Virgin of the Rosary founded by Bartolo Longo.

Since 1258 it has kept the relics of St. Thomas arrived from Chios; destroyed in the Second World War and rebuilt, it preserves the Gothic portal of Nicola Mancino of 1311 and, in the left nave, access to the Diocesan Museum.

The Via Umberto, the "strata' a fera" of the walk, with sundials on the facades, the arch of Via Archi, portals and balconies in sandstone; Piazza Municipio with the stairway used as amphitheatre and the nineteenth-century Municipal Palace with the clock of 1884; the Piazzetta Badia with sea-themed sculptures. A dozen vertical solar clocks form the sundial path.

Borgo della Valceresio, part of the Italian-Swiss Palaeontological site of Monte San Giorgio, UNESCO World Heritage Site: the Civic Museum of Fossil Exhibits the Besanosaurus, while the fossil path leads to the Rio Ponticelli Park and the former shale mines; in the village the parish church of San Martino and, above, the Colle San Martino with a view of the Ceresio.

In the basin of the ancient lake Carera, formed about 14,000 years ago behind a moraine barrier and then transformed into a peat bog, remain the poles of palafittic villages inhabited between the Neolithic and the Bronze Age. Discovered in the middle of the nineteenth century during the extraction of peat and systematically investigated from 1969 to 1976 and again since 1981, the site has been UNESCO World Heritage since 2011 on the serial site "Siti palafitticoli prehistorici dell'archo alpine" . It is inside the nature reserve Carera, biotope of provincial interest and Site of Community Importance with birds, amphibians and marsh flora; you can visit freely on catwalks with information panels.
One of the most beautiful caves in Italy, with river and underground waterfall.

Born in 1954 in the center of the village, in the former Hotel du Chamois, to preserve the historical memory of Rorà: it reconstructs environments of daily life (kitchen, stable, bedroom, school) and has rooms dedicated to the history of Waldensian, stone and lime processing. Open in July and August on Sunday 10-12 and 16-19, in other periods on request; accessible to those with reduced mobility only on the first floor.

The medieval centre, at 1,210 metres, contains a pentagonal tower of the 13th-XIV centuries, an ancient bell tower and the clock tower, with heraldic coats of arms of the Counts of Celano, the Piccolomini. The village formed between the 11th and 12th centuries with the phenomenon of the castle, on a rocky spur at the foot of the Great Mountain. Built by the Venetian family Duodo on the site of the ancient castle of San Giorgio: the oldest wing is from 1593 on a project by Vincenzo Scamozzi, the façade of 1740; on the left side there is the large 17th century stone staircase, the Exedra dedicated to San Francesco Saverio. The oldest sanctuary dedicated to Saint Anthony; the museum collects the works once in the Antonian Art Gallery, including numerous paintings by the Swiss painter Melchior Widmar (second half of the seventeenth century), and stuccoes of the eighteenth century recovered after the collapses of 1976.

Seat of a Benedictine hermitage on the summit plateau of Monte Santo, donated in 1065 by the judge Torchitorio-Barisone I of Torres, together with Santa Maria di Bubalis, to the abbey of Montecassino. It has two naves with barrel vaults: the north perhaps of the late XI century, the widening of the second half of the XII; traces of bichromy remain in the arches between the naves. The Fontana degli Scogli (1675) is the work of Carlo Fontana, a pupil of Gian Lorenzo Bernini; the church of Santa Maria Maggiore, of Byzantine origin, was rebuilt in Baroque style.

The regional museum of modern and contemporary art has been based since 2005 in the eighteenth-century Palazzo Belmonte Riso, in the historic centre.

One of the rock villages of the Ligurian Alps, inhabited already in the Neolithic and documented since the 7th century. The Baroque parish church of Saints Nazarius and Celsus preserves part of the fourteenth-century Romanesque bell tower; at the south-eastern end of the village the late Baroque sanctuary of the Madonna dei Colombi was destroyed by the earthquake of 1887 and rebuilt.

The hilly village of Castelnuovo, on the Arno at the border with the territory of Arezzo, is dominated by a large castle with a high tower, built after the 1000 and changed several times; it is named after the Fioraia family, who received it at the beginning of the fifteenth century as a prize for the services to the Florentine Republic.

A circular cruise without stops in the part of the Adda included in the Adda South Park, known for its flora and fauna, starting from the Gera boat; it can be combined with the guided tour of the walls.
Erected in the fourteenth century and extensively rebuilt, it preserves the Gothic portal, a stone sculpture and the seventeenth-century canvas of the Paradise of Battistello.

Trail No 8 of the Park, ring from the square of Baone: 5 km, 170 m of difference in altitude, about 1 hour and 30 minutes, tourist difficulty, of high interest for flora and panorama. Crossing hedges, an olive grove, rocks of latites with onion exfoliations and woods of black hornbeam, touches the ruins of the castle and of house Bolcato and the "vegri" , arid meadows with the Ruta patavina and various orchids.

Monastery of the thirteenth century, still inhabited by a small group of Poor Clares: it houses two Madonnas and an Annunciation of the Sassoferrato, a painting by Antonio da Pesaro and a seventeenth-century Crucifixion of a Nordic artist.
Chapel founded in 1924 by Andreas Kuppelwieser as a thank you for coming back with the brothers unharmed from World War I; his initials are carved at the base of the wooden stall.
Long natural beaches.

109 steps up to the top of the hill, flanked by red brick houses arranged with fishbone; in the middle there is the Polenta Well, where according to legend the inhabitants cooked polenta during the sieges. The legend lives again in July in the Polenta Pozzo Contesa, with over 300 re-enactors.

A neo-Gothic church designed by Luigi Poletti and built between 1864 and 1868, with a beautiful rose window on the façade; it rises in the upper part of the city, on a street with porticoes of the seventeenth century.

Church of the fourteenth century, parish since 1605, known for its antiquity and ornaments. It is the church of the Feast of the Assumption: in August the procession of the "Three Giants" , candlelights of 9 tons high 8 meters, dissolves a vow made during a plague of the thirteenth century.

From Sesto you can reach the Rifugio Tre Cime (Locatelli) with path 102 in about 3 and a half hours and about 950 meters of difference in altitude; alternatively shuttle from Sesto (tickets online or at the tourist office) or car to the Rifugio Auronzo, with obligatory booking.

Bridge-aqueduct about 80 meters high and about 230 long, on 9 pylons joined by ogival arches in local limestone; the current aspect is of the XIII-XIV century and connects the city to the wood of Monteluco.

Born on the initiative of Fiat 500 Club Italia and inaugurated in July 2007, it tells the story of the 500 and its role in bringing Italy to modernity in the sixties. You enter through a magical tent: inside there are the reconstruction of an old workshop, showcases with models, components and accessories, touch-screen stations with documentaries and commercials, two driving simulators with the seats of two real half cars, some working cars, a bar in vintage style, library and themed emerotheque. MiC timetables: mon-ven 9-18, sat 9-12, sun closed; booking for groups. Tel. 0182 582282.
The Etruscan origins of Viterbo.

Built between 1877 and 1894 on a project by Gaetano Canedi and inaugurated with the Carmen of Bizet, it has three orders of stages and loggia; restored between 1987 and 1999, it hosts the seasons of prose and opera.

X century church with square plan with pronao, three naves and barrel vaults, overlooking the square; facade with clock, staircase and atrium are baroque. At the time of the Republic of Amalfi was the Palatine chapel where the Doges received the ducal berretta. It preserves a 12th century marble slab with two peacocks and the fourteenth-century plaque of Filippa Napolitano; the bronze doors of 1087, donated by Pantaleone Viarecta, are now kept in Santa Maria Maddalena.

The gate of Sicily on the Strait, reborn after the earthquake of 1908: Piazza Duomo with the Norman cathedral, the largest astronomical clock in the world and the Fountain of Orione, the Annunziata dei Catalani, the MuMe with Antonello and Caravaggio, the Madonnina del Porto and Capo Peloro.

Lake at 2,087 m in a glacial basin, reached by Villa Poma (right side of Lake Ceresole) with path 521: about 2 hours, 4 km and 503 m of altitude difference, through one of the most interesting coniferous forests of the Park (laric, red and white firs, pine trees) and pastures in front of the East Levanna. Support point of the Refuge Leonesi; recommended period June-October.

Franciscan complex built between 1371 and 1411 with two cloisters, a single nave church, a wing of the novitiate of 1708 and a library of 127 codes. Today it remains the main cloister of Renaissance imprint, with the seventeenth-century well surrounded by arches on columns; the cloister is open every day 9-12,30 and 15-17,30.

It is reached from the bridge over Topino along via Umberto I; the 15th century civic tower bears the coat of arms of Baglioni. Of the medieval circuit remains sections of walls with a tower and a circular bastion.
The megalithic walls of Circe.

In 1910, he marked with a stone the place where King Umberto I was killed on July 29, 1900: Greek-Byzantine-inspired mosaics and about 180 bronze crowns.

Cologne founded by the Romans in 296 BC and then important stop of the Via Appia, famous for the thermal baths frequented by Roman matrons and patricians; in 375 it suffered enormous damage due to a catastrophic earthquake. The remains of the submerged city are located in the hamlet Le Vagnole. On the occasion of the Appia Day 2026 the Superintendence opened the Regina Viarum Archaeological Park in Mondragone with free guided tours.

Molise country linked to the architect Giuseppe Barone, who in 1897 donated his collection of art and archaeology to the Municipality, today civic museum, and signed the fountain of Cerere and the enlargement of the church of the Rosary; on Mount Vairano, towards Busso, remain the walls of a city of the Sanniti Pentri.

Cathedral with neoclassical façade, born with the foundation of the city in 1198, with the altarpiece of Andrea Pozzo; here is celebrated the patron Saint Michele on September 29.

Romanesque-Gothic church of the XII century, renovated in the Two-Three-th century, with bell tower with cross-windows and portal fourteenth-century flanked by two lions; in the bezel an Annunciation frescoed by Paolo da Visso.

Country of the Canal del Ferro in the Natural Park of the Julian Prealps, where for over a century the mines of the Rio Resartico at the slopes of Mount Plauris gave work to the community and since 1844 beer was produced with the waters of the river Resia: today they tell the exhibition of the mine and the ice tunnel of the brewery.

With Pontechianale, the highest municipality in Val Varaita, divided into ten hamlets of stone and wood: it houses 34 restored sundials dated between 1734 and 1934, the Museum of Time and Meridian in Celle, the fifteenth-century parish church of San Giacomo and the eighteenth-century church of the Holy Spirit.
Route of industrial archeology between mills and hydraulic mills, with arched stone channels.

The 15th century cloister, with trapezoidal plan with sixteen arches on thin columns in serene stone and carved capitals, is the only structure surviving the earthquake of 1920 that destroyed the village, then rebuilt.

In the former premises of the livestock market, it collects the finds of the territory from the Paleolithic to the Middle Ages: the vegetable fossils of the petrified forests of the Anglona, the oldest stone instruments found so far in Sardinia, the statue of the mother Reduced for groups of at least 20 people, schools and over 60.

The most famous of the thirty churches of the village, near the promenade: of origin XI-XII century and rebuilt in the nineteenth century, has a crypt rearranged in the eighteenth century with a coeva urn that guards the remains of the patroness. In the presence of the relics is linked the survival of the rites of Holy Week, with the processions of the "baptants" and the traditional songs.

Begin in 1568 as the headquarters of the Superguard that led the Comarch of Caesarea, from which the name of "Torre Capitana" was demolished and completely rebuilt in 1622. It is the largest sighting tower in size: square plan of 22 meters on the side, 16 meters high, thick walls in tuff, two floors, caditoie and crowning on catchatelli; it communicated with Torre Squillace to the south and Torre Chianca to the north.

Founded on 29 December 1898 thanks to the generosity of the faithful, it is one of the oldest museums in Campania and occupies the birthplace of San Pompilio Maria Pirrotti (1710-1766). In five rooms he exhibits objects from the house of the saint and works of art from other churches of Montecalvo, including the statue of the Mother Bella dell'Abbondanza (XVI-XVII century) and a seventeenth-century portrait of the saint. Visit by reservation.

Museum Polo inaugurated in 1960: the Pinacoteca donated by Leonida and Albertina Repaci with works among others by Guercino, Manet, Corot, Fattori and Guttuso, the Gipsoteca by Michele Guerrisi, the Museum of ethnography and folklore "Raffaele Corso" , the Museum dedicated to Francesco Chilea and Nicola Antonio Manfroce and the Antiquarium with the artifacts of Tauriana.
One of the great beech woods of Veneto, to be turned calmly.

Fortress on the slopes of the Apuan Islands, strategic for the proximity to the sea and the control of the Via Francigena, one of the oldest of the Lunigiana and already Byzantine garrison at the Longobard border; the name refers to the Aghinulfo mentioned in a document of the 8th century. A circle of walls with towers contains two spaces; the mast is built on a large octagonal building, perhaps of the twelfth century, connected to the circular tower of San Paolino. In 1945 it was one of the main German strongholds of the Gothic Line; restored since 1998, it has a panoramic terrace and a room with glass floor on the stratifications of the building.

At the ancient Forum Clodii on the Via Clodia, mentioned already under Leo IV (847-855) as ecclesia Sancti Marciani: a 9th century nave, frescoed apse of the 11th-XII century with the Saints Marco and Marciano on the sides of the Virgin, bell tower of the 12th-XIII century and chapel of San Liberato added by the Augustinians; in 1965 landscaper Russell Page created a botanical garden with native plants and precious species. Today owned by Sanminiatelli.

Two of the churches built over the centuries that enrich the village: Sant'Agata preserves paintings and frescoes, St. Nicholas a wooden choir.
Housed in the fourteenth-century church of Sant'Antonio, it collects mainly local collections, including the Calappilia mani, species of crab present only in this area.

Inaugurated in 2003 in the closed courtyard, partly still inhabited, of the fourteenth-century agricultural village of Camporeso, among the terraces: it tells the life and work of the folk classes of the Brianza hills and of the Lecchese between the nineteenth and twentieth centuries. It is one of the few demo-ethno-anthropological museums recognized by the Lombardy Region and leader of the REBEL network.

Formed by the Senise dam, Europe's largest clay dam, it is referred to as the largest artificial lake on clay in Europe and the third in the world. The shores alternate Mediterranean maquis and forests of oaks and pine trees; on a promontory of the lake, in the Pollino National Park, stands an observatory for the sighting of numerous species of sedentary and migratory birds. On the lake you can practice rowing, canoeing and sailing, in the surroundings trekking, horse riding, climbing and mountain biking.

Historical neighborhood in the gravina that crosses the city, where shops and ovens occupy ancient cavities and underground environments used once also as mills; there is worked a ceramics known all over the world. In May it hosts the festival     Â"Good morning Ceramics!Â" .
Medieval complex with church of the XII-XIII century and convent, overlooking a short visible stretch of the Roman road Karalis-Ulbia; in the courtyard there is also the museum Is Lollas.

Rest of one of the most important castles in the area, documented by 963 and perhaps already Etruscan settlement; the castle, which had two towers, survives the watchtower about 27 meters high, about 500 meters above sea level. Inside a multimedia path on the history of Galatrona and the castle; climbing five floors of stairs you have a 360 degree view of the Valdarno and the Chianti Mountains. Open from April to October, usually on Saturday and Sunday.

Palaces and junk in grey granite and tree-lined avenues in a city that was diocesan and courthouse. In Piazza Gallura the eighteenth-century Palazzo Pes di Villamarina, seat of the Curia; the Palazzo dell'Ex Me, of 1663, was first prison and then market. On Piazza San Pietro you can see the cathedral, the oratories and the Teatro del Carmine.

The town of ceramics in Val di Noto, a UNESCO World Heritage Site for Baroque rebuilt after the earthquake of 1693: the staircase of Santa Maria del Monte with its majolica lift, the Regional Museum of Ceramics and a hundred workshops.
Romanesque synagogue with cusp façade and sailing bell tower, which has been active for the Jewish community since 2005.

The Malatesta walls form two circles: the first, close to the fortress, with Guelph and Ghibelline blackbirds; the second, wider, contains the historic center with fourteen towers and a fortified door with the Sforza, Della Rovere and Farnese coats of arms. The outer belt, with square crenellated towers, can still be walked along the round walkways.

In the former convent of the Capuchins, built in 1705 and suppressed in 1866, the guided tour follows all the stages of the work, from the decoration of corks and fini products (slips, shoes, bags, panels, insulation, even baseballs), with videos and photos of the first machines, benches, turnings and a cork nativity scene. The official production in Calangianus began in 1851; at the exit we receive a cork souvenir. Hours indicated: mon-sab 10-18, sun 10-17.

In an old house with a loggia on three floors reconstructs the traditional house: kitchen with cupboard and pantry, wooden crockery, beds and cots, a room with tools for agriculture and breeding, tools for spinning and tiles with a large frame, lace, embroidered linen and typical costumes, different from country to country, with a photographic collection of vintage clothes. It is part of the High Verbano Museum Network. The Municipality indicates opening every day 8-20 (from 15 November to 31 March 9-18); steps at the entrance, not accessible to the disabled.

The fourteenth-century fortress with pentagonal plan at the highest point of the village, almost unchanged from the Middle Ages, with towers and walkway: the courtyard is free, the climb on the stands is paid.

The village of Sila Piccola was built around the year 1000, with a Norman tower dating back to the 13th-XIV centuries that now houses an astronomical observatory, the fifteenth-century church of Santa Maria Assunta with the Museum of Sacred Art and a museum of oil in an ancient oil mill; in the territory the canyon of Tempe Rosse, the waterfalls Campanaro and Mount Gariglione.

The old Belpensiero farmhouse, mentioned in 16th century sources and still surrounded by fields, is located in the historic centre, with a centuries-old plateau in the courtyard; the health and fertility of the area are due to the monks' reclamations, which healed a swampy area.
The collection of the canon Angelo Maria Bandini: gold-bottomed plates and Robbian terracotta.

Historical residence of Kalsa became a regional museum; it is part, with Palazzo Abatellis and the Oratorio dei Bianchi, of the Regional Interdisciplinary Gallery of Sicily.
One of the most intact stone villages in Abruzzo.

Born in 1975 on the initiative of private individuals, it collects an ethnographic section with tools and artifacts on the production and processing of flax and silk, textile activities on which the local economy was based until the 1930s, including the complete set of tools for the breeding of the silkworm. It also exhibits objects for lighting, from oil to electricity, tools and everyday objects, and preserves over 2,500 hand-embroidered items, especially in linen, from the 18th century to the early 20th century.
Fresh in summer, spectacular in autumn.
Small museum founded and opened by the National Alpine Association in 1950 at the end of the bridge, with views of the city and the mountains.
A sulphuric spring in the woods.
A piece of Rapa Nui in the Tuscia.

Church from its origins in the 11th century on the top of the hill, closed in 1799, reopened in 1808 and consolidated after the earthquake of 1915 until 1944. Inside stuccos attributed to Gregorio Grimani (1636) in the chapel of the Immaculate, paintings by Vincenzo Manenti, squasantiere in pink marble by Cottanello and an organ of 1831 by Count Alderano Spada. At about 50 meters the seventeenth-century bell tower, built on one of the six towers of the walls, next to a medieval arched door.
The red Cesanese in his cellars.

The centre of Parteolla, born in the early twentieth century from the union of San Pantaleo and Sicci San Biagio: the symbol is the former Romanesque cathedral of San Pantaleo, consecrated in 1289, with its fifteenth-century retablo; in the village also the Museum of the olearia tradition is the "Sa mola de su notariu" and the Villa de Villa.
The Norman cathedral reborn after the earthquake.
The ancient Romanesque church on the hill of Castagnola, in the medieval district \"Villa" with wide views of the lake.

Borgo dell'Alto Monferrato Ovadese which takes its name from the Grimaldi, lords from the sixteenth to the nineteenth century: on the spur above the valley of the Orba rises the castle with medieval tower and eighteenth-century garden, and the village is known for the Lachera, the ritual carnival told in the Museum of the Mask.

In Pratica di Mare, the area of the XIII altars and the monument called Heroon of Enea belongs to the ancient Lavinium; VisitLatium is a sign that can be visited with a guided tour and the Superintendence organizes free extraordinary openings in the annual cycle   Â Lavinium: archaeology and territory Â .
The curved façade of a pupil of Bernini next to the palace.

Established by the Municipality in 1977 in a historic building of the square next to the town hall, it preserves more than two thousand finds on the rural life of Modena of the first half of the twentieth century, on the history of Bastille, of the fifteenth-century basin on the Naviglio and the extensive mill. Themed rooms on hemp, cellar and lambrusco, housekeeper, laundry, worldly, school and ancient crafts, with the suggestive hall of the fireplace; in the Pavilion of the agricultural machines vintage tractors, the threshing machine "Carra" and the prototype of the tractor Fiat 60R (1940-41), buried to remove it from the Nazi troops and recovered in May 1945. Damaged by the earthquake of 2012 and the flood of 2014, it was re-arranged also with multimedia media; it has the regional certification of Museum quality. Closed in August and on national holidays; for times contact the museum (museo@comune.bastiglia.mo.it).

The center rises on the slopes of Monte Civita, where the ruins of a medieval fortress with four bastions remain; the walls of 1410 originally had five doors, including Porta Romana, Porta Valeria, Porta San Rocco and Porta dei Marsi.
The mountain dairy life, in the dairy where it took place.

The political, religious and commercial heart of the city, surrounded by noble frescoed buildings, with the eighteenth-century Fountain of the Neptune in the center that holds the trident, recalls the ancient name Tridentum.

On the highest point of the village the fortress built by the Aldobrandeschi in the 13th century, remained to them until 1439 when it passed to the Sforza with the county of Santa Fiora: today it is a two-storey building flanked by the clock tower. In front of the church of St. Nicholas, several times restored, with a painting from the seventeenth century attributed to Sienese painters; the church of Our Lady of the Rosary contains paintings from the sixteenth and seventeenth centuries. From the village, whose name according to legend comes from a game of dice between the Pope and the Emperor, the view spans the Val di Paglia and Lazio.
A tower on the rock wire.
The Cathedral of Adrano, built in Norman style.

Medieval village of the Euganean Hills where Francesco Petrarca lived the last years and died in 1374: you visit his house, the tomb in red marble in front of the church of Santa Maria Assunta and, just outside, the Laghetto della Costa, a UNESCO World Heritage site.
Porta crelata in terracotta of the walls decorated with noble coats of arms, with the arch in Sansovino style.
Documentation centre on the history of stonemasons over the centuries, with panels on the work of quarry and a collection of tools for stone processing.
open in dedicated days with the volunteers Touring

The Apennines are located at the foot of the ridge of Monte Cusna, in the heart of the National Park of the Tuscan-Emilian Apennines and the UNESCO MAB Biosphere Reserve. It preserves the tradition of dramatic May in the museum inside the old fortress, the medieval fortress of Minozzo, the springs of Poiano and the mountain towns of Civago and Febbio.
The Catalan Gothic in the heart of the Meilogu.
The farmhouse of the holy child.
Spa complex on a hill, behind an ancient forest.

Large Liberty style villa designed by Carlo Nigra in 1926 at the entrance of the village for those arriving from Miasino: more two- or three-storey bodies with a panoramic tower, in a vast park with rare conifers, azaleas, rhododendrons, a forest of araucaria and secular beech trees. Private property, visible only from the outside.
The bohemian neighbourhoods beyond Termini: the pedestrian area of Via del Pigneto with the daily market, set of Rome open city and Accattone, and San Lorenzo with shops, street art and clubs.
14th century palace with Celtic Mask.
11th century castle with panoramic view of the valley.
Panoramic municipal park above the village, reachable on foot by an ancient staircase or with the free panoramic elevator of via Cassisi.

Lake of glacial origin reached by Pierabech with the signs CAI 141 and 142, between larch woods and about 900 meters of difference in altitude; along the path the source Fleons, at 1,370 meters, from which flows the water Drop Carnia. It is a wildlife oasis with cedar roosters, marmots, deer, roe deer and royal eagles, gentians and orchids.

The most important monument of the country, probably of thirteenth-century origin, remodelled several times after the earthquakes and survived that of 1805; the relics of the saint arrived in 1099 with two pilgrims headed to the Holy Land. The bell tower has a wrought iron dome; inside the tomb of Bishop Attilio (1536), two marble altars of the eighteenth century, the chapel of San Carlo Borromeo (1737), the Carafa chapel and the Treasure chapel (1609) with busts of silver copper saints.

In the medieval residence Larchgut, a monument protected with a tower mentioned in 1301, about 1,000 square meters of exposure on the history of fruit growing and rural life: from the objects of viticulture, including the oldest wine press in South Tyrol (1570), to the tools of the nineteenth century, vehicles and machines in the barn; tells the boom of fruit after the reclamation of the Val d'Adige. Behind the parish with the altar of Schnatrepeck.

On the acropolis of Cori, built between '89 and '80 B.C. by the magistrates Marco Maglio and Lucio Turpilio, whose names are engraved on the architrave of the door; it is a Doric temple reinterpreted in an italic key, with the pronao of eight columns in travertine about 7 meters high, trigliph frieze and metope. National monument since 1898, dominates the Pontina Plain.
Shaded paths in the woods around the village, among rocky walls, rich vegetation and viewpoints on the valleys.
Geosite on the slopes of Monte Barbaston, rock exploited since ancient times for millstones and pots in ollar stone; by car to Cloutraz and then on foot.
A peasant house as it was, between popular devotion and ex-vote.
The village of the Malavoglia, between boats and granite.

Locality of the Riviera del Conero divided between Numana Alta, the ancient village on a promontory with the Costarella and the Arch of Torre, and Numana Bassa with the marina and the long beach towards Marcelli. The state Antiquarium exhibits the tomb of the Queen of Sirolo, the Sanctuary of the Crucifix a Byzantine wooden crucifix.
Sacred art in the valley above the lake.
The castle door.
A fifteenth-century church, today deconsecrated, with one of the most beautiful cycles of frescoes in Friuli, painted between 1498 and 1522 by Martino da Udine called Pellegrino da San Daniele.

On a spur of Monte San Martino (850 m) above Campi, the remains of a large building of the II-IV century A.D., probably a sanctuary dedicated to female deities, built on places of worship more ancient and frequented until the Middle Ages; the finds are at the Museum of Riva. Always open.

On the left bank of Lake Patria, north of Cuma, rise the remains of Liternum, Roman maritime colony founded in 194 BC for veterans of the second Punic war: forum, Capitolium, basilica, theatre, a stretch of Via Domitiana and, little to the south, the amphitheatre.

A corridor tomb between the seventeenth and fifteenth centuries BC, the best preserved of the Murgian territory: a cell of about 2 for 1,6 meters, 1.80 meters high, closed by three plates and covered by a 2.40 for 3.80 meters, with a 10 meters long access corridor facing east; identified in 1909 by Angelo Mosso and Francesco Samarelli.
A Baroque façade in front of the Waldensian temple.
Walking street with historical buildings and cafes, dominated by the bell tower of San Giorgio in the shape of a Doric column with the statue of the saint on top.
The great forest of the south-east of Sardinia.
The walls become park.
Birdwatching and bike around the karst lake of the Ciociaria.

Borgo 4 km from the capital, on top of a road that rises to 869 meters between ancient oaks and chestnut groves; in the nearby woods remain fragments of the Via Vandelli, the road between Emilia and Tuscany of 1749 that takes its name from Domenico Vandelli, who directed the construction.
The convent linked to the source of St. Francis.

Fortress of federician age with square courtyard with corner towers and rustic fender, 360 meters on the road between Bari and Taranto, with pre-Norman, Norman and Swabian phases and restorations of the twentieth century. Since 1977 it houses the National Archaeological Museum with the findings of Monte Sannace: geometric vases, kantharoi, attic, ionic and corinthian ceramics, a gorgonic antefix and a black figure crater of the painter of Memnon. Open 8:30-19:30, calendar Sundays.

The heart of the ancient Nuceria Alfaterna: the early Christian baptistery of Santa Maria Maggiore, the Rotonda, the great Hellenistic-Roman theatre of Pareti, the domus of the Decumano with mosaics and frescoes and the archaeological park with walls and necropolis.
A late antique village-fortress remained almost intact.
The working history of the mine and the first major strike.
Built in the 15th century as the residence of Archduke Sigismondo, it is one of the most complete and best preserved castles in South Tyrol.
The Early Christian Round.
The starry sky of the Lodigian plain by the telescope.
The testimonies of Russia's retreat.
From the silkworm to the fabric, in the granaries of the convent.
Started in 1257 as the safest papal seat in Rome, with the acute arched loggia; it houses the Hall of the Conclave, where the cardinals were locked up until they elected the pope.
It starts from Zogno and runs for 21 km to Piazza Brembana with 200 meters of difference in altitude, on the path of a former railway: the gentle slope makes it suitable for everyone.
Wide and free beaches of the Riviera dei Fiori.

The highest artificial basin in Sicily, about 1,000 meters away, supplies with drinking water much of the internal Sicily; it is surrounded by 4,200 hectares of state forest in the Nebrodi Park, suitable for walking and horseback riding.
The neoclassical theatre of the ducal city.
The gulf from the walk.

The expansive delight built for "schivar la borezo": the Salone dei Mesi, frescoed for Borso d'Este by Francesco del Cossa, Ercole de' Roberti and the Ferrara school, is the largest profane cycle of the Renaissance.
Pomili's painting.
A walk through boats and pine forests.

Monumental tree of 1370, considered the largest plane tree in Italy: over 25 meters high, about 15 meters in circumference and a crown of 300 m2. In 1937, during the Army's Great Summer Maneuvers, a company of one hundred Bersaglieri hid among its branches; in 1944 the German troops tried to thin it out for fear of partisan ambushes.

In the workshops founded in 1840 by Ferdinando II of Borbone, the first Italian locomotive factory, next to the first railway of Italy Naples-Portici, the museum of the FS Foundation with locomotives and historical carriages overlooking the gulf.
