On the hill of Montelce, according to legend, is the tomb of Asdrubale, the Carthaginian leader defeated by the Romans in the battle of Metauro (207 BC); Montaigne, Giacomo Leopardi and Giovanni Pascoli would pass there.
Carruggi, loggia and traces of the medieval port.

Village of medieval origin at about 1,320 meters, at the foot of Monte Calvario and at the edge of the plateau of the Cinquemiglia, between the parks of Abruzzo and Majella; it preserves doors and fortifications and the church of San Nicola di Bari, and is known for the living nativity scene, among the oldest in Italy, held every 5 January since 1951.

Under the grassy slopes of the Paularo, Dimon and Neddis mountains, frequented in every season, the Dimon lake (1852 m); the 14.8 km ring (about 875 m of altitude difference, 5 hours and 20, difficulty T2) starts from Castel Valdajer. In summer, the Zermula, Lodin Alta and Pizzul mountain huts offer dairy products and local specialities.

Founded by the Annibaldi in the 13th century, it remains the mastic and counter tower called "maletto"; the Caetans expanded it and created the Camere Pinte. Towers, bastions, gun square with cistern, Hall of the Cardinal of the sixteenth century and kitchen with large fireplace; restored by Gelasio Caetani and managed by the Fondazione Roffredo Caetani. Set of "We only have to weep" and "The story of the stories."
The peak-utopia of the prophet, with a view of the Amiata.
The highest point of the village, between Ionian and Aspromonte.
By bike or by canoe along a river of rise.

Settling perched on a bargage spur, probably Celto-ligure and then Roman, became Lombard fortification and castle around the year 1000: defensive village where food and flocks were kept. It preserves Celtic ares with votive cups, a high stone tower, a viscontea fortress with ghibelline merlons and monofores added by the Visconti in the fourteenth century, and the chapel of Saints Antoninus and Anna with Romanesque apse and fourteenth-century frescoes. It was the Guala di Casallone (1200), the Visconti (1300) and the Avogadro (1400-1800); since 1978 it is of the Cavallari family, who restores it as a dwelling and uses it in part for events, exhibitions and fairs.
The artificial hill formed by the ridges of the amphorae discharged into the ancient river port, with caves at the base today trattorie.
Science and historical collections of the University, good with the boys.

Designed by Ciro Ciri with Francesco di Giorgio Martini and built between 1485 and 1498 for Ferdinando I d'Aragona on the Swabian fortifications: irregular pentagonal plant surrounded by the moat, three cylindrical towers and a rampart to launch towards the sea with the 1578 ramps, the coats of arms of Antonio de Mendoza and Pedro de Toledo and the great coat of arms of Carlo V on the portal.
The place not to be missed by Leonessa.

Camp wanted by Settimio Severo around 202 AD for about 6,000 legionaries of the II Legion Partica, on about 10 hectares: there are still sections of walls, towers and doors. The Porta Pretoria, main entrance from Via Appia, 36 m wide and 14 m high on two floors, was brought to light by the bombings of 1944; next door is the Porta Principalis Left.
Teodolinda's treasure.
On the shores of the lake, it preserves frescoes from the thirteenth century in the right aisle.
The oldest church on the belvedere.
The ancient village on the sea.
The castle over the valley.
The stone houses that tell the Albanian origin of the country.
A piece of the Middle Ages in the country.
The view of the Locride.
The heart of Florence, free.

Cittadina del Ponente Genovese with the longest seafront of the Riviera di Ponente, about 3 km of beach, a historic center of carruggi and ancient lime kilns and the house that tradition indicates as the birthplace of Christopher Columbus; in the hinterland of Sciarborasca the house peasant museum.
The exhibitions of the moment in the center.

The church, which the Municipality defines as a masterpiece, overlooks Piazza Orsini del Balzo and has a history linked to that of the castle; it is one of the four Baroque churches of the itinerary  "Mesagne," the Baroque heart of Salento.
The Roman ships sunk by the Vandals in the harbor.

Archaeological civic museum inaugurated in 2016 in the former barracks of the Guardia di Finanza, Liberty building built after the earthquake and tidal wave of 1908, recognized as a museum of regional interest in 2019. It exhibits the findings of the territory from the excavations of the Superintendence (1995-2004): the cleft of Ferrina dedicated to Demeter (III century BC), the materials of the fortress of Santo Niceto, the remains of the Roman villa with mausoleum, the lead slingshots of the X Legio Fretensis and a Jewish skylight of the IV-V century A.D. with the menorah, exhibited in 2017-2018 at the MEIS in Ferrara. Open every day 9-12.30 and 16-20 (Common); access with stairway, without ramp or elevator.
The most famous body shop prototypes.
A cappuccino cloister in the centre of Arco.
One of the first printers in Italy.
A page Visit Trentino also calls it "UO.MO" , name to verify.
Closed since 1995 to protect bats; visitable in summer with the Speleological Group L'Orso di Castell'Azzara
The village of wool around the abbey.
Paths between the Alps and the plain.
By bike along the water.
Outside the walls, connected to the Fortress by an underground passage, it is decorated with frescoes by Giulio Campi.
The Norman tower and the Guevara wall garden.
Alvignanello's devotional treasure, from ex-vote to vestments.

In the former headquarters of the National Opera Fighters, about a thousand finds tell the story of the population and the Pontine territory in the twentieth century, from the swamp to the reclamation.
The city's covered market, indicated in the official tourist map of Lombardy Region.
On Mount Guardia, around a neoclassical building, founded in 1980: a circular path with over 70 native species and some rare orchids at risk of extinction.
Sulphur, liberty and murals on a walk.
Church with Romanesque tower.
€7 whole; €5 reduced (15-17 years, over 65); free up to 14 years
Better in spring and autumn.
The routes between sea and mountains.

The cyclopic papal fortress, born from events related to the salt trade, at the southern end of the historic centre; after the restorations you cross on foot, with escalators and tunnels, in the subsoil of the city.
The costume of Busachi and linen, from flower to embroidery.
Wild island known since ancient times for its thermal baths and healing mud, with the sea heated by fumaroles and black sandy beaches; the crater of the Fossa di Vulcano is the stop not to be missed.
recorded by the MiC among abandoned cultural heritage; status and accessibility not indicated
Panorama to Montecassino.

The main church of the ancient village, dedicated to the Assumption and frescoed. It is believed that Isabella Morra is buried in the basement: in 1928 Benedict Cross had excavated there to search for her tomb, without success.

White shrine at 600 meters, at the highest point of the island above the hamlet of Cure, built on the site of a pagan building and rich in ex-vote; it is considered among the oldest places of Marian worship in Italy. Walk up (about 4 km and 1 hour and 30 from Peschiera Maraglio, path no. 1) or by minibus, with dedicated summer rides; near refreshment and picnic area.
Antonio da Fabriano and the story of Leo XII.

The capital of the National Park of the Archipelago of La Maddalena, the first of Sardinia (1994), with more than 60 islands: in Caprera, united by a bridge-diga, the Compendio garibaldino where Garibaldi lived 26 years; in the city the Diocesan Museum with Nelson silvers and the naval museum of the wreck of Spargi.
open only on request (tel. 0323 885101)
The Gothic vaults of the Bishopric.
steep paved streets with river pebbles, stone fountains, granite portals and flowered wood balconies.

Santu Lussurgiu is a medieval village 500 meters on the south-eastern side of Montiferru, inside an ancient volcanic cone, known for carpets, knives and saddles. It preserves the churches of Santa Croce and Santa Maria degli Angeli and the Museum of Agricultural Technology; in the nearby woods there are the village of San Leonardo di Siete Fuentes and the waterfall of s'Istrampu de sos Molinos.

Church in the hamlet of Clenia with late-Gothic apse that houses a golden altar of 1601-1602, then modified by Bartolomeo Ortari; on the walls of the aisle there is a cycle of frescoes from the fifteenth century.
The heart of devotion to the three holy brothers.
The warm waters that gave the city its name.
A Roman lion on a medieval fountain.
One of the best preserved castles in the South.
The life of a manor house in Sarcidano.

In the rooms of the second level of the castle, connected to the path of the noble palace, he exhibits in five rooms and twelve windows a sample of the about 30,000 excavations carried out in the castle between 1993 and 1997 by Marcello Rotili: painted ceramics and protomaiolica (XIII-XIV century), graffite (XIV-XV), cooking vases, majolica in blue, and six-seventh-century dishes with the coat of arms of the Caracciolo. The route passes through the former hanging garden, which gives access to the defenses and tower.
The 18th century stone portals.
A historic local market.

In the building of the bus station: materials of local culture including ancient measuring instruments, a plastic of the center as it was before the deviation of the Panaro (1880-1886) and a section on the final Jewish community of the late nineteenth century.
From the fourteenth century, with paintings from the seventeenth and eighteenth centuries.
The striped dome and the Neapolitan canvas of the eighteenth century.

Fortress of the 13th century on opholithic cliffs overlooking the Mozzola stream, among the possessions of the Marquis Pallavicino from the early thirteenth century: here in 1269 he died besieged the leader Uberto Pallavicino called the Great. Today remains the ruins.

The most interesting monument of the village, around which was born in the early eighteenth century the first inhabited nucleus; it has the façade in lava stone and since 1811 is sacramental church by decision of the Archbishop of Messina. The Metropolitan City dates back to the seventeenth century, italia.it places its construction between the eighteenth and nineteenth centuries.
By bike on the Bucket under the steel arch.

Villa liberty built in 1911-1916 for Count Lodovico Mazzotti Biancinelli on a project by Antonio Vandono di Cortemiglia and Alessandro Citterio, with peristyle, skylight and original furnishings; his son Franco was among the creators of the Mille Miglia. The park of about ten hectares, redesigned in 1927, has fountains, outdoor theatre, gazebo and statues; it is open free (9-17 in winter, 9-20 in summer), the villa only for events, on request or with guided tours.
Gothic church that dominates the valley, with works by Duccio di Buoninsegna and Guido da Siena and the relic of Santa Caterina, lived in Siena in the fourteenth century.
Bosco consecrated to Jupiter by the Romans, refuge of hermits from the sixth century, with the Hermitage of St. Francis of 1218 and the church of St. Julian.

The river that gives the name to the municipality was born in the Panic Valley; a ring path of about 4 hours, from the road to Calcara, goes up the high valley to the Callarelle waterfall and continues up to Ussita.
XV century church in Monteortone, with the stone portal of Istria of Matthew and Thomas Allio (1667).
The first village of the Aosta Valley coming from Piedmont, born around the spectacular Roman bridge in a single span on Lys.
The most famous "tropical" sea on the coast of San Teodoro.

Inside the Fortress, parish since 1948: two rooms connected by a triple arch. The oratory, before 1201, preserves the Adoration of the Magi of Niccolò dell'Abate and a 16th-century fresco of San Giovanni Battista in a stuccoed ancon; the church of Saints Peter and Paul, with a single nave without facade, has two works by Francesco Viacavi (late 17th century) and a wooden pulpit of the eighteenth century.
15th century church along the road to Mogliano, with a fresco of the Madonna and Child considered miraculous over the centuries.
Church of 1546 annexed to the convent of the Capuchins, with the paved cloister in bricks and the well; today in the complex are the museum and the historical archive, with documents from 1213.

Church of the fourteenth century with the convent of the Friars Minor, rebuilt in the nineteenth century, with Ferrara and Emilian painting of the fourteenth century and a Pietà attributed to Tullio Lombardo.
17th century Sanctuary in panoramic position, with Baroque frescoes and a altarpiece of the Scalvini.
The pilgrim church.
Terraced gardens at the top of the Pigna, created since 1754 on the site of a Genoese castle.

From the central square starts the visit of the village, which grew lower than the hill where at the beginning of the thirteenth century the fortified village arose; in 1303, after the victory of the Florentines over the Pistoiesis, the castle was conquered and destroyed and few traces remain.

Easy theme path for children, inspired by a fairy tale on the animals of the forest (caprioli, badgers, wild boars, hares, ibex): starts from the square of Palazzo Veneziano at Casa Krahvogl, crosses a forest of pine, hornbeam and ash trees and rises to the clearing of the chapel of Calvary, panoramic, with return along the ancient Via Crucis. At least an hour.

The centre of the Savovato valley with the Museum of Sacred Art "San Giuseppe" which collects works from the sixteenth to the eighteenth century of the local master carvers, and in the territory the section of the Middle Savovato with the waterfall of the Cannavina and the ancient bridges.
To understand how glaciers and water have drawn the Great Paradise.
A five-sixth-century oratory.
Three hundred in the square.

The basalt plateau was born from a lava flow of 2-5 million years ago, in the form of a 'T' inverted, of about 2,5 per 1,5 km and about 360 meters high, covered with stain and cork; it houses about twenty nuraghi and the sacred source Conca 'e sa Cresia, and from above you can see Campidano, Marmilla, Gennargentu and on clear days the sea.
The lake of the Park between woods and mountains.
The largest state forest in Italy, 24,000 hectares, covered by hiking, horse riding and mountain biking trails that reach huts and huts.
The vaporous caves above the city.
Hiking on the paths once used by smugglers to Switzerland.
Dragon teeth at high altitude above Resia.

The largest fortified complex in the Camonica Valley, which controlled the passage between Lower and Middle Valley: it preserves traces from the medieval fortification to towers-residence and palaces of the XII-XVI centuries, under sieges in the Middle Ages and was abandoned in 1598. Inside the medieval church of San Michele, the oldest monument of Breno, a noble house-tower and the 20-metre tower can be visited; today it houses concerts, re-enactments and archery competitions with wide meadows.
Nature protected a stone's throw from the beaches.

In the center there are sacred places of the eighteenth and nineteenth centuries, including the churches of the confraternities of the Battuti Bianchi (San Bernardino) and the Battuti Neri (San Giovanni Decollato). On July 5, 1944 the bell tower of the Black Battuti was targeted by German machine guns; on the church of San Giovanni the recent restorations brought to light a fascist writing painted on the wall.

Borgo Gonzaghesco sul Po, collected around the scenic Piazza XXIII Aprile, porticoed and remained substantially unchanged from the seventeenth century; around the church of Santa Felicita, the small Jewish cemetery, the Theatre 900 and, beyond the embankment, the Garzaia Nature Reserve.
The hamlet-balcony on the gulf.
Between the basilica and the theatre.

Symbol of the municipality, on the gorge of the Val d'Ega: built in the 12th century as the seat of the Greifensteins, in the fourteenth century passed to the lords of Fiè, then to the balivo Heinrich Gessler and to the Counts Lichtenstain; it preserves almost intact the sixteenth-century appearance, with the rooms of the knights and an ancient chapel with valuable frescoes. Private, visit only with guide: April, May, June, September and October on Friday at 15, with telephone reservation.
Enter a nuragic village almost intact.

Ruins on the San Casto hill: born as a fortress Volsca, then Roman and Longobard, it was transformed by the Della Rovere in 1520 in the fortress reached until today; remains of the Roman castle are partly visible in the underground. It became a noble residence with Cantelmo, Della Rovere, Boncompagni and Borgia. It is a natural monument and can be reached on foot with CAI paths, with wide views of the city.

Bishop's fortress built in the second half of the fourteenth century by Archbishop Giacomo D'Atri on a structure of the thirteenth century, on the edge of a gravina, with a tower greater than twenty blackbirds, ground floor dug into tuff and sixteenth-century garden. Since 1999 its 11 rooms house the Ceramic Museum, about 500 works from the 8th century BC to today. Opening hours from the source italia.it: weekdays 10-13 and 15:30-19:30, Sunday 10:30-13 and 16:30-21.
Established by the Municipality in 2001 to preserve the heritage of local viticulture. For timetables and visits you can contact the Municipality (tel. 0141 959610).

Workshop of blacksmith ferraio of the early eighteenth century, only surviving among the artisan workshops of the country: in the first room the machines still work thanks to a hydraulic wheel. The forging room exhibits tools for iron processing, the last illustrates the construction of weights, sizes and staders; rich sample of locks and agricultural tools. Open on Sundays in the summer season (in 2025 from July 6 to October 19), free admission.
The medieval tower of the upper village.
Gate of the Roman city cut into the rock, at the foot of the sanctuary of Monte Sant'Angelo.

Private collection started in 1956 by Domenico Gentili: more than forty vintage cars, a dozen motorcycles and vintage bicycles in a 650 m2 shed, including the Zedel of Queen Margherita, the Fiat 527 Ardita of General Kesselring and the Alfa Romeo Arccia d'Oro of 1949. Open by reservation.
The Gothic-Catalan in red stone, with a view.

The peaks Cima Otto, Cima Nove, Cima Ten, Cima Eleven, Cima Twelve and Cima Una indicate the time of the day according to the position of the sun: a show that strikes especially on clear days in winter.
The two lakes, known as the Sperlonga's eyes, form part of the natural heritage of the territory.
You listen under a sound chandelier.
The viewpoint of Monte Berico next to the basilica, with views over the whole city and the plain.
The hamlet of the painted walls, with the Rocca and the Enoteca regionale in its cellars.
The small 19th century theatre in the Rocca Pallavicino, dedicated to the composer born a few kilometers, with audiences and decorated stages.

Historical capital of Lunigiana and border town between Liguria and Tuscany, a medieval village remodeled in Renaissance forms at the end of the fifteenth century: a walled center on the Via Francigena between Porta Parma and Porta Romana, two Medici fortresses (Firmafede and Sarzanello), the Teatro degli Imavevidi and the low and sandy sea of Marinella.
The arsenal-ferruginous waters of the Lagorai.
The history of the city-fortress.
The arena of the legionaries of Septimius Severus.

In the former church of Santa Caterina tells of the surgical school born in the Abbey of Sant'Eutizio: when in 1215 the Lateran Council IV prohibited clergy surgery, knowledge passed to the laity of Preci, surgeons requested until the sixteenth century at the courts of France and Spain and in the hospitals of Rome and Florence, specialists of cataracts and hernias; Andrea della Croce wrote the Surgery universalis opus absolutum. Exposed tools such as scalpels, pliers and needles.

In the seventeenth century Palazzo Tommasi Leschiutta, on three floors: prehistory of Carnia with the reconstruction of part of the necropolis of Misincinis (VIII-IV century BC), finds of forum, baths and domus of Zuglio with Pompeian frescoes of the frigidarium, and the life of the Roman city; also exhibits five wooden sculptures of the altar of Domenico da Tolmezzo recovered by the Carabinieri in 2016. Open Thursday-Sunday from June to October, Friday and Saturday from November to May.
The castle of Juliet and its terrace on the plain of Vicenza.
Wool and silk still produced in the village.

Torrente that descends from Monte Nerone in Candigliano; since 1960 its central stretch is a canyoning destination, with a path equipped with 12 descents, the highest of 25 meters. In the spring you will meet small tritons.
Art in the rooms of the castle.
The maze brings luck to lovers.
Facade in stone with a superb rosette and incredible decorative richness; inside the baptismal font of the thirteenth century and the Last Judgment frescoed in the fourteenth century.
The last court of the Della Rovere and its graphic collection.
Holy Week nissena.

Born in 1927 from the union of Sforzatica, Mariano and Sabbio, Dalmine is an industrial city grown around the seamless tube plant of 1906: the company town designed mostly by Giovanni Greppi from the 1920s, the anti-aircraft bunker of 1943 reopened to the public and a museum with over 900 nativity scenes.
Stories of mountain men and women.

Villafranca di Verona grew up around the Scaliger Castle, started in 1201 and restored in 2023 with insides and walkways to visit; at Palazzo Bottagisio, where in 1859 the two emperors of the Armistice stayed, the Museum of the Risorgimento is located, and along the course there are the Duomo and the Baroque church of the Discipline.
See how wheat was ground with water.

The peak is almost 1000 meters in the Aurunci Mountains Park, which the old shepherds call ... the Cima della Croce for a cross that once stood there; the view extends over the village, the Piana di Fondi, the Pontine Islands and the Abruzzo mountains.
Very degraded, with recovery programs: is observed from outside
You dig behind the theater.

Liberty villa of the early twentieth century in the historic center, birthplace of the poet and literary Cesare De Titta (1862-1933), who called it  "Cenacle of Fiorinvalle": there were artists and writers of Abruzzo of the time like D'Annunzio and Michetti, and also Pirandello and Gentile. It preserves the original furnishings, objects of the poet, postcards and vintage photos, a bust, the library and the historical archive; it is among the Italian museum houses recorded by the Ministry.
A break in the shade inside the walls.
A Romanesque-Gothic fortified abbey, several times among the Places of the FAI Heart.
Cited from 1208, rebuilt in late dogotic style by master Benedikt Weibhauser of Bressanone and consecrated in 1494; inside a folding illustrates its history and works.

It was originally built in 1185 and rebuilt in 1934-36 and has a small porch with inserts from the mosque of Rabato; inside the Madonna del Soccorso in marble carved in 1503 by Bartolomeo Berrettaro of Carrara for the Salamone family, whose tombs are in the chapel on the right of the choir.
The hamlet-balcony overlooking the Garda.
A medieval tower in the plain.

Lucan Country overlooking the Ionian, surrounded by the almost lunar landscape of the calanchi, home of the Amaro Lucano; it preserves the Mother Church of Saints Peter and Paul, the Abbey of Santa Maria del Casale and the Castle of San Basilio, with eight kilometers of beaches in Marina di Pisticci.
A museum that you listen to.

Built in 1810 instead of the Accademia degli Erranti, neoclassical, with five orders of stages and the Ridotto frescoed with golden stuccoes and mirrors; national monument, with guided tours in summer.
The hamlet of artists.
A village on stilts of six thousand years ago, a UNESCO site.
Sepulchral environment with thick walls of niches for cinerary urns.
The Benedictine monastery of Santa Maria di Palazzo, then Cistercian and later active pastoral church until the fifteenth century, was built on the acropolis of Iuvanum, above the oldest temples.

The Archivio di Stato, founded in 1858, constantly exhibits the Tablets of Biccherna: the painted covers of the registers of the financial judiciary of the Municipality, decorated from 1257, flanked by a documentary exhibition.
The basilica of the patron with the octagonal tower unfinished, overlooking the market square called by the Reggians Piasa Cèca.
The peasant life around Pastena oil.
A 16th century fresco.

Impressive castle in Romanesque style, between the residences of Frederick II, on a strategic hill overlooking the Calaggio valley and the borders of Irpinia, Lucania and Daunia; in the Middle Ages it was military-administrative district and last outpost of the Longobard Duchy of Benevento, and around the Mille belonged to the Landolfo and Pandolfo princes. From the top opens the view that is worth the name of the "Loggia delle Puglie" (Puglia Loggia).
The tour of the walls.

Country of the Picentini Mountains at 697 meters, at the foot of Mount Termino, overlooking the Dragon Plain, karst basin whose waters disappear in the swallowery of the Bocca del Dragone; on the hill the ruins of the castle of San Michele, in the village the Ethnographic Museum and the historic center with the Gothic houses.

In Spelonga, parish church of the second half of the fifteenth century with a Renaissance sandstone portal and a trussed cover; it houses 17th-century tempera, a 15th-century terracotta group, frescoes attributed to Panfilo da Spoleto and the Turkish flag that, according to tradition, a hundred Spelongans tore from an enemy ship in the battle of Lepanto (1571). Many goods come from St. Maria di Collepiccioni, destroyed in 1933; the "Festa bella" (Beautiful Festival) recalls Lepanto.
One of the most photographed villages of the Maremma.
Just a stone's throw from the centre, one of the largest outdoor markets in Europe.

Along the Rötbach copper was extracted for over 500 years: first citation in 1426, definitive abandonment in 1971, museum opened in 1996. A mine train takes more than a kilometer into the tunnel of Sant'Ignazio, excavated from 1761 and arrived at the deposit after 43 years; two ring routes with reconstructions show tools, machinery and life of the miners, and a preserved copper vein can be touched. Even today, cementation copper is obtained with the help of bacteria. Visits only by reservation, last entry at 15, closed on Mondays not festive and in winter until Easter.
The art of the painted cart.
The museum of the Cathedral of Cagliari, recommended by the Municipality in the itinerary of sacred art museums together with those of Bonaria and the Genoese.
The church of the first Mass of Padre Pio.
The Neolithic village of 40 hectares, one of the largest entrenched villages of the Tabletop; visits by reservation.
The fountain of the Bacchino, symbol of the city: the original is in the courtyard of the Town Hall, in the square a copy of the twentieth century.

Wine country on the Wine Road, about 18 km from Bolzano, overlooking Lake Caldaro, the largest and warmest bathing lake in South Tyrol: in the center the Provincial Museum of Wine and the market square from which the wine path starts, above the village the historic funicular Mendola of 1903 and in the surroundings the ice holes, the rastenbach gorge and the early Christian ruin of San Pietro in Altenburg.
The archaeology of the territory.

The village of the museums in the hills of the Gerrei, overlooking the valley of the Flumendosa and born around a nuraghe that rises in the middle of the houses; it is the birthplace of Emilio Lussu, remembered by a historical museum and the murals.
The view of the valleys.
An artist who tells himself about the walls of the house.
The look in the marble mountains.
Walk through historical buildings and shops.
The square and the palaces of the village.
On Piero's trail.
The baroque lounge of the village.

Small Romanesque church on the shore of Lake Capo d'Acqua, with arched porch mirrored in the water. Originally a single nave with narrow windows, in the eighteenth century it had three baroque altars; damaged in the Second World War. Its most important fresco, a Crucifixion of the 14th century, was detached and restored in 1973 and is today in the church of San Rocco, in the center of Castrocielo.
Born as a private chapel of the Federici family, it contains frescoes by Callisto Piazza dating back to 1526.
A curious memento mori of the eighteenth century at the entrance of a hamlet cemetery.

Fortified village documented since 1235 under the Basque family; in the middle of the sixteenth century, after a massacre, the inhabitants destroyed the castle and ruled themselves until the unification of Italy.
The equestrian statues of the Gonzaga in the palace of the duke.
A pilgrimage church with medieval roots.
The Blue Grotto by boat.
A century of food labels in a 19th century palace.

Only Romanesque part survived the eighteenth-century reconstruction of the abbey, stands for six floors in stone masonry marked by bands of hanging arches in terracotta, with narrow slits on the lower floors, a monofora in the fourth and pairs of double-fores in the fifth and sixth; inside a stone staircase rises up to the bell cell. You can see it from the outside.
The amphitheatre under the rose.

Overlooking the viewpoint of the old town, it was founded in the 16th century as a defensive structure and in the 18th century it was transformed into a fortified palace; it preserves ribbed cruising vaults and wolf windows. It houses the Museum of War for Peace.

Easy ring of about 6 km with minimal difference in altitude around the historic center, accessible all year round, which touches three natural waterfalls returned accessible thanks to recovery interventions; suitable for families.
The trullus domes of the Holy Spirit, curiosity of the ancient center.
Storks and ibis hermit at your fingertips.
Among ancient olive trees, the Messapian chamber tombs, sections of basalt roads and the amphitheatre built under Trajan (98-117 A.D.), confirmed by the excavations of 2011-2017.
The statues of the Roman theatre and the daily life of Falerio.
Free bridge; Room of the Heroines according to the times of the City
See live an infernot, the symbol of the UNESCO site.

On the hill of San Nicolò, about 1 km in front of the village: the church and the ancient hermitage collapsed with the earthquake of 1693, but the fresco of the Virgin and Child, of the sixteenth century, remained unharmed and was incorporated into the new sanctuary. The patroness is celebrated on the last Sunday of August.

Church of the patron, attested in 1136 and rebuilt in 1896 with facade in Romanesque style and Gothic interior with three naves. The nineteenth-century bell tower has a statue of the saint of Teodoro Coletti and Mariano Laura and a rare mechanical clock by Salvatore Salvatorelli that also marks days, months and phases of the moon. Within four terracotta altars (three designed by Nazareno Biscarini), a wooden crucifix, a seventeenth-century tabernacle, a Madonna enthroned and saints of Perugia school of the sixteenth century and the Incredulity of St. Thomas of Vincenzo Chialli (1831).
To be combined with the nearby tomb of Giants, to read a nuraghe "in section."
The monument symbol of the foundation.

Church of Norman origin with fifteenth-century portal surmounted by a bas-relief and two lions guarding the central gate, dated 1264. Inside there is a monumental Baroque wooden altar with a mother-of-pearl tabernacle, a fifteenth-century statue of the Madonna and Child, an Ecce Homo in 18th century terracotta, the relics of St. George and St. Francis of Paola, a collection of silver and the crypts of the early church.
The view of the center.
Medieval church of the patron saint of Mutignano, which preserves a triptych of the painter Andrea De Lithium.

In the old town, home to the Castromediano-Limburg family, recognizable by the bastion of lace. It was the Duke Sigismondo Castromediano, with his discoveries, who started the protection of the Messapian area from which the Museo Diffuso was born.
To understand the rite of snakes all year round, not only on May 1.

It rises on an islet of trachyte 113 meters high, joined to Ischia Ponte by a masonry bridge of about 220 meters. The first fortifications date back to 474 B.C. with Gerone I of Syracuse; in 1441 Alfonso V of Aragon made it a fortress with walls, towers and ramparts against pirates and dug into the rock a gallery of 400 meters. Inside churches, courtyards, convents and gardens, including the church of the Immaculate Church with the large dome and the Cathedral of the Assumption with frescoes of the sixteenth century; an elevator rises to 60 meters.
MiC card (updated 2020) indicates closed every day; visit to be agreed with the person in charge indicated on the card
The city of the bicycle.

In a 17th-century house in the historic centre, founded in 1991 by the artist Maria Petrucci in honor of his father Raniero: four rooms on several floors with wooden sculptures, oil paintings, the old fireplace, the orcs for oil and legumes and the studio of the artist; a fifth room collects objects of peasant life. Reservation not required according to the MiC card; tel. 0765 326248.

From the village you go up towards Monte Mirabello between olive groves and cherry trees, follow the panoramic ridge up to the Cross of Monte Bastia, with views of the Val Tramigna and the Val d'Illasi, you go down to Castelcerino and to the woods to Contrà Meggiano, returning among the vineyards to Piazza Castello. Recommended during the Cherry Festival, the second week of June.

Cemetery church on a rock spur overlooking the Sarca, above the Antica Vetreria, first documented in 1244; the decorations of the Baschenis began in 1461 and the frescoes of Simone II Baschenis are dated between 1519 and 1534. On the southern outer wall the Macabra Dance with the seven deadly sins, with the characters arranged according to the medieval social hierarchy; inside, on the north wall, the great fresco of 1534 with Charlemagne assisting the baptism of a catechumen by Pope Urban I, linked to the legend of the passage of the emperor.
The wax nativity scene in the lava cave.
Frabosa Soprana is part, with Prato Nevoso and Artesina, of the ski area of Mondolè, with 100 km of slopes and 30 lifts; in summer the Falesia dei Quarzini is a climbing wall.

Resurgent cave at the apex of the gorge above Stiffe, where an underground stream of water returns to light after about 3 km in the heart of the mountain; discovered for modern uses in 1906 during the works for a power plant, then destroyed in the Second World War, was equipped in the eighties and the tourist complex was inaugurated in 1991. The guided tour lasts 60 minutes on a route of about 1.4 km round trip with 150 steps, touching the Sala del Silenzio (the only dry environment), the Sala della Cascata, the Sala delle Concrezioni and the great environment of Lake Nero. Inside there are constant 9 °C: they serve jacket and closed shoes; ticket office every day 10-18, to be reached 20 minutes before the chosen time. The MiC card also mentions the museum of speleology (paleontology, mineralogy, geology, speleological photography), refurbished in 2020.
The hunting castle of Frederick II in Basilicata.
To be verified
From the village you can climb to the meadows of Valcava and Monte Treaso, from which you can enjoy an exceptional view.
Large green area a few minutes from the center, suitable for picnics, hiking, cycling and horseback riding.
The Franciscan church of the thirteenth century.
The bridge designed by Sergio Musmeci, built between 1967 and 1981, at the entrance of Potenza sud on the Sicignano-Potenza motorway.
45 min

Traditionally attributed to Count Ruggero in the 11th century and restored in 1595, it preserves a bell tower and walls with slits; a short distance is the Guardiola, massive defensive tower also with slits.
In Spinetta Marengo, the multimedia museum on the battle of 14 June 1800: causes, conduct and consequences of Bonaparte's enterprise.

Public garden wanted by Spontini on his property and dedicated to his wife Celeste, on a hill east of the village: a long tree-lined avenue leads to a grove and a balcony overlooking the valley of the Esino and, on clear days, on the Adriatic.
The thirteenth century, of great strategic importance, takes its name from the coins coined there; the circular tower, the belt and the ruins of the chapel, 15 minutes walk from the village.
The Pompeiana symbol.

In the eighteenth-century Cuttica palace of Cassine, part of the civic collections with the archaeological finds of Dertona, works such as the polyptych of the Coronation of the Virgin of Gandolfino from Roreto and a section on Napoleon and Marengo.
The city of time is divided between the high district of Piazza, on Monte Regale, and Breo at its feet, joined by the funicular of Giugiaro, with the fake dome of Andrea Pozzo and the sundials.
The life of Lussu in his home country.
The square near the funicular station, surrounded by ancient buildings.
The historic Trastevere market along the avenue of Trastevere.
The coats of arms of the Magnificent Homeland under the porch.

Rebuilt after the earthquake of 1688 with anti-seismic criteria, with regular plan, without walls and with large avenues; private palaces of the eighteenth century (Ciaburro, Ungaro, del Viceconte, Magnati, Nardella, Giordani, Carizza, Villa Langer) with portals to bugs and masks, and road plates and furnishings decorated in ceramic.
Ring of about 9 km with sea view between holm oaks, pine trees and arbutes, frequented by hikers and cyclists; on the promontory also a climbing cliff (grades 3b-7b+).
Bring home a handmade vancale.
Archaeology and granite.
private cellar; the source does not indicate times or ways of visiting, contact the cellar
The treasure of silver busts and the bishop's grave.
Village on the slopes of the castle hill, with medieval buildings and narrow and colorful alleys overlooking the plain and the sea; from the promontory once saw pirates and invaders.
The big square.
The early medieval frescoes.
The old seaside village preserves its structure intact, with narrow caruggi, arches and bridges covered around Via Aicardi and Via Ghiglino.

Fortification of the Copper Age (2500-2000 BC) on the slopes of Monte Baranta, about 3 km from the village, reoccupied in the ancient Bronze and to a lesser extent in Nuragic and Roman age. A wall of large rocks, almost 100 metres long, contains a horseshoe tower and rectangular huts; outside the walls a sacred area with about 80 thick stones arranged in a circle of about 10 meters and a village of seven rectangular huts.

In the historic center the Mother Church rises next to the ruins of the castle, built according to the Municipality by the Beneventan princes and by Ludovico II, then abandoned and demolished by decision of the authorities in the thirties of the twentieth century. The Madonna del Bosco is brought to the Mother Church in procession on Tuesday after Easter.

The city was founded in 1938 for miners of the Sirai-Serbariu basin: the large mine became the Coal Museum, the Phoenician and Carthaginian colony of Mount Sirai and the prehistoric necropolis of the territory.

Rural houses in raw earth built with poor materials found on the spot: walls of earth, clay, straw, chaff and pebbles, roof of tiles in brick on a frame of reeds sealed with mud; the name would come from the dialect "li pinge" the tiles. Their period of maximum diffusion was probably the beginning of the nineteenth century, when under the dominion of Murattiano the lands of the convents were distributed to the citizens; some exemplars are still seen walking through the country roads of the territory.
A Romanesque church on a Roman villa.

The smallest municipality in the province of Trieste, on the Karst at the Slovenian border: the fortified fortress with the sanctuary of the Assumption dominates the plateau, in Rupingrande the Carsica House tells about the peasant life of the nineteenth century and every two years it hosts the karst weddings.
The UNESCO World Heritage Buildings.
The Longobard core of the country.
Sawmills and mine along the stream.
€7, reduced €5, minor €1, family €12
the MiC card indicates to contact the Municipality for the visit and closed on the other days

Completed in 1893 by the inhabitants of the districts Baglio and Ficarra and enlarged in 1937, it has Latin cross plan, coffered ceiling with rosettes and artistic windows; on the main altar dominates the nineteenth century effigy of the Madonna della Catena, carried in procession on the first Sunday of September.
Energy and climate explained with laboratories.
The greenery on the Castle Hill, crossed downhill by a grove of acacias and elderberries, with the panorama of the city.
An amphitheatre in the rock.
Visitable with monthly guided tours and during events.
the city card indicates it as not accessible, while reporting opening hours
One of the most beautiful springs of Pollino.
The complex of Villa Vitali brings together the Polar Museum Silvio Zavatti, the Ornithological Museum Tommaso Salvadori, the Pipe Museum and a collection of photographic devices.
In the hamlet of Paravati, large church of 3,000 places linked to Natuzza Evolo, a destination of numerous pilgrimages.
Private baroque in a palace.

Relief between Riva and Torbole, a protected area for Mediterranean flora and orchids and inhabited by rare Mediterranean birds, with ancient olive groves; it was the fulcrum of the Austro-Hungarian defensive system at the border with the Kingdom of Italy. The ring of 6.1 km (about 3 hours) of the Path of Peace from Porto San Nicolò touches Forte San Nicolò (1860-62), Forte Sant'Alessandro (1881) on the summit, Batteria di Mezzo (1900) and Forte Garda (1907).
A century and a half of Lario boats in an old spinning mill.

The Capuchin friars settled in Caraglio in 1611, restored the churches in ruins and distinguished themselves during the plague of 1630. The former convent, renovated, is the seat of the Cultural Association Marcovaldo; next to the former Romanesque church of Saints Peter and Paul with wooden altar, under restoration.

The tower of the twelfth century, at the highest point of the village, is the only survivor: square base with base to escarpment and the Beneventana Port, ancient entrance on the road to Benevento; watched over the valley of the Miscano and the border between the domains of Benevento and Puglia. It is surrounded by a defensive castle in Gothic style, in local grey stone, with five entrance doors, repeatedly damaged by earthquakes and transformed over the centuries.
On St. Martin's Square, it housed the tavern, the theatre and the prisons, completed in 1711; italia.it signals feudal prisons among things to see.

Italy.it signals the clear sea and bathing, the evening walks on the seafront when the lights of the coast and the mouths of Platani, Verdura and Magazzolo, where the encounter of the waters creates suggestive landscapes; Seccagrande is the seaside hamlet that arose after the 1960s, with villas and houses used especially in summer.
The "men of stone" wrapped in legends.

Built in several phases in four centuries: the pentagonal tower was wanted in 882 by Docibile I, ipato of the Duchy of Gaeta, to spot Saracen raids; the nephew Marino I added the square mastium and around 1250, with the Caetani, rose the cylindrical tower called the Crocodile, linked to the legend of a reptile in the moat. Inside the private chapel of the Caetani with a fresco of Sant'Antonio Abate and a panoramic terrace on the Ulysses Riviera; from the cavea you can see Vico Giudea, the ancient Jewish ghetto.
A Roman city overlooking Argentario and Giglio.
The heart of the old town at the foot of the castle, reached by the Porta Navina of 1560: houses and palaces porticoed, the Palazzo del Comune, the church of San Francesco rebuilt in 1788.
The richest Alpine Gothic in the valley.

Summer residence built in the early nineteenth century for Francesco Melzi d'Eril, Napoleon's ally; the villa remains private and closed, but the English garden, designed by Luigi Canonica and by the botanist Luigi Villoresi (authors also of the Park of Monza), stretches for almost a kilometer along the lake. You can visit exotic plants, sculptural groups (including Dante and Beatrice), the Moorish temple, the Japanese pond with water lilies, the chapel and a small museum; open every day 10-19 (ticket office until 6.30 pm) from the end of March to the beginning of November.
Frescoes and the crucifix of the thirteenth century.
The halls with the Dogi medallions.

Museum dedicated to the work of the sculptor and artist Pino Pascali, born in Polignano and died in the 1960s, in the former municipal slaughterhouse: Italia.it indicates it as the only permanent museum of contemporary art of Puglia and hosts contemporary art exhibitions. Open from Wednesday to Sunday, 10-13 and 16-20.
The Federici's manor above the valley.
The sixteenth-century sanctuary next to the museum.
Beach of stones in locality Calozzo, quiet and isolated; the area is windy and lends itself to windsurfing and kitesurfing with departure directly from the shore.

Medieval village of the Costa degli Etruschi with paved alleys, the parish church of Sant'Ilario and the Renaissance Santa Maria della Pietà; in the territory the Etruscan tombs of the Palazzino and the yellow caves, the Macchia della Magona and, on the sea, the Fort of the Cavalleggeri and the Blue Flag beaches of Marina di Bibbona.

Project realized in 2010 and among the first paintings in Molise: 8 large murals, 2 collectives and 6 individuals, of internationally renowned artists under the artistic direction of Lorenzo Canova. In 2011 two murals by Alessia Cerio were added dedicated to the grape harvest and pressing, in a corner of the village with arches and stone steps.
The main road with porticos and paintings by the artist Vincenzo Piccato inspired by nature and wine.
Aironi, ibis, spatula and the rare little bitch.
Deer and deer in the woods and the view of Borta Melone.

Built between 1579 and 1586 for Alfonso II d'Este on a medieval village, the last bulwark of the Duchy of Ferrara on the border with Lucca; in the Napoleonic age passed to the Principality of Lucca and Piombino and in the twentieth century was summer residence of the Italian-Scotland family Bechelli, who transformed a building into a liberty villa. Since 1980 it has been of the Province of Lucca and houses provincial offices and the Park of the Apuan Alps: about 1,150 meters of wall with 7 bastions enclose the house of the captain and the quarters of the troops of the sixteenth century, on about 60,000 m2. Exhibitions and events, including the festival "Mont'Alfonso" under the stars "Stars," and 360 degree views of the Tuscan-Emilian Apennines, Pania and Apuane.
Mount of 1,027 meters with rocks rich in marine fossils, hiking and cycling routes to the summit.

In the valley below the village, is for VisitLatium the most precious jewel of Ausonia: upper church of the fifteenth century and crypt with a cycle of frescoes dedicated to Saint Remicarda. Seriously damaged in World War II, it has been restored.

Ancient church of the historic nucleus of Romano Banco, already the parish centre on which Buccinasco depended; according to the report of Cardinal Ferrari's pastoral visit in 1901 dates back to 1196.
The birthplace of the first Italian Nobel laureate for medicine, told with his instruments.

Small village perched on the hillside in the Mongia torrent valley, in the Mongia Valleys and Cevetta Langa Cebana: the castle, one of the best preserved of the ancient marquisate of Ceva, houses the Bonaparte Museum on the countryside of Italy of 1796; around the archaeological area of the Colle di Sant'Andrea and the natural bridge of the Masentine.
Walk in the footsteps of Waldensian history in the upper Germanasca Valley.
Small church of the Upper Borgo, called at the Arapezzzana: above the portal a 11th-XII century bezel depicts Christ with the book of life between two kneeling angels and hooded monks.
A medieval fresco rediscovered in the countryside.

The center preserves the medieval system with Romanesque, Gothic and sixteenth-century architectures; of the walls remains little, including the Porta di Santa Maria in corso Giolitti, built between the fifteenth and sixteenth centuries. To see the church of the Holy Trinity, called "la Rossa" and the Santissima Annunziata, "la Bianca" (the White), a Piedmontese baroque with a Greek cross designed by Francesco Gallo; recently restored the chapel of St. James.
Small lake with views of Monte Camicia and the Leomogna valley, with the panoramic church of Santa Maria in Pagliara.
The nature of western Friuli.

On the summit of the Mount of the Madonna, second relief of the Euganean Hills, a church is already attested by a testament of 1253; in 1508 Pope Julius II entrusted it to the Abbey of Praglia. Rebuilt largely in 1940, it has next to a small monastery with cloister built between 1955 and 1965; the restoration brought to light the walls of the sixteenth century chapel and in the presbytery there is a Madonna with the fourteenth-century Child in polychrome stone attributed to Andriolo de' Santi. On Sundays and holidays, the monks of Prague celebrate there.

Behind Piazza XXVII January and facing the sea and Procida, it was built in the seventeenth century by Cardinal Ascanio Filomarino and dedicated to the Assumption; enlarged in the eighteenth and nineteenth centuries, took its present form at the end of the nineteenth century. It preserves the statue of the Assumption of the Neapolitan sculptor Francesco Verzella (1814) and an ancient image of the Madonna considered miraculous, destination of the faithful on 15 August.
The old fishing village beyond the Ponte di Tiberio, with colorful houses and murals dedicated to Fellini's films.
The heart of the Piazza district with the palaces of the Governor, of Città and Fauzone, which tell over eight centuries of history.
The village's life revolves around the marina, with the row of colorful boats docking and departing and the fish market.

A labyrinth of paved streets, stone houses and squares on the edge of the ravine, with the two medieval districts dominated by the cathedral, the church of Purgatory (Santa Maria del Suffragio) and the Four Fountains.
The brick tower made with the furnaces of the house.
The Baroque "Spanish" of the Friars Minor.
A neoclassical theatre.
The tour of the walls of the Venetian fortress.
Founded in 1475 by Roberto Orsini and modified by various reconstructions.

Open air theatre inspired by Greek tradition, where before 1908 there was the Pier of Porto Salvo. At the top, almost at sea, the marble chip of 1932 by the Messinian sculptor Bonfiglio dedicated to Vittorio Emanuele III, with the bronze statue of Athena Promachos.

A Visconti castrum novum is documented at the end of the fourteenth century, renovated by Pandolfo III Malatesta and with a revelt of the sixteenth century; in 1701 Eugenio of Savoia used it at the Battle of Chiari. Of the five-door walls there is nothing left on the surface, but the quadrangular plan and the corner towers of the fortress are read in the building that dominates Martiri della Libertà square, and the ring road follows the moat.
Streets with stone houses and some elegant buildings, with panoramic views that connect the main points of interest.

One of the most important towns of the Lower Valtellina, of medieval origins, at the entrance of the Val Gerola: in Piagno remain the bell tower and the apse of the priory of Cluniac of San Pietro in Vallate, founded in 1078, and in the village of Sacco a picta room of 1464 preserves the famous figure of the Homo selvadego.
The Dominican cloister.
A staircase to the Byzantine fort.
An island mountain above the plain, with views and ruins.
The story of a stronghold on Via Emilia.
A farm of Roman wine with its press.
Building built by the Florentines at the beginning of the fifteenth century, after the submission of Arezzo to Florence; it preserves a fresco of the Annunciation of 1610.
At the top of the old village, towards the hill, there are still walls and a tower of the fortress around which Marano grew, passed between Este, Pico, Rangoni, Pio di Carpi and Montecuccoli.

Villa of the sixteenth century with a representative room, the Barchessa, frescoed in the eighteenth century; on the other side you can see the historic Mira Lanza factory, which for decades produced candles and detergents.
The Tuscan landscape of a local painter.
The medieval bridge of the village.
Old town, monuments and municipal museums only partially usable (Let's Marche)
The castle of Verona overlooking the Mincio.
In the former Peroni brewery of the early twentieth century designed by Gustavo Giovannoni, the "Museum for Preventive Imagination."
Cellina's original turbines.
To be checked: visits and tastings for a fee
The nineteenth-century building (1840) delimiting Piazza del Ferrarese, designed with the Margaret Theatre and the Murat Room at the Polo delle Arti Contemporanee.
The shirts of the greats of cycling.

Cittadina dell'Oltrepò Mantua inhabited by Etruschi and Romans and then dominion of Bonacolsi and Gonzaga until the eighteenth century; it is known for the Suzzara Prize, born in 1948, whose Gallery preserves works of the realism season, and preserves the Civic Tower, the only rest of the ancient castle.
One of the most famous beaches in Europe.
The brig papers.
A Roman city on the coast.

The old quarter, with alleys, palaces and noble villas along the main streets; on the main street residences of the eighteenth and early nineteenth century and family shops, once tailors and shoemakers, today fashion shops and handicrafts. The village was defended by the castles of the Tower and San Pietro and the Rocchetta, which guarded the road near the gorge of the Walnut.

Città della Brianza known for its MAC, the contemporary art museum born from the collection of the Lissone Prize (1946-1967), and for the rationalist Palazzo Terragni; in the center the prepositural of Saints Peter and Paul, with a bell tower of more than 77 meters.
The Roman Rieti under the streets.
A fourteenth-century church rebuilt in Gothic-Lombard, with works of more than centuries.
The Shroud.

Church mother, born in the second half of the 10th century in place of Santa Maria ad duas Basilicas (V century), destroyed by the earthquake of 1456 and rebuilt between 1695 and 1725 on a project by Francesco Ferradini with Greek cross; the appearance is largely baroque.
Theatre of late 19th century Italian on the course, with trapezoidal plan, with baroque façade and frescoes.
The ancient landing and arching of the boatmen under the great walls of the left bank of the Po, today place of nightlife, dedicated to Fred Buscaglione and Gipo Farassino.
The starting point to understand the Sardinian castles.

The village is surrounded by medieval walls with gates and towers, including the Tower of Ponente that still bears the coat of arms of the Municipality; in July the Palio delle Boache carries the boats shoulder-to-shoulder up the alleys up to the Rocca.
The high-altitude war told by glacier finds.
Millennia of prehistory in one park.
€3, children 11-17 years €2, free up to 10 years and members WWF

In the seventeenth century Palazzo Gavotti the Pinacoteca Civica and the collection of the Milena Milani Foundation in memory of Carlo Cardazzo, with works by Arp, de Chirico, Fontana, Magritte, Mirò and Picasso, connected to the Ceramic Museum.

Late-Byzantine rocky settlement in the Canalotto valley, with two two-storey churches dug into the rock and about thirty caves used as dwellings or shelters for animals, overlooking the Erei Mountains.
The church-symbol signed by Morandi.
Palace overlooking the harbor, with painted decorations trompe-l'œil on the facade.
A Romanesque high ground parish with a thousand years of history.
The remains of the fortress above the village.
The promenade of Roseto is awarded with the Blue Flag; the beach, also the one in front of the castle, is several times nominated for the "Places of the Heart" of the FAI.

The castle was built in the Arab age on a hill on the left of the Verdura with the name of Misilcassin, fortified by the Normans and named in the sixteenth century to Diana Moncada, he married in 1511 Count Gian Vincenzo Luna; the earthquakes of 1578 seriously damaged him. The irregular plan of about 3,000 m2 in sandstone remains part of the walls, an angular bastion and a cylindrical tower 25 meters high with cruising vault ribbed on octagonal plan, typical of the Swabian age.
In Piazza XX Settembre.
The statue of Matidia, sister-in-law of Hadrian.

It dates back to 1502; according to tradition in 1512 Our Lady appeared to the young Pierina Carobbio, called Petruccia, in a place dominated by a large ash, from which the name. It preserves the Polyptych of the Visitation of Santacroce, a family of painters from the Val Brembana, also active in Venice. It is an important devotional place in a panoramic position on the Val del Riso, reachable with a climb of about 5 minutes.
A rare prehistoric funeral ritual visible from close up.
The great neoclassical theatre built between 1852 and 1857, seat of the Paolo Borciani Prize for string quartet.
A miniature Pantheon.

The current temple was inaugurated in 1846, after more modest buildings existing since the mid-500s; floor (1925) and wooden galleries (1938) give it an excellent acoustic appreciated for concerts, and the bell tower houses the municipal clock.
Renovated in 1777, it is dedicated to Saint Valentine, patron saint of children and lovers, and preserves paintings and sculptures, including a reconstruction of the Lourdes Cave.
For the table of Niccolò Alunno.
The Roman sea of Torre Astura.

Next to the Cathedral, built at the end of the nineties and dedicated to the patrons Felice and Fortunato: historical section with part of the relics transferred from Malamocco in 1110, iconographic section with works by Paolo Veneziano, Cima da Conegliano, Giovanni Bellini, Palma il Vecchio, Andrea Vicentino and Andrea Brustolon, silverware of the cathedral and objects of popular devotion.
The baroque villa was born and then remodeled in neoclassical style; in the park there are traces of the Baroque garden and a nymphaeum of Neptune.
The South of Scotellaro in the shots of the great photographers.
The fortification on a hill near Pomarance from which you could see the whole Val di Cecina to the sea.
The story of an illustrious son of Greci in a 19th-century palace.
High altitude pastures in the mountains of the valley.
From the 14th century, the bishops of Aosta retired until the mid-19th century; they remained a circular tower and sections of walls.
20th century art on the sea.
Frescoes of the fourteenth century and a medieval door under the bell tower.
The fifteenth century in the valley.

The public heart of the ancient city, surrounded by the Capitolium, the Basilica, temples, public spas, theatres and amphitheatre; on the walls of the city also political graffiti, linked to the elections scheduled for the days before the eruption.
The parish church of 1485, rebuilt in the eighteenth century.

Rare private collection of the 19th century by the brothers Giovanni senior and Giulio Jatta, remained in the original layout, acquired by the State in 1990-1991: over 2,000 finds in four rooms on the ground floor of Palazzo Jatta, including about 700 vases with red figures and a masked crater of the fourth century BC attributed to the painter of Baltimore. In Room 4, the famous Talos vase (420-400 B.C. about), with the death of the giant guardian of Crete among the Dioscuri. Closed on Monday.

Medieval village of upper Oltrepò Pavese, not far from the Passo del Penice, grown around the castle of Dal Verme, in whose tower the museum of peasant civilization is located; also worth seeing is the parish church of San Lorenzo, the oratory of Penicina and the botanical garden of Pietra Corva.

The park, which is located in the municipality, surrounds the village with more than 35 paths of various difficulties between woods, hermitages and gorges, suitable for hiking, mountain biking, horseback riding and climbing.
The regional portal indicates historical center, monuments and municipal museums accessible only in part
The ancient defenses of the city.

Excavated in the Temenite hill and facing the sea, expanded by Ierone II in the third century BC by a theatre of the V; of the 67 rows of the cavea remain 46; every May-June hosts the cycle of classical shows.

Didactic structure rebuilt with pieces of an ancient sawmill in the valley, on the stream Val Marcia: the water wheel and the mechanisms show how wood was cut with the force of water. Visitable only by reservation.
The treasure of Alcamesis churches suppressed.
The stone country.
In the Palazzo Carpegna near Fontana di Trevi, the academy born from the ancient University of the Arts of Painting, with the gallery of academic collections of paintings, sculptures and drawings.
The Gothic of the Swabian city.
The front of Costabella rebuilt in a stable.
A second Romanesque, a stone's throw from the town hall.
A tree that survived the tertiary age.
The fortress that dominates the village and the sea.

Sarcidano Country, in the center of Sardinia, Orange Flag of Touring: it has the Aymerich Park, the largest urban park on the island, the Museum of the prehistoric statuary in the palace of the Marquises Aymerich and is the birthplace of Sant'Ignazio, the most venerated saint of the island.
The romantic garden of the Ray.
The church of Antonelli and its windows.
The city of the popes on the Ernic Mountains, home to four pontiffs: the Romanesque Cathedral with the frescoed crypt in the thirteenth century, the Palazzo di Bonifacio VIII of the
The noble villa of the Fenaroli, linked to the Park of Bacchus.
The frescoes by Martin Figure.

Baroque church between the late seventeenth and early eighteenth centuries designed by Domenico Antonio Vaccaro, with the majolica floor by Leonardo Chianese designed by Francesco Solimena depicting the expulsion from Paradise.

The village is surrounded by centuries-old chestnut groves that give the chestnuts of Drena, symbol of local gastronomy; in the northern part of the village, among chestnuts and trekking trails, is located Drena 3000, park of outdoor sculptures.

The old part of the village remained almost intact along an ancient paved street in local stone, divided in two by the highway; in the lower part there is the church of San Pasquale. You arrive through the Plain of San Marco, and beyond the village the hills are covered by a forest of pine trees of Aleppo.
The library in the building.
The baroque palace of the bishops princes and their treasure of art.

Inaugurated in 1995 thanks to the inhabitants of the village, in the salon of the archpriest Salvatore Sberna: an ethnographic section with agricultural tools, tools of shoemaker and carpenters, pattese ceramics, and one of the sacred objects of the parish with a sixteenth-century pivial, vestments of the eighteenth century and wooden statues of the seventeenth-seventeenth century.
The DOP cheese of Barbagia, from pasture to table.
The bridge of the ancient city.

Fraction on a hill above the Black which preserves the fortified centre plant, born after the end of the XII century; inside the walls the church of San Sebastiano, from the western gate the view of the abbey and the bridge over the Black and the departure of the path "La Pia" , about 1.5 km to Sant'Anatolia passing through Santa Maria di Narco. It is the birthplace of the brothers Campani, opticians and watchmakers of the seventeenth century.

About 750 hectares once almost all corkscrew, cut down largely after the Second World War and reforested by the Forest Corps with conifers and eucalyptuses; today pines, cypresses, holm oaks and aromatic herbs, with rabbits, hares and istrices. It has parking lots, areas equipped with tables, cooking points and games for children and paths up to a hilly lake; from a hill of 642 meters you can see Segesta with theatre and temple, Monte Inici, Monte Sparagio and the Gulf of Castellammare.

Re-emerged in 1928 during works in a private residence and excavated in 1938: an auditorium of about 75 meters for at least 6,000 spectators; the nearby museum in Via degli Ammirati tells the ancient Lupiae.
A small 19th-century theatre.
The westernmost UNESCO flap near Bologna.

The hilly village was founded around the ninth century by the inhabitants of ancient Sanagasi, on the coast, fleeing from Saracen raids; it was long in the Barony of Badolato. The earthquake of 11 May 1947 destroyed most of it, but it remains narrow alleys, portals decorated in granite, a substantial stretch of the ancient city walls and several noble palaces. Every seven years there is represented the Tragedy of St. Martial, one of the few surviving hagiographic tragedies.

The church of the Blessed Virgin of Itria (XVII century), around which at the beginning of July the ardy of St. Constantine runs; the Baroque St. Pasquale Baylon, seat of the Jesuits; the late Dogotic oratory of St. Cross (XVI century).
The country residences of the Ascola aristocracy.
The Abbey of Celestine V.

On a granite rock about 140 meters above sea level, about 5 km south of the center: probably built in the 13th century under the Pisan Visconti, in the mid-300s passed to the Hospitallers of St. John of Jerusalem and then to the Aragonese, and was abandoned from the following century. A recent staircase rises to the top, where the quadrangular mast is about 10 meters high (two of the four original floors) and an underground cistern; halfway up the remains of a small watchtower.

In the monumental church of San Domenico, with the tomb of Jacopo del Cassero, the Fondazione Cassa di Risparmio di Fano exhibits sacred art from the 14th to the 18th century: the Marriage of the Virgin of Guercino (1649), works by Simone Cantarini, Warriors, Barocci, Palma il Giovane and Zuccari.

Natural park around the sacred springs to the cult of Jupiter Clitunno, which fed a large navigable river connected to Rome; an earthquake of the fifth century destroyed a part of it. In the second half of the nineteenth century Count Paolo Campello della Spina rearranged the place and created the pond of cold and clear waters, among green islets, weeping willows and cypress poplars, with swans and ducks. He inspired Pliny the Younger, Corot, Byron and Carducci. Open every day from 8.30 to 20.

Narrow core between the hill and the Scrivia stream, with the bridge of the Lastricus, alleys, squares and houses with bright colors of Liguria; there are the Collegiate of Saints Martin and Stefano and the oratories of the "White" and "Red" with works of art. From the center you can see the ruins of the castle on the hill of the Arimanni, not to be visited.
A forge as it was.
A church of the ancient village.

Inaugurated on April 16, 1989 by volunteers from the country, it collects posters, anecdotes, photographs and original props of the films, including the Guzzi sidecar, Peppone's bike, Don Camillo's dress and bicycles, with reconstructions of some places.
The life of the fields of the low Brescia.
For those who love ancient books.
In the old town you can see some valuable portals, the 16th century Monastery (today Ca' Moiana) and the Cà del Tay with its characteristic "lobbie" .
The Morellino story.
The symbol of the Catanzaresi.
A gallery of Verona painters in the parish.

In the center, on the ruins of the Castle of the Island, the palace of the feudatorio (now Battistoni) has an artistic portal of the sixteenth century; next stood the large convent of the Girolamini, demolished in the early Sixties. The church of the friars, today parish, restored and enlarged, contains three fine paintings including the Madonna del Carmine, already in the first Girolamine church.
Church built in 1152 next to the castle and bombed in 1944.
The parish parish of Carnia, overlooking the valley.
The rooms and the garden of the Visconti di Modrone.
An alpine lake for a stopover or a day of fishing.
About 18 kilometers of sandy coast with equipped bathrooms, health trails and playgrounds; the beach of Levante starts from the cliff of the Madonna dell'Angelo.

Founded in 1914, with the collections transferred to Bolzano in 1938 and returned in 1978 to the former convent of the Capuchins, reopened in 1992: it houses the Treasure of Loreto, donated around 1700 by Queen Maria Anna of Spain to her confessor Gabriel Pontifeser, with vestments, sacred furnishings and paintings of Spanish and Italian workshops of the sixteenth and seventeenth centuries, including the altar from field of King Charles II; sacred art from the fifteenth to the nineteenth century and works of the artistic colony of Chiusa (1874-1914). The visit includes the Baroque church of the Capuchins (1699-1701), with the main altarpiece of Paolo Pagani (1702).
Tiana's mother church.
Cast gold and watch in a noble villa of Varesotto.
The monthly antiques market.
An opera night in Como.

Built in the 13th century and enlarged in the 15th century, it has a late-Romanesque structure that opens to Gothic influences, especially in sculptures, and closes the panoramic square of hamlet Serre. In 1493 the Flemish painter Hans Clemer, active in the valleys of the Marchesato di Saluzzo, frescoed presbytery and apse with scenes of the life of Mary and the infancy of Christ and a great Crucifixion, which earned him the name of ...Master of Elva. Open all year round; if closed, the keys are at the Locanda San Pancrazio (tel. 335 5736255).

First Cistercian settlement of the Aquilan valley, founded in 1222 by Placido da Roio and Cistercian since 1248: square cloister with church, refectory, dormitory and capitular hall; in the church frescoes of about 1280, in the chapel-sacred stories of the Blessed Placido of the late fourteenth century. Managed by private individuals: accommodation on reservation, museum available by telephone appointment.

Along the Garibaldi course, it faithfully reproduces a cuisine of the ancient peasant civilization, linked to the tradition of transhumance still alive in the village. You can watch the processing of local dairy products, scamorza, caciocavallo, ricotta, braid and manteca, and then taste them; you can visit the museum together, by reservation.
The shrine of Manarola.
Frescoes and sixteenth-century tabernacle.

The Sabina municipality mentioned in 747 in the Regesto di Farfa: in the plain of Vescovio the church of Santa Maria, Sabina cathedral until 1733 with frescoes of the Cavallinian school, rises on the remains of the Roman town hall of Forum Novum; on the gorge of the Laia are facing the twin fortresses of Rocchette, still inhabited, and Rocchettine, abandoned village.
The shrine of former vows.
The halls of the ancient frescoed guilds.

Abbey dating back to the year 1000, originally belonged to the Camaldolese monks, then besieged and transformed. Inside the frescoes of the sixteenth century and the Coronation of the Virgin of Neri di Bicci (1472); near there is a secular oak tree, one of the "trees" of memory.
A stop on the Via Francigena.
A Gonzaghesque tower with views of the Garda hills.

At the entrance of Val Seriana, Alzano Lombardo houses the Baroque basilica of San Martino, designed by Gerolamo Quadrio, with the three sacristies inlaid by Fantoni and Caniana and the Museum of sacred art; on the hill the medieval village of Olera preserves the polyptych of Cima da Conegliano.
An interior full of stuccoes and marbles.
In the fifteenth century Palazzo Galvani: from prehistory to Etruscan and Roman Bologna, with an Egyptian collection of over 3,500 objects among the most important in Europe.
Work tools in the high valley of Grana.

Cathedral of Saints Cassiano and Maria Assunta, with origins in the 10th century and last Baroque reconstruction in the 18th century: eighteenth-century façade with two bell towers, neoclassical vestibule and baroque interiors that the prince bishop commissioned called the antechamber of paradise.

Born from a collection of the eighties of the association "Guido Ascanio Sforza" and opened by the Municipality in 1993 in four halls of Palazzo Sforza, exhibits about two thousand domestic objects and tools from the 16th to the 20th century. In June 2026 it was re-assembled on the top floor of the palace in the MUD - Urban Museum Diffuso, a journey on sharecropping and agrarian culture in five sections (history, land, hands, community, future) extended to the whole village.
On the first floor of the Doge's Palace, it collects objects from the agricultural world and reconstructions of typical environments of the place.

Built between 1898 and 1899 by the will of Commendatore Carlo Ricci, entrepreneur of modest origin with international interests, then returned home as mayor and promoter of public works. The project is by Cecilio Arpesani, in neo-medieval style with castle shapes, a scenic tower and the brick of the Padano Lombard language. Inside it contains three frescoes from the fifteenth century coming from Bergamasca, integrated in the decorations of the painter Ernesto Rusca, pupil of Brera; the villa is surrounded by a park.
The castle on the water at the mouth of the Astura.
On the trail of Padre Pio in Irpinia.

Monte Catria (1,701 m) overlooks the hermitage of Fonte Avellana, surrounded by holm oaks, oaks and hazelnuts; the monastery is the starting point for walks in the woods of Catria between beech and chestnut trees, on panoramic paths.

A few meters from the Villa dei Misteri, founded by Franco Gracco to show the influence of Pompeian painting on modern art: his collection since the seventies, the Sala Enea with a canvas of about 2 x 9 meters (1978-1980) on the journey of Enea,       Â The fresco found Â with reconstructions of lost Pompeian frescoes and temporary exhibitions.
Eight watermills still functioning.
From the ramp of Piazza del Ferrarese, via Venezia climbs along the walls towards the Fortino di Sant'Antonio Abate, the highest point of the old town, overlooking the sea.
The hill of the castle, between medieval history and panorama of Franciacorta.
Third Romanesque church of the territory, in the hamlet Mondonio next to the eighteenth-century farmsteads of Garesio.

The capital of Basilicata is more than 800 metres away, the city with its escalators: the historic centre along Via Pretoria, with the Guevara Tower and the Cathedral of San Gerardo, and the national and provincial archaeological museums; the bridge over the Basento of Sergio Musmeci.
The Catria massif is suitable for trekking, hiking, mountain biking and equestrian tourism; in October Cantiano hosts the Regional Exhibition of the Horse of Catria.
Hiking trail, trekking shoes
Caves inhabited by prehistoric times.
The industrial history of salt, inside and outside the museum.
Visits through the Park Qui Sportello, tel. 0921 674083 (Parco delle Madonie)
The amphitheatre and the mosaics of the Roman Larinum, with free entrance.
Coal mines.
The most beautiful walk at sunset.
Civic collection with works by Mattia Moreni and artists of the twentieth century.
The regional art museum that houses the Annunciation of Antonello da Messina in 1474.

Managed by the MIdA Foundation, in two sections. The geo-spele-archaeological one (MIdA 01) tells the karst and the underground environment with finds of the Caves of the Angel, reconstructions of caves in real scale and a multimedia path that starts with a virtual elevator. The agri-environmental one (MIdA 02, Museo del Sole) has live plants, historical and contemporary herbal plants with 800 exposed leaves, collections of soils, seeds, woods and bulbs and an open-air historical orchard.
A small frescoed theater.
The fortress on the cliff, rebuilt for the Montefeltro, prison and place of death of the Count of Cagliostro.
The Riviera delle Alpi is a mild climate spa town with palm trees, olive trees and domestic pines, known for its spas and casinos.
Baroque and Baron in the same church.
The marble arch of entrance to the city.

The Bell Towers, the Clock and the Prisons are what remains of the castle wanted by Ermanno, Marquis of Verona, and the fortified system of the center; they are dated between 1152 and 1297 and attributed to the Scaligeri.
18th century frescoes of Chiarottini and Canal.
Remains of the thermal baths and walls of the Roman city of Iulia Concordia, recorded by the Ministry of Culture.
In the heart of the Friulian Risorgive area: Villa Manin, residence of the last doge of Venice where Napoleon signed the Treaty of Campoformido, the Park of the Risorgive and the ancient mills.
The Savoy Park.
Olive groves and views from Monte Grosso.
The hemp and hand weaving of Valnerina.

It tells the history of the city, a hub between the Plain of Catania and the interior, from the Neolithic and the Bronze Age to the growth from indigenous center to the Greek city and Roman civitas: Hellenistic houses with architectural terracotta and paintings, the famous centuripin vases with relief and polychrome, marble sculptures and epigraphs of the imperial age. Open entirely in June 2024 after ten years; there is exhibited, on loan from the Museo Paolo Orsi until 2026, a head of Augustus considered his best portrait found in Sicily.

12th century monastery, before the Antonians and since the 14th century Augustinian; abandoned in the Napoleonic age, it was restored by Leo XIII on a project by A. Bonanni and A. Camaiti. Two Cistercian protire with stylophorous lions, frescoes in T's basin. Troja (1888), wooden choir and a Gothic organ donated to Leo XIII by the diocese of San Gallo; in the convent the Ritiana art gallery.
The history of the Pesaro sea.

Chiappera (1,614 m) is the last inhabited village of the Upper Maira Valley, dominated by the profile of the Provençal-Castle spur of quartzite, a climbing destination; besides, the road becomes dirt road towards the Stroppia waterfalls and the French border can be reached only on foot from the Maurin Hill. It is the base for GTA, Chamberyron Tour and Occitani Routes; between Colle Greguri and Monte Maniglia you can see ibex.
The hill between the two rocks.
The suspended village of peperino overhanging the ditches, with proffers, medieval houses and the only Moai outside Easter Island.

Romanesque parish church of the XI-XII centuries in the upper part of Pievebovigliana (a plaque probably bears date 1162), of which remain the eastern apse with monofore and the stone wall; facade, bell tower and interior were renovated from the eighteenth century. The coeva crypt, rediscovered in the twentieth century, has five naves on four rows of columns and three apses, altar columns in piperin, a Roman plaque of the second century A.D. and a fresco of Saint Lucia attributed to Archangel of Cola (1420-25 about): it is among the most famous Romanesque monuments of the Marches.
The island in the center of the Cagnan Grande created by the Austrian government in 1856 to host the fish market, above the waters of the Botteniga.
Free (Guided tours on the calendar)
A seventy-year rebirth.
