A monastery clinging to the rock overlooking Lake Maggiore.
The baroque villa of the Chigi in the countryside.

Medieval village on the hill behind Diano Marina, among the most beautiful villages in Italy, among terraced hills in Vermentino: caruggi, the Baroque parish of San Nicola, the Romanesque Santa Maria Assunta and the underground cisterns.
The eye on the sea.
The crypt of martyrs under the Collegiate.
Get lost in the white maze of the Itria Valley.
Borgo Bandiera Arancione between Langhe and plain, heir of the Roman Augusta Bagiennorum, whose remains are protected by a special nature reserve.

The only example of Swabian architecture in central-north Italy, wanted by Frederick II and built between 1237 and 1248 by Riccardo da Lentini, with portal to white and green bands and Swabian lions; in summer outdoor cinema.

Summer residence purchased by Napoleon in June 1814 with rooms decorated by Pietro Ravelli as the Egyptian Hall and the Sala delle Colombe; Prince Anatolio Demidoff built the Neoclassical Gallery there, today with Napoleonic prints.

Fraction just over seven kilometers from the village, born in the late nineteenth century: in 1906 the Royal Army opened a horse breeding centre for police and carabinieri, passed after the fifties to the Institute of horse ride of Ozieri, which raises Anglo-Arabic-Sardi horses, Sardinian pony and white donkeys of Asinara. Between woods and old buildings of the military village start paths born for the knights; a tree-lined avenue leads to the Neo-Medieval church of San Salvatore, with bichrome facade, portal and gothic rosette.
The Sienese polyptych by John of Paul.
The ancient Jewish quarter, with frescoed ceilings and lunettes decorated above the windows.
The colors of the Ponze houses.
The ruined tower.
The parish church on Piazza Campello and the bell tower called Torre Ligariana, whose first stone was laid on March 29, 1740.

Pastoral complex made of dry stone: the main building is the largest and only two-storey building between the about 500 of the area, with smaller huts, a small inhabited nucleus and remains of the enclosures for animals; near the Fonte Cugnoli with picnic area.
The church of the patron saint and the urn of Manfredi.

Built in 1550 by the will of the Doge of Genoa to defend the coast from pirate raids, on a project attributed to Antonio de Càrabo, already author of the castle Rapallo: rectangular plan with rounded corners, tower in the south-west corner and main hall with a large central pillar and vaults. Stairs and trails connect it to Villa Durazzo. Restored in 2000, it hosts art exhibitions and multimedia halls of the Museo del Mare, with videos, speaking squares and interactive totems on the backdrop and the maritime history of the city.
Dedicated to the patron saint of Santa Margherita d'Antiochia, whose cult was introduced by the Olibria family; it is today the main church of the village.
The long sea front of the city with beaches and walk.

Above the village, at the foot of Mount Salimmo and in the Adamello Park: Lake Valbione is about 45 minutes walk from the cable car Ponte-Tonale, and at 1,530 meters there is the golf course surrounded by the woods.
Times not available on the MiC website
Oasis near the Po, destination of bike rides and observation of protected water birds.
By bike on the track of the old railway.
The church of the pilgrims of Francigena.
Under the stars in downtown.
Waterfall and ancient bridges along the Savato.

Public garden in the center, next to the Town Hall and near the Mother Church, designed in 1974 by the architect Sebastiano Maltese and completed in 1984; among pines, cedars, cypresses, willows and oleanders are placed sculptures, many of the local artist Salvatore Galante. It is told the tree of witches, the cypresses in love and the avenue of lovers.
discordant times: the MiC card (July 2020) reports "closed" every day, the Metro City Tuesday and Thursday 15-17 or by appointment
Medieval tower houses and a Matilda church.

Inaugurated in 2003: the theatre was built after the middle of the first century A.D. terracing the hill, the amphitheatre a few decades later on an embankment. The outer walls of the amphitheatre are entirely discovered, the theatre is visible about a third; in the upper part runs a long aqueduct that supplied both. Illustrative panels along the route; management Pro Loco Cividatese, closed on Monday.

Civic museum opened in 2010 in Villa Sottocasa, tells the history, art, economy and society of the Brianza est, between Lambro and Adda, in 14 rooms on two floors (about 1000 square meters): on the ground floor a chronological path from the first Roman settlements to the nineteenth century, on the first floor industry, transformation of the territory and local memory. It exhibits archaeological finds, paintings, 3D models, multimedia installations, photographs and historical movies; in 2012 it received the ICOM Museum of the Year Award for the best Italian setup. Opening hours: Wednesdays and Thursdays 10-13; Fridays, Saturdays and Sundays 10-13 and 15-19.
Five centuries of peasant and mining life, farm after farm.
A day on foot towards the Bird Pizzo.
A stop in the green.
A panoramic ridge above the Stura to the sanctuary.
Hiking and panoramic views of Val Gandino within reach of cars.
The valley of the springs under the Matese.
A 17th-century fraternity church.

Born in 1997 on the initiative of the teachers of the Don Milani school, it collects objects from the history of the school; since 2013 it is in the basement of the new Municipal Theatre. Openings and visits only by reservation.
The first cathedral.
Forre, medieval bridges and otters along the heat.
The neoclassical villa reflected in the Naviglio.
Not far from the village, the former salt pans host rare bird species such as flamingos and hawks.

Founded in 1973 by Don Sergio Campana in two rooms on the left aisle of the Collegiata: processional crosses from the fourteenth to the seventeenth century, a fourteenth-century turbole, a peace in ivory and ebony with the Pietà (XV century), two golden wooden statues of Saints Peter and Paul of the school of Antonio Bencivenni, silver and vestments.
With an octagonal plan, it completes the Piazza del Comune next to the Cathedral.

Founded in the 11th century by the Crucifers as a hospital for pilgrims, on the remains of a early Christian basilica in the Roman city.

Ancient capital of the Marchesato at the foot of the Monviso, with the medieval village of cobbled streets dominated by Castile and the masterpieces of the Saluzzo Renaissance.
The "city of great fashion" of the eighteenth-century carnival.
In Masentine the erosion of the Mongia stream has dug over millennia a natural bridge, used for centuries as a passage between the two banks of the valley.
The artistic twentieth century of Versilia in a historic villa.
Dune and sea lily on the gulf.

Small village of the pedemontana pordenona, land of the red onion, dominated by the sixteenth-century Palazzo Polcenigo-Fanna, the "Palazat" today town hall and headquarters of the section Work and emigration of the Museum of peasant life
The stars and the first sauropode of Italy in the same afternoon.
The Benedictine church on the square.

Borgo once inhabited almost only by fishermen, with alleys connected by arches and stairs and flowered houses of geraniums; it is the most convenient landing point (traghetti every 15 minutes from Sulzano), with restaurants and shops on the lakefront.

In the rooms of the sixteenth-century apartment of the Counts Gonzaga, on the noble floor of the Rocca: the frescoes of Lelio Orsi detached from the Casino of Sopra, his Annunciation on board, the tapestry of Alfonso I Gonzaga with Jason and Medea (1554), Romanesque-Bizantine frescoes from San Giovanni della Fossa and one of the most important European collections of pharmacy vases, from the Jesuits' spices. Tuesday-Friday 10-13 (call on arrival), Saturday and Sunday 10-13 and 15-19; free on the first Sunday of the month.

Borgo della Valle di San Lorenzo, between woods and olive groves, born around the Romanesque church of San Gregorio and belonged for centuries to Porto Maurizio, which bought it in 1162; it is home to the stroscia, ancient oil cake, and includes the hamlets of Boscomare, with the open-air museum of murals, and Torre Paponi.

Rebuilt in the current forms on the banks of the river Musestre in 1492, with the bell tower of 1493; in 1903 it was renovated, raised almost three meters and equipped with a new facade and a frescoed ceiling.
The capital of the Canavese on the Dora Baltea: the ancient city with the Duomo and the castle of the red towers and the industrial city of the Olivetti, UNESCO heritage since 2018.
A masterpiece of the fourteenth century in Siena.

Between the Archbishop's Palace and the Cathedral: the Stauroteca, a 12th century gold reliquary cross linked by the tradition to Frederick II and the consecration of the Cathedral in 1222, a polyptych of the Annunciation of 1545, ancient glasses and paintings by Luca Giordano and Andrea Vaccaro.

Protected area since 1998 on Mount Lignano, guarded for centuries by the walls of a Franciscan monastery: oak, green peaks, foxes and at the entrance the large holm oak of 200 years linked to the brigand Gnicche.
Walk among the places of Don Guanella at altitude.
The Madonna of the shepherds and of the tratturi.
The picnic on the lake.
The ancient village preserves noble palaces, ancient oil mills and historical collections; there is also the Town Hall.

Linear path of 3.5 km (about 1 hour and 30 one way, +250 m, from 175 to 400 m) on asphalt, dirt road and path, suitable for children from 6 years old but not for strollers; passes through the 17th century church of San Rocco and a panoramic panel, with short detour to the top. Recommended period from spring to autumn.
The Liberty of Basile in the center.
The largest fountain in the city, near the castle, with two stone lions at the ends.

A 17th-century shrine leaning against the rock on a ridge, surrounded by greenery and overlooking the river Lao; it is a destination for pilgrimages for a fresco considered miraculous in the 17th century.

A beech forest of humanity just a stone's throw from the country.
Walk inside the walls of the Columns.
The triangular fortress overlooking the Val di Magra.
Next to the basilica of San Vicino, vestments, liturgical objects and paintings of the parishes of the ancient diocese of Sarsina.
On the hill behind the palace, the remains of the castle probably built in the 11th century and abandoned during the 17th century; on clear days good views over the plain.

Built in the second half of the fifteenth century and rebuilt in 1743, it preserves a wooden statue of the late fifteenth century and an eighteenth-century painting on the ceiling; the feast is celebrated every January 19th.

Cittadina at the foot of the Ligurian Apennines, at the confluence of Borbera in Scrivia, long under the Republic of Genoa: the archaeological area of the Roman city of Libarna on the Via Postojna, the hall of the artifacts in the town hall and a historical center with a Ligurian imprint.
Marghine Center on the basalt plateau: the Nuraghe Santa Barbara symbol of the city, the complex of Tamuri with the betiles, the domus de janas of Filigosa and the museum of the ancient arts.
A church born from a synagogue.
The medieval square.
The fourteenth-century loggia.

The name "del Cingaro" dates back to the last decades of the sixteenth century; with a single nave, with two lateral altars that give it a Latin cross. The ancon of the high altar is attributed to G. Bertesi and it is preserved    Â The miracle of the host of the Genoese. Without architectural barriers.

The valley of the language and the Resian culture, largely inside the Julian Pre-Alps Natural Park and dominated by Mount Canin: the Museum of Arrotino in Stolvizza, the sanctuary of Santa Maria Assunta in Prato and the widespread ecomuseum.

Church with a basilica plan with three naves, about 27-28 meters long, with six columns per side, which the Superintendence (Moretti) dates to the IX century and the Municipality classifies as a Longobard construction between VIII and IX century; it was the seat of a Benedictine preposition. The earthquakes of the Tre-Quattrocento brought down the three apses, around 1450 the orientation was reversed and in the eighteenth century came the Baroque covering and the bell tower. The façade has a walled loggia with a pre-Romanesque print and a portal with a carved Greek cross, with Roman materials of re-use; on the medieval apses of a cat with two heads and a lion, and on the walls fragments of fifteenth century frescoes.

Medieval village of Cilento, 'balcone sul mare', born around the castle of which the Abbot Costabile Gentilcore laid the first stone on October 10 1123: alleys, arches and staircases in grey stone, the basilica of Santa Maria de Giulia and the Museum of sacred art; on the coast the hamlet of Santa Maria with the Port of the Cats and Villa Matarazzo, and the Marine Area protected up to Punta Licosa, linked to the myth of the mermaid Leucosia.
A Swabian castle overlooking the Pollino.
The Parmesan walk.
Black sand and caves to explore in canoe.

Two large halls and six sections on the traditional life of Gallura: house (bread and cheese tools, a carved cone of the wedding races), vine and wine with palms and presses, agriculture, breeding, carriages with oxen and crafts of blacksmith, carpenter and shoemaker. Open from the end of March to the beginning of November; in the rest of the year by reservation.

Established in 1982 on 200 hectares of the first hills, it protects the group of sauces, cold mud volcanoes, larger and more singular in the region. Free access, always open subject to exceptional conditions; trails can also be reached by wheelchair. A cycle path connects it to the castle of Spezzano.
The two Flaminies seen from above.

The navigable canal built between 1754 and 1766 on an area of salt pans, the heart of the neighborhood born when Trieste became a free port; partially buried in 1934, with piazza del Ponterosso and piazza Sant'Antonio.

A common hill between the southern slopes of Pratomagno and the right bank of the Arno, at the gates of Casentino, established in 1808. The most important monument is the Pieve di Santa Maria a Sietina with its frescoes of the fourteenth and fifteenth centuries; around, medieval parishes such as San Giovanni and San Martino Sopr'Arno and villages such as Bibbiano, Santa Margherita and Castelluccio.
The industrial villa Necchi Campiglio, today of the FAI, which tells the high-bourgeois Milan of the first half of the twentieth century, part of the Case Museo circuit.
The porticoed street of the markets and palaces and the square of the locals, evening meeting of students together with Piazza della Pera.

Born in 2004 in the building of 1822 that housed a wash-house porch on the ground floor and the elementary school on the first floor, it tells for themes the use of water in rural communities: tools for washing clothes, drawing, transport and domestic and agricultural use, with customs and popular beliefs; among the pieces a fire machine of the second half of the nineteenth century perfectly working. In 2018 the collections passed to the civic center Fabio Casartelli; the wash-house remains open as a permanent exhibition and hosts the municipal hostel. It offers routes to discover fountains, wells, glaciers and ancient aqueducts of the territory.
Triangular fortress built by the Genoese in eleven months and inaugurated on March 12, 1756 to curb the drive of independence of the city; next to the Old Port.
On the trail of Modigliani.
The Cistercian abbey of the plain.
The history of ancient Capua.
Birdwatching in a swamp among the rice fields.

The convent dates back to 1531; the chapel of Saint Catherine of Alexandria, dating back to 1532, is frescoed with scenes of the life and martyrdom of the saint, and the crypt excavated in the rock rests on 36 slender columns in four rows, with traces of frescoes.
The 56 views of a small state.
The walnut choir of the French friars.

A village above Merano that named Tyrol: Tyrol Castle, home of Tirol's counts and today the Province's historical and cultural museum, Castel Fontana (Brunnenburg) with the South Tyrolean Agricultural Museum, the bird care centre for birds of prey on the castle's motto, the ground pyramids of the Mutbach gorge and the church of St. Peter with Romanesque frescoes.
The only salt pans in Lazio, today a nature reserve.

A compulsory passage through the caravans between Rome and Naples: here on 11 October 1254 Pope Innocent IV, who arrived from Anagni, met Manfredi of Swabia, who had to cross the bridge holding the bridles of the mule of the pontiff; Dante remembers the episode in Purgatory. According to the Manfredi tradition, killed at Benevento, he was buried under a bridge pylon. In mid-October, the Palio delle Corti evokes the encounter with flag-wavers, falconers, archery and fire arrows launched on the river.

Municipality of Monte Pisano with the Certosa.

At the center of the September festival.

Feudal castle of late-medieval foundation, belonged to the Counts Da Gombola until the beginning of the fifteenth century: the small village, the thirteenth-century tower and the remains of the crenellated walls rise on a mass of serpentine, rock of underwater volcanic origin. Nearby there is the "Grotta Taxoni" (Taxoni Grotto).

The main stage is the Sciara del Fuoco, a slope of debris that descends from the crater to the sea, formed by lava, lapilli and glowing dross, from which the eruptions are observed.
On the hills south of the village, attested in 1309 and linked to the judges of Arborea Mariano IV and Eleonora: the walls and the remains of the medieval village remain.

A walled village with views of the Amiata.

Rebuilt in the seventeenth century, it contains frescoes by Allegratto Nuzi from 1360.
The areas of the territory of Murlo linked to the Etruscan civilization, celebrated every year by the Bluetruscan Festival.
Archaeological exhibition in the capital with finds from prehistory to the Middle Ages.
The landscape around the village is made of vineyards, Lake Arancio and Monte Genuardo, where the nature reserve offers hiking trails.

The ancient Piazza Vecchia, considered one of the best preserved examples of medieval square in Italy: houses-towers of the Three and fifteenth century, porticos, the Civic Tower, the sixteenth-century triumphal arch, the ancient Civic Palace and the monument to the patriot Santorre of Santa Rosa. In a wrought iron newsstand there is the Tourist Office.
In the locality of Villa di Montalto, it preserves the fresco of the "Mater Misericordiae" with knights of 1468, attributed to Giovanni Angelo d'Antonio da Bolognola.

Municipality between the valley of the river Simeri and the Gulf of Squillace: on the hill of Simeri, the oldest village of medieval origin, the Byzantine castle and the Collegiate of Santa Maria d'Itria; on the coast the beach of Simeri Mare, known as "Costa dei Gigli" .
A painted octagon.

Between Busso and Baranello, one of the richest centers of the Sanniti Pentri: a stone belt of about 3 km contains about 50 hectares and the peaks of 968 and 997 m, with three doors visible to oblique corridor (two excavated). The excavations have found homes, including the LN house at the south gate, and a circular cistern about 6 m deep.
The Muto frescoes in a baroque hamlet church.

Founded in 1970 by Father Augusto Mozzetti in the oratories of the ancient confraternities on the sides of the main altar of the parish, with a section in the oratory of Santa Croce. He collected works from the 14th to the 20th century: a fresco of the Madonna with Child, a wooden sculpture of the 15th century, the  "Madonna delle rose" attributed to Bernardo Zenale, a painted iron dragon used in the Rogations and a large collection of ex-vote tablets.

Villa built in 1885 by writer and politician Anton Giulio Barrili, volunteer of Garibaldi, who dedicated it to his mother. On the first floor, already family apartment, four rooms with personal objects and collections of the writer: rare books, five hundred, prints, pamphlets, scores and manuscripts of his lectures at the University of Genoa; the lounges on the front house art exhibitions and the ground floor, since 1981, the civic library. Accessible even in a wheelchair.

From the hill you can see the city, the Metauro Valley and on clear days the Adriatic. The sixteenth-century church of St. John the Baptist, today the sanctuary of Blessed Benedict Passionei next to the Capuchin monastery, has wooden altar, walnut choir and an eighteenth-century canvas by Gaetano Bessi; in front, a large iron cross illuminated every night.

Romanesque church of 1330 in the village of Marano, with frescoes from the XIV-XVI centuries attributed to the school of Gentile da Fabriano.
The plain was born from the largest lake in Tuscany.
The castle of the hamlet on the mountain.

Set up in the approximately 500 square meters of the Borbonico Salone del Real Convitto di Santa Maria delle Grazie, next to the Vanvitellian style church on the ancient Via Appia, it tells the rural life from the early twentieth century to the mid-century in four areas: the fields, with a large mangano and the macennole for hemp; the road, with the tools of the carpenters, blacksmith and cantiere shops; the courtyard, with the well, the vinnolo and the catalog; the house, with kitchen and bedroom reconstructed. In the hall there is also a permanent municipal nativity scene of 2003; since 2009 it is a museum of regional interest and is free of architectural barriers.

Cities along the Via Emilia, the ancient Julia Dertona: the sixteenth-century Cathedral, Palazzo Guidobono with the Archaeological Museum, the Pinacoteca "Il Divisionismo" in the Medieval Palace, the Colle Savo with the castle tower and the Basilica of the Madonna della Guardia with the large golden statue.
A fifteenth-century nativity in crypt.

Cala Rossa takes its name from the reddish stripes of the cliff; in front of the islet it becomes snorkeling. Near the Tower Alba, with a very suggestive view, often hosts exhibitions and exhibitions.

In the palace built between 1521 and 1545, with the graffiti façade of Cristofano Gherardi on a design attributed to Vasari, twenty-one rooms of works from the fourteenth to the nineteenth century: among these the Gonfalone della Santissima Trinità, a youthful work by Raffaello, and the Martyrdom of San Sebastiano by Luca Signorelli.
The Cathedral of Francesco Gallo.

The monographic museum of the sculptor Bergamasco (1908-1991), author of the Gate of Death of St. Peter, who settled in Ardea in the early 1960s: in 1969 the Amici di Manzù collection was born, donated by the artist to the State in 1979 and opened to the public in 1981. About five hundred pieces among a hundred sculptures, graphics, jewelry, medals and theatrical sketches, with Cardinals, sketches for the Death Gate, Lovers, David of 1939 and Adam and Eve of 1929; in the garden sculptures such as \"Nastro" and the tomb of the artist. Tuesday-Sunday 9-19.30, Monday closed.

Wet area along the Tronto, near Pagliare, with two ponds fed by the layer, riparian vegetation, poplars and centuries-old oaks; it nests the heron ash, symbol of the oasis, along with folagues, hens and germans. A path accessible with panels crosses the ponds on a wooden walkway; there is a wildlife recovery center, an eco park in recycled materials, fences with courtyard animals and Marche cattle and free bikes for bikes.
The fourteenth-century baptismal font.
The medieval village on the hills.
The new square overlooking the river in front of the Tiberius Bridge, with a walk with water, the floating bridge and the park that tells the story of the bridge.
Typical village of Lower Lodigiana crossed by bike paths in the open countryside, it houses the Museum of Toy and Child, which traces the evolution of the toy in the last three centuries.

The picture gallery of the convents suppressed.
The village seen from the stream.
A karst amphitheatre a hundred meters deep.
The ancient Savoia hunting reserve around the building, today a natural park of fields and woods with visitor center, picnic area and recommended itineraries.
The Cagnacci in Rimini.

The Donut degli Sposi, a sweet handmade ring and Traditional Agro-food Product of Lazio, has its festival usually in September; the "rocchicianella," a small sweet chestnut, is celebrated on the third Sunday of October. On the table polenta with sausage, cheese or mushrooms, borlotti soup, cod in stew and lamb shell with broad beans.
The civic halls behind the cathedral with the cycle of medieval frescoes inspired by the stories of King Arthur and the knights of the Round Table, works by Giovanni Migliara and Alberto Caffassi.
Always accessible
A unique museum in Italy, made of memories of the common people.

The axis of the historic center, via Roma and via Camuzzoni, brings together the Duomo, the Palazzo di Giustizia, Palazzo Cavalli and Palazzo Scaligero or the Captain, now the seat of the Town Hall; the squares of Foro Boario, the Horses and the Grani Market recall in the names the medieval commerces. Here in May is held the medieval festival of white wine and in September the Grape Festival.

The horseshoe ravine, about 3 km of green that was the natural defense of the country during the invasions, hosts on the right side of the descent the village of Rivolta: 66 caves on five levels, considered one of the most important rock villages in Italy, with cisterns, ovens, fireplaces, gardens and palms for oil and wine, of a very high ingenuity. The first settlement was dug into the tuff and the parietal decorations are still visible. The ravine is set to "The Gospel according to Matthew of Pasolini (1964) and to "Who has seen me" (1964). Better go in spring or early autumn, morning or evening.
In San Rocco, just outside the city on the street of Ofantina: thermal baths of the I-III century A.D., a domus with mosaic and the first early Christian basilica with hexagonal baptismal font.

Built around the year 1000 to guard a road used by the Romans to reach the Adriatic, it was fortress of the Duchy of Montefeltro between the fifteenth and sixteenth centuries, with a particular arched plant attributed to Francesco di Giorgio Martini; then residence of the family of the Porta, from which the name. Today it is open to visitors, it hosts events and exhibitions and the municipal collection of art with works from the churches of the territory and the castle, partly sorted by chronology and partly by iconography. Reduced for children and groups over 15 people.
The Baptistery with the gates of Ghiberti, Giotto's Bell Tower and the museum with the originals of the square, including the Paradise Gate and Michelangelo's Pietà Bandini.

In the new part of the village, it rises where an older church was destroyed in 1144 during the war between Acquapendente and Orvieto; the new, octagonal plan with colored windows, was begun in 1987 and inaugurated in 1993, with terracotta by the sculptor Mario Vinci of Acquapendente.
Music and violin, local tradition.
Small panoramic villages.
The cathedral at the end of Via Vittorio Emanuele, the road that starts from Piazza Umberto I.
A century of confetti.

The fortress was built between the 8th and 9th centuries by the survivors of Sinuessa and abandoned between the 15th and 16th centuries; since 2001 the municipality finances an excavation campaign. It rises about 500 meters on Mount Petrino with wide view; the front is too steep, you climb from the road on the back and then walk on a path. During the feast of St. Michael, in early October, the castle was illuminated.
Lombard church of late VI-early VII century in the area of Gardola, with a fine window and a small museum of high medieval tombs; every summer hosts an exhibition of local artists.
The Challant Tower.
The villas of cotton manufacturers.
Brother Innocent's miraculous crucifix.
Caveoso rock church, used by Benedictine nuns until 1283, with frescoes.
Walk on the lake among the monuments of the open-air museum.
The sixteenth-century ramp flanked by stone walls that go up to the castle: it is formed by 15 raised slabs of stone laid cut and by stretches in pebbles of 30-40 cm.
In the municipal territory, a thermal spring already known in Etruscan-Roman times with the name of Caldane.

Alm complex at 1,686 meters on the plateau of Erèra-Brendòl, documented from 1466 and abandoned in the fifties: the 27 meters long casera and the pendant, 91 meters canopy with 25 stone arches for the cattle, collapsed in part in the thirties and after the earthquake of Friuli 1976 and restored by the Park. Go up from Lake Stua to the CAI 802 mule track.
Mountain life a century ago.
The castle where the drama of Beatrice di Tenda was consumed.
An open-air sculpture museum.
The world of Fellini in his city.
The procession at the lake.
Contemporary art in the old city.
The village crossed by the Gothic Line, destroyed in the Second World War, preserves the remains of the walls of the ancient Malatesta bulwark between Conca and Ventena.
The rose up close.
The largest building for antiquity shows, about 600 by 140 meters, with the Torre della Moletta and the Circus Maximo Experience in augmented reality.
The mountain symbol of the Central Marches.
The statues of the Easter rites.
The fountain of legend, symbol of the country.
The Roman port on the promenade.
High altitude lakes and beech trees a few kilometers from the village.
Fedra's sarcophagus.
Reforestation that recreates the oak-carpinet of the Po Valley, along the Canal of the Mills.

The city of knives, seat of the knife-making district: Piazza Italia with the late Dome of San Mauro and Palazzo d'Attimis Maniago with the lion march attributed to Pomponio Amalteo, the ruins of the castle on the hill and the museum of art craftsmanship in a former knife factory.

The municipality of the hills of Pescia, in whose territory stands Villa Badessa, a community of Arbëreshë arrived from Epirus in 1743: its church of Santa Maria Assunta, unique of Greek-Byzantine rite in Abruzzo, preserves a rich collection of icons, and a museum tells its origins and traditions.
The symbol of the village, survived the flood of 1994.
In the hometown of Gianni Rodari.
The medieval village at the entrance of the Grana Valley.

In an elegant 19th-century building already a granite mountain: on the ground floor the finds of the village of Genna Maria (pots, stone and metal instruments) exposed according to the environments of origin, on the upper floor materials of the Marmilla from Neolithic to the Byzantine age; the path arrives at the cult of Demeter and Core. Open Tuesday-Sunday 9:30-13 and 15:30-18 (April-September until 19:00).

On the Garigliano, on the border between Lazio and Campania, it was commissioned by Francesco I and completed by Ferdinando II of Bourbon on a project by the engineer Luigi Jura: completed in 1832, it is the first iron chain bridge suspended in Italy and among the first in Europe. Theatre of a clash on October 29, 1860, was blown up by the German spoilers on October 14, 1943; today it is entirely restored.
A small museum with memories of the founder, St. Benedict Cambiagio Frassinello (1791-1858), and the early years of the congregation. Tel. 010 935914.

Built between 1778 and 1787, it is considered one of the wonders of the Lecce baroque: the large rococo façade, scenographic, is lengthened by two lateral arches. Inside, with a single nave with vault decorated with rococo stuccos, canvases on the life of the Virgin and the Immaculate altar; it is home to the brotherhood of the same name, active since the seventeenth century.
Menaggio's canyon.
Along the Fiora, a waterfall creates the small swimming pond of Pellicone, in the oasis desired by the WWF.
The ancient entrance to the island.
It combines on foot the two natural destinations of the municipality.

Historical capital of eastern Lunigiana: the Medici square with its fountain inside the walls, the memory of the press of Jacopo da Fivizzano, the castle of the Verrucola dei Malaspina and, in Equi Terme, the caves in the Park of the Apuan Alps.
The Franciscan church of the fifteenth century.
A Romanesque bell tower among the first Marian churches in Canavese.
It is about 40 metres high and is one of the highest lighthouses in Europe.
Built around the year 1000 and rebuilt by Angioini and Aragonese.

To the north of the settlement, cyclopean walls that legend attributed to the paladins of Charlemagne: the preserved stretch is about 180 meters long and 5 meters high, in blocks of local limestone just rough, with three small doors (about 80 cm for 2.3 meters) lined up with paths still in use. The polygonal belt, about 4 km long between built sections and rock walls, should not be older than the 5th century BC.

Permanent exhibition on the products and history of the biomedical district of Mirandole, considered the most important in Europe: opened in May 2010 in the Castle of the Pico, after the earthquake was reopened on 27 May 2013 in Via Focherini.
The medieval memories of the capital of the valleys.
Forest of the Leonessan territory that includes the Valli dell'Organo.

Museo d'arte contemporanea a venta tra piazzas e vie del paese, started in 1991 by the Piscinese painter Antonio Panino to represent the currents of Piedmontese art at the end of the millennium: about seventy works by artists of different generations and schools, along a city itinerary.
An easy ring in the chestnut groves of the Park.
The Trident in one room.
A hilly village in the shape of a grape cluster, among woods, vineyards and geothermal phenomena of the Val di Cecina.

Founded by Saint Benedict of Norcia in 529 on the site of an ancient tower and temple of Apollo, destroyed by the bombings of 15 February 1944 and rebuilt; the museum exhibits codes, choral books, vestments, works and paintings of the eighteenth century Neapolitan.

The city of Carnival and the Art Nouveau promenade on the sea of Versilia, between the pine forests of Ponente and Levante; in Torre del Lago the villa of Giacomo Puccini on the lake of Massaciuccoli.
the MiC card (updated to 2020) indicates closed every day; check openings with the Municipality (089 828210, cultura@comune.baronissi.sa.it)
The gold mine.
The 16th century frescoes and the view from the hill.
The fifteenth-century chapel.

7.4 km hike (about 2 hours and 50, 507 m of altitude difference) from the parking lot Jochalm-Kaseregg, for trails no. 15 and 1 between woods and meadows, to the refuge at one of the highest pilgrimage churches in Europe, at 2,341 meters; in summer there is a bus excursionists from Lazfons by reservation.

Managed by the mineralogical group of the Lanzo Valleys, it exhibits about 150 minerals of the valleys in six windows: one petrological and others dedicated to the mine of Balangero, the Valley of Ala, the Valley of Viù and the minerals of Canavese and Valle d'Aosta, with photos of the Amientifera of Balangero and a geological map of the Western Alps. Times to be agreed with the association.

White pebble beach and clear water between the Marinella and the Natural Arch, sheltered by the Molpa cliffs, frequented by climbers. A path climbs to the hill with the ruins of a castle, from which you can see the Buondormire, the Marinella and the Scoglio del Rabbit.

Former cultural center Giovanni Santi, born in 1994 for the sixteenth century anniversary of the death of the painter and became in 2019 a path of reading the landscape, with a permanent exhibition on Giovanni Santi, painter, writer and stage designer of the court of Urbino: reproductions of works such as the Visitation of Fano and St. Jerome of the Vatican Art Gallery and the poem in 23,000 verses about the life of Federico da Montefeltro.

A country at the gates of Cosenza, whose first stable settlement was formed according to tradition by refugees from Cosentino fleeing around the year 1000; around Piazza San Giorgio there are the church of San Giorgio Martire, built around 1480 by Blessed Francesco Marino, and the Museum of sacred art with a triptych of Bartolomeo Vivarini.

The lake, close to the village and to the ancient olive trees, is surrounded by granite; along its banks passes the line of the Green Train, which stops in Luras, and from Sant'Antonio di Gallura you can reach the olive grove also with a shovel boat.
An alley of 43 centimeters.
Country of orchards at the outlet of the valley of the same name, known since ancient times for the mines of manganese and copper.
The erosive forms surrounding the country are produced by water on clay rocks; about two million years ago there were seabeds here, today rich in fossils.
The 12th century walls and the most recent tower, restored in 1310 and abandoned in the 18th century; today it houses concerts and events.

Borgo della Franciacorta at the foot of Monte Alto, between the river Oglio and the hills of the vineyards, mentioned for the first time in a document of 879; the historical center of medieval appearance is dominated by the Castle, which became a convent in 1692, and preserves the parish church of San Giorgio with works of Romanino and Callisto Piazza; on the estate Ricci Curbastro is home to the Agricultural Museum and wine.
A ring between water and woods.
Pickles, pastures and paragliding take off above Feltre.

Wanted by the parish priest Don Antonio Cavatorta, it was built between 1899 and 1904 on a project by Giuseppe Gallo from Turin, in modern Baroque style with Corinthian capitals, and inaugurated on 1 October 1904 in the presence of Cardinal Richelmy; the bell tower is 1924. Four side altars dedicated to the Souls of Purgatory, to the Immaculate Heart of Mary, to the Madonna del Rosario and to the Sacred Heart; next to the canonical house of 1825.
The sand desert on the sea.
A stop between sea and inland.
Walk in the village with works of art exposed to the open air, to Australia Square and Villa Vidua.
A church of the sixteenth century devoted to Our Lady.

Baroque church with elliptical dome covered with majolica hembrics; it houses the sacred art section of the Ceramic Museum, with a calendar of reliquary cesellato that houses relics of various saints and a fragment of the Cross.
The peaks of Val Trebbia.
Octagonal Baptistery next to the Duomo, with the Baptism of Christ and the apostles in the dome.
The Renaissance Church of the Knights.
Venus Anadiomene.
In the hamlet of Pieve di Sinalunga one of the oldest churches in the area, with a Romanesque basilica on much older foundations.

On 2-3 May 1815 in the territory of Pollenza, then Monte Milone, the battle of Cantagallo was fought, one of the bloodiest of the Napoleonic period, considered by many scholars the symbolic beginning of the Risorgimento. The church of Santa Maria Ausiliatrice di Cantagallo, commissioned by Don Nazareno Boldorini, is a temple-hospital in honour of the fallen.
The statues and epigraphs of the Roman Suasa.
The peasant architecture born under Vesuvius.
Inaugurated in 2004, it is a 60-hectare park with over 50,000 plants from the Mediterranean scrub, the wildlife recovery centre and the military historical museum.
From the hills to the mouth.
The first church built in the territory of Bellagio, enlarged and restored in 1785.
Listing in extension: the guide covers for now 8 of the 13 places of culture recorded by the Ministry of Culture in this municipality, as well as churches, squares and nature.
The history of caving before or after the cave.

Objects of everyday life, work and religiosity popular between the late nineteenth and mid twentieth centuries: tools of peasants, spinners, carpenters and blacksmiths, and photographic plates of the historic center. Open Monday and Sunday.

Oil Town in Puglia Imperiale, surrounded by the Alta Murgia National Park, less than 15 km from Andria and about 40 km from Bari. The medieval center has a ray system around Largo Cesare Battisti, with the Matrix Church of Santa Maria Maggiore, palaces like De Mattis and a nineteenth-century theater; in the territory the necropolis to mound of San Magno and the Dolmen of the Paladini.

In the municipal territory, on the promontory of Capo Bianco overlooking the sea, there are the ruins of the Greek city of Eraclea Minoa with the theater of the fourth century BC and the Antiquarium, inside the natural reserve Foce of the river Platani, with the amphitheatre beach under the white cliff.

Borgo on the eastern shore of Lake Como, crossed by the stream Pioverna that dug there the Orrido, which can be crossed on walkways; in the old town the late Dolomian church of Santi Nazaro and Celso and the fourteenth-century church of Santa Marta, while above the village pass the Path of the Wanderer and, in Val Muggiasca, the churches of Vendrogno and Mount Muggio.
The symbolic flavor of the Lepini.
Two Romanesque churches on top of each other.
The great monastery of the Branciforte.
The first half of the nineteenth century complex on the right bank of the Panaro, in the area called  the "Riviera" where stands a series of ancient villas once accessible by river.

On the top of the hill, the fortress was rebuilt in 1239 by Frederick II of Swabia on the remains of a Byzantine castle conquered by the Longobards in 602, demolishing the ancient parish church of Santa Giustina; Monselice became the seat of the imperial court of appeal for the Trevigiana Brand. The pyramid trunk base is covered with blocks of trachyte and supports a quadrangular tower, today uncovered; you can visit the excavations with the crenellated walls and the apse of the parish church, and in the Mastio are exhibited ceramics, tools and silvers with a plastic of the fortification. The last siege was that of the League of Cambrai in 1509.

In the region of San Pietro, perhaps rest of a Romanesque bell tower; at the base are faded frescoes with the coat of arms of the De Contesa next to San Sebastiano, dated 1448 and attributed by the scholar Aldo Moretto to Domenico della Marca d'Ancona.
The memories of the Avogadro and a nineteenth century organ.

Built in the 12th century on a Basilian church of the 8th century, with neoclassical façade of 1848 and a 16th century baptismal font. It preserves the Madonna del Cardellino, carved in 1517 by Stefano da Putignano, which the Touring defines the most valuable art treasure of the village.
The best view of Aeolian and lakes.
Romanesque along the Seven Bridges.
closed all month of August; openings by reservation (Abbazia Foundation)
Church founded in 1218 and rebuilt after the earthquake of 1741, with the convent on three sides: it preserves three polyptychs of the Crivelli brothers and works of Jerome of Giovanni da Camerino.

Part of the Augustinian convent complex, documented by the end of the 13th century and today in the 16th century reconstruction with 18th century renovations: unique hall in red brick with barrel vault and twelve altars carved, carved and golden. It is a real art gallery, with paintings by Claudio Ridolfi, Guerrieri, Presutti, Tiarini and the workshop of Barocci, a polychrome fifteenth-century sandstone Pietà, a bar of the 16th-century Magistrate and a 17th-century cloister next door.
The mountain of the house.

Outside the town of Ponna Inferiore, it has Romanesque origins (XI century hypothesised), was enlarged in the fifteenth century and preserves a fresco of Ambrogio da Valsolda of 1504. Faces and walls are frescoed with squares of the Barelli, stories of St. Gallen and St. Desire and paintings of Felice Trivella; altarpieces of Christopher and Carpoforo Tencalla (1745) and high altar at temple of Pietro Giacomo Barelli (1756). The access road is marked by the fourteen chapels of the Via Crucis designed by Gallo Barelli and decorated by Carlo Scotti in 1771; on the south side there is an atrium with a trompe-l'oeil painted façade.
The walls of Francesco di Giorgio and the panorama.
A market that has lasted for over six centuries.

In the park of the ancient villa of the Counts Salazar, destroyed during the war, two redwoods of about one hundred years recorded among the monumental trees Italian dominate firs and cedars: the highest measures about 50 meters, the other has a circumference at the base of 10,5 meters. In the park there is also a large araucaria and two rare specimens of Thujopsis dolabrata; in the area stands Casa Auxilium, of the Salesian religious.
Over two hundred contemporary works of art donated by artists.
Ancient tower and pier on the sea.
The most original bell tower on the lake.

Fortility of the 13th century, castle and manor residence that barred the road to the enemies of the Republic of Genoa, for centuries of the Fieschi. The best preserved part is the tower; behind stood the real castle, leaning on a rocky spur that preserves traces of the internal layout. The site is especially valid for the remarkable landscape value.

Maccarruna of the house and taggiarini with castrated sauce, pasta ca fasola, chops of castrated, sasizzunedda wrapped in the laurel and cooked with fire, fresh tuma with sugar or anchovies; between the sweet vuccunetta and seraphids with honey and almonds.

Rebuilt in 1868, with classical façade and three naves inside: it houses the Assunta altarpiece by Carlo Rizzi, a Santa Filomena by Adeodato Malatesta and a San Luigi Gonzaga by Luigi Asioli. Next to it, the oratory of San Luigi and the Oratory of the Whites.

Itinerary from the Pieve di Sofignano to San Leonardo between medieval villages and pastoral places: the Buca del Tasso, a horizontal cave over 65 meters long, the Passo del Mandrione (841 m) towards Mugello, the hawthorn called Spina Vagliucci, 8 meters high and about 400 years old, the travertine of the Sasso Spugnoso on the river Nosa, Savignano with the church of Saints Andrea and Donato and Parmigno with the chapel of Santo Stefano frescoed in the fifteenth century.
Dedicated to the Blessed Virgin of the Graces and St. Peter, it was built by the pampers in the first half of the seventeenth century to ask for protection from the plague.
Ancient cornerstone of the Republic of Siena in Valdichiana, closed by walls with four doors; the Orange Flag is for the walled hamlet of Montefollonico.
The baroque cathedral of the city.
The places linked to Eugenio Montale, from Punta Mesco to the "Casa del Doganiere" (Casa del Doganiere) with the Cinque Terre Card free excursions from April to August.

Visitor center and modern information with interactive exhibition on the Dolomite front of the First World War and on the first historical ascents, and panoramic terrace with free entrance. From 26 May to 27 September 2026 open Monday-Friday 8.30-17, Saturday 8.30-14.30, Sunday 10-12 (5 July-6 September).

It collects the findings of the excavation campaigns financed by the municipality. The oldest materials date back to Aurignatian (about 34,000-27,000 years ago) and include engraved pebbles and bone fragments; they follow protohistoric, archaic and Roman-age objects, including materials related to the Aurunci.
The house where the Armistice of 1859, with the relics of the Risorgimento, was signed.
Ancient high-altitude refuge reassembled in the village as a museum of the history of mountaineering.
The sanctuary dates back to about 1200; devastated by the Saracens between 1542 and 1550, it was ruled by the Carmelites from 1569 to 1624.
The wooden furniture of the fraternity.

Villa of the eighteenth century with a U-shaped plan with palladian pronaos, enlarged by Federico Mazzucchelli and his son Gianmaria until 1753: the museum house preserves period furnishings and frescoes by Francesco Savani.
A delightful villa with a scenic garden on the Valcuvia.

Country of water on the eastern slopes of the Euganean Hills, grown along the navigable canal and once among the major Italian river ports: the Museum of Fluvial Navigation, the Conca di navigazione, the Castle of the Catajo and Villa Selvatico with the thermal park.

Seaside resort of the Tyrrhenian coast of Messinese, with the promontory of the sanctuary of Maria Santissima and the ruins of the castle overlooking the Aeolian, the Roman baths of Bagnoli, the seaside village of San Gregorio and Villa Piccolo, house museum of the Barons Small cousins of Tomasi di Lampedusa.
The tour of the covered walls, with a view to the sea.
One of the most beautiful castles in Italy, set of Ladyhawke.

Opened in July 2010 in a 19th century rustic villa inside the park: on the ground floor architectural elements and finds of the agora and theater, with statues of satyrs and menads, on the first floor the reconstruction of the peristyle of the House; among the pieces a cup attic to red figures of about 500 BC. Sections also on medieval and numismatic cities.
The city on the cliff of the Costa degli Dei, with the sanctuary of Santa Maria dell'Isola on the rock, the Norman Cathedral, the palaces of Via Boiano and the white sandy beaches.

In Masseria there is the mineral enrichment plant of about 150 years ago, the unique monument of the industrial revolution.Its main features include large crushing machines, flotation tanks, inclined braking planes and horse-drawn sections of the huge rail transport 27 km from Monteneve to the station of Vipiteno, born after the opening of the Brennero railway (1867). The mine remained active until May 1985; the Poschhaus tunnel runs for 6 km in the mountain towards the Val Passiria.

Protected area of 47 hectares on the lake, between reeds and water lilies, ideal for birdwatching: tarabusini, diving ducks, divers, cormorants, folagues, herons and birds of prey like the royal dawn. Overelevated passerelle on the water lead to observation huts; the tour centre hosts the Museum of Pallustrated Ecology and offers guided tours, boat trips, canoeing, kayak or rowing boat, workshops and summer camps.
The life of Padre Pio in ten scenes.

Just over two kilometers from Arzachena, it is the only nuragic religious building that has so far been investigated in the territory: a megaron temple of the Middle Bronze (XVI-XIV century BC), more ancient than the other temples of this type in Sardinia. Dress and room of about 8 meters with seats, counter for the offers, two niches and fireplace ritual in the center; around a collapsed nuraghe, a circular hut and burials in the tafoni. Open every day 9-19.
The river and its bridges.

Granite outcrop of the upper Paleozoic modelled by the wind in the shape of a bear facing La Maddalena, on a rise of more than 120 meters; already Ptolemy indicated it as  "Areti Promontorium" and in 1993 the Region declared it a natural monument. Go up with a panoramic path of about half a kilometer (about ten minutes) from the fort of Capo d'Orso, with many steps; from the top the view embraces the archipelago and Corsica. Access for a fee, also with a cumulative ticket with Fortress and Ethnographic Museum (€7).
Woods and streams between Reventino and Sila.

Rebuilt in the middle of the fourteenth century by Aimone di Challant and completed at the beginning of the fifteenth century by his son Bonifacio I, who decorated the courtyard and interior with frescoes of the international Gothic, including San Giorgio who kills the dragon; Alpine furnishings collected in 1935-36. Visit accompanied.
The grave of the last Duke of Urbino.
The 18th-century residence of the Biandrates with its English garden.
The Via Crucis in marble by Antonio Bonazza.
A country where the rock has become an art gallery.
The roots of families.
The tomb of the Garibaldi of the battle of 1860.
The town hall.

Small agropastoral village about 600 meters on the edge of the Jar that gives it its name, between Sarcidano and Trexenta: on the plateau stands the nuragic sanctuary of Santa Vittoria, one of the major of Sardinia, and in the village the Romanesque parish church of San Basilio Magno.
Odigitria and the sacred furnishings of the village.

Founded in 970 on a pagan temple, rebuilt in the 12th century and renovated in the 18th century mainly by Neapolitan artists; ceiling of 1878. The 12-column crypt contains 14th-century frescoes and remains of mosaic flooring.
Built around 1450, with bell tower and wrought iron gate, it closes the visit of the village.
The 14th century frescoes of Nuzi.
On the tomb of the father of verism.
It keeps part of the herbarium of the abbot Famine.

In an old renovated restaurant in the historic centre, it illustrates the phases of the processing of olives, from milling to pressing and oil harvesting. It probably dates back to the XVII-XVIII century, it was active until a few years ago (propriety of Carlo Bartoletti) and from the origins it was called "Il Montano" (The Montano), described as the largest and oldest oil mill in the area, preserves the mill, the oak beam with counterweight in stone and an old block of notes.
The Tamerici complex and the thermal parks surrounding the establishments, including the Redi.
Pure Romanesque and fourteenth century frescoes.

Città degli Ernici closed by polygonal walls of about 2 km with five doors; on the Civita, the Cyclopic acropolis with the Cathedral of São Paulo, while in the medieval center there are Santa Maria Maggiore, Palazzo Gottifredo with the Civic Museum and the fresco of Christ in the Labyrinth.
The convent houses the church of St. Andrew the Apostle, rich in works of art of the seventeenth century.
A pyramid in Rome.

One of the most important historical buildings in the country, it was the seat of the court of the Counts of Gorizia in Pusteria; the north façade is painted with the coats of arms of Gorizia, Tyrol and several noble families.

Built by the Colonnas and renovated several times, it guards the country from the north: military fortress, transformed into a noble residence by Pope Martin V in 1417 and then papal residence in the sixteenth century; between 1611 and 1639 Philip I Colonna renewed the north-eastern tower, with a chapel frescoed in 1616 by Marzio Ganasini.
the MiC card reports the museum closed every day; check on tel. 0131 225810
Late-Gothic construction built between 1582 and 1610.
The most famous pistachio in Italy, in its land.

Section of the Civic Museum inaugurated in December 2012 in the underground rooms of the Palazzo Comunale, former convent of the Augustinians: nine plaster statues over 4 meters tall representing the Epiphany, carved by Ferri in 1947-48 after winning a competition of the Pallottini Fathers for Sant'Andrea della Valle in Rome. Visitable all year round.
An easy walk in the woods of the Campo dei Fiori, with erratic rock.
The abbots court.

The summit is 2,260 m with a 360° free view: Sass de Putia, Odle, Sciliar, Catinaccio, Latemar, Corno Nero and Corno Bianco, with the UNESCO Dolomites arch from southeast to south. Cableway (Via Tann 21, Collalbo, bus 166) open in summer and autumn (2026: from 14 May to 8 November) and in winter for the ski area; with the RittenCard a free climb a day.

Built by the Normans in the 12th century to control one of the southern entrances of the Peligna Valley, it was severely damaged by the earthquake of 1706: the ruins of the fourteenth-century tower, the residential complex and an arch of the early sixteenth century remain. In 1904 Gabriele d'Annunzio set the tragedy under the bush.
The Byzantine fortress shaped like a ship on the Strait.
One of the five villages of the UNESCO site; via Colombo rises to the upper part of the country.
The villa on the slopes of Monte Morello, with the Italian garden with three terraces, the courtyard frescoed by Volterrano and the 14 lunettes of Giusto Utens.
Some links are affiliated: if you buy a ticket the guide receives a small commission, without cost for you.

Among the most beautiful Romanesque churches in Italy, built between the 10th and 12th centuries: rosette of the Wheel of Fortune of Brioloto, reliefs of Niccolò (1138), bronze door with 48 tiles, the "San Zeno che ride" and the altarpiece of Andrea Mantegna on the high altar.

Hunting and party residence designed by Filippo Juvarra since 1729 for Vittorio Amedeo II, crowned by the deer on the dome; since 1919 it houses the Museum of Art and Furniture, today of the Foundation Ordine Mauriziano. UNESCO World Heritage.

Consecrated in 549 by Archbishop Maximiano, in Classe: the green apse with Saint Apollinare among the lambs is one of the sereneest visions of the Ravenna mosaics.
National public bodies: Ministry of Culture, Italy.it, UNESCO, ISTAT.
In the villa the great groups of Bernini, the Rat of Proserpina, Apollo and Dafne and David, the Paolina Bonaparte of Canova and Caravaggio's works.
